papers.title: A species comparison of videofloroscopic metrics of swallowing in healthy dogs and cats.
papers.authors: Grobman M, Luciani E, Reinero C
papers.abstract: Videofluoroscopic swallow studies (VFSS) are the criterion standard for diagnosing dysphagia in veterinary species. However, a lack of normative swallowing variables in cats hinders assessment of cats with potential aerodigestive disease. Species variation in swallowing could lead to over- and under-interpretation of findings on VFSS, resulting in misdiagnosis. Compare differences in objective swallowing metrics between cats and dogs using VFSS. We hypothesize that cats will show differences in objective swallowing metrics on VFSS compared with dogs. Healthy adult cats (n = 13) and dogs (n = 12) without clinical signs (CS) of respiratory or alimentary disease. Prospective, cross-sectional study. Cats and dogs underwent standardized VFSS. All were evaluated according to 16 objective metrics and compared between species. Between group comparisons were made using Mann-Whitney-U, T-test, or Fischer's exact test with a P < .05 significance level for all comparisons. Cats had significantly longer inter-swallow intervals, shorter pharyngeal transit times, and more pharyngeal swallows to generate primary peristalsis compared with dogs (P < .05). Cats were also more likely to have esophageal volume accumulation and slowing of distal esophageal transit time compared with dogs (P < .05). Physiologic reflux was identified in 2 (15.4%) cats vs 6 (50%) dogs. Pathologic penetration-aspiration (P-A score: 7; aspiration without attempt to cough) was found in 1 cat despite a lack of respiratory or alimentary CS. Species variation should be considered when interpreting VFSS. In 1 cat, occult tracheal aspiration of contrast (P-A score 7) was detected without accompanying cough.

papers.title: Multimodal imaging characteristics and case management of intraspinal Spirocerca lupi infection in a dog.
papers.authors: Carrillo AJ, Grosso FRV, Walden HDS, Alas O, Garcia GA
papers.abstract: A 1-year-old female spayed mixed breed dog was ambulatory with paraparesis and proprioceptive ataxia, absent conscious proprioception in pelvic limbs, and spinal pain with a T3-L3 neurolocalization on presentation. Thoracic radiographs revealed caudal mediastinal mass, pneumothorax, and pleural effusion. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple mediastinal masses with vertebral canal extension, extradural compression at T5-T6, intramedullary T2 hyperintensities at T5 and T9, esophageal compression and dilation, and aortic aneurysmal dilation. Transdiaphragmatic ultrasonography was suggestive of parasitic involvement. A right T5-T8 hemilaminectomy and parasitology confirmed Spirocerca lupi. Treatment with ivermectin (400 mcg/kg SC q24h for 3 days followed by once a week for 6 weeks), prednisone (0.7 mg/kg/day), and clindamycin (10.7 mg/kg PO q12h) was initiated. Recovery of independent ambulation occurred 2 months after treatment. Computed tomography revealed resolution of mediastinal and esophageal nodules with progressive aortic aneurysmal dilation. Multimodal imaging was essential for the management of spinal spirocercosis.

papers.title: Clinical and serologic variables associated with dissemination and seasonal presentation in dogs with newly diagnosed coccidioidomycosis.
papers.authors: Chittick L, Jaffey JA, Hanzlicek AS, Kreisler R, Rayhel LH, Balaban J, Alcott C, Adams C, Gould AG
papers.abstract: Disseminated coccidioidomycosis in dogs is associated with substantial morbidity, yet distinguishing pulmonary from disseminated disease can be clinically challenging. Antibody serology might assist in predicting dissemination, but its performance across disease sites requires clarification. To identify clinical and serologic variables associated with disseminated coccidioidomycosis and to evaluate differences in antibody magnitude among common sites of infection. Two hundred fourteen client-owned dogs with newly diagnosed coccidioidomycosis. Retrospective study. Anti-Coccidioides spp. immunoglobulin (Ig)G was measured by enzyme immunoassay (EIA) and agar gel immunodiffusion (AGID) at a reference laboratory. Disease was classified as pulmonary in 148/214 (69%) and disseminated in 66/214 (31%). Higher EIA IgG concentration and AGID IgG titer were independently associated with dissemination. Enzyme immunoassay discriminated disseminated from pulmonary disease well (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74-0.87), estimate likely representing an upper bound because serology contributed to case classification. Agar gel immunodiffusion performance was not statistically distinguishable (AUC: 0.74; 95% CI, 0.67-0.82; P = .65). Exploratory cutpoints included an EIA IgG threshold of 37 enzyme immunoassay units (sensitivity 86%, specificity 63%) and an AGID IgG threshold of ≥1:32 (sensitivity 48%, specificity 86%). Pulmonary diagnoses were least common in spring and peaked in late fall and winter. Coccidioidal IgG serology might provide clinically useful adjunctive information when assessing dogs for disseminated coccidioidomycosis. However, overlap in serologic results between disease phenotypes precludes the use of serology alone to determine disease extent. Serologic results should therefore be interpreted alongside clinical findings and appropriate diagnostic evaluation.

papers.title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.
papers.authors: Stylianou G, Vassallo F, Nishii N, Diana A, Tardo AM, Del Baldo F, Fracassi F
papers.abstract: No simple, blood-based biomarker to estimate tumor size in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism (PDH) has been evaluated. Determine whether the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)/cortisol ratio differentiates pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with PDH and correlates with pituitary size. Seventy privately-owned dogs with PDH (microadenomas, n = 30; macroadenomas, n = 40). Retrospective multicenter observational study. Endogenous ACTH and cortisol concentrations obtained at the same time point before treatment were used to calculate the ACTH/cortisol ratio. Pituitary tumor size was classified using the pituitary-to-brain (P/B) ratio. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Dogs with macroadenomas had significantly higher ACTH/cortisol ratios than dogs with microadenomas (median, 9.12; IQR, 6.46-14.28 vs median, 4.90; IQR, 3.08-8.10; P < .001). The ratio showed moderate discrimination for differentiating macroadenomas from microadenomas with an area under the curve of 0.77 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89; P < .001). A cutoff >5.69 yielded 85% sensitivity and 60% specificity (positive likelihood ratio 2.13), whereas a higher ratio >11.74 achieved 90% specificity and 35% sensitivity (positive likelihood ratio 3.50). The ACTH/cortisol ratio showed moderate positive correlation with pituitary size (Spearman's ρ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.26-0.64; P < .001) and remained independently associated with macroadenoma classification in multivariable analysis (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40). The ACTH/cortisol ratio is associated with pituitary tumor size in dogs with PDH and may support clinical risk stratification, particularly when advanced imaging is unavailable.

papers.title: Serum fibroblast growth factor-23 concentration in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease.
papers.authors: Iwasa N, Shimizu M, Okamoto T, Kosuga H, Morikita N, Kawabe M, Iwata M, Watanabe K, Kobatake Y, Takashima S, Nishii N
papers.abstract: Circulating fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF-23) is primarily a kidney-related biomarker, but also may be influenced by cardiovascular remodeling and hemodynamic load. Verify whether serum FGF-23 concentration increases with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) severity. Forty-two client-owned dogs with MMVD without overt kidney disease. Retrospective cross-sectional study to evaluate serum FGF-23, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine (Cr), and symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) concentrations. Imaging variables included vertebral heart score (VHS), vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), left atrial-to-aortic root ratio (LA/Ao), normalized left-ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN), and diastolic transmitral E-wave velocity (E-vel). Differences among American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine stages were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Correlations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with serum FGF-23 concentration. Dogs with ACVIM stages C and D had higher serum FGF-23 concentrations than those with stages B1 and B2 (P < .05). Serum FGF-23 concentrations were positively correlated with VLAS (rs = 0.500, P < .01), ANP (rs = 0.455, P < .01), LA/Ao (rs = 0.384, P < .05), E-vel (rs = 0.372, P < .05), and NT-proBNP (rs = 0.366, P < .05). ACVIM stage was significantly associated with serum FGF-23 concentration after adjustment for serum Cr concentration and loop diuretic use. The potential influence of MMVD should be considered when interpreting increased circulating FGF-23 concentrations in dogs with MMVD.

papers.title: Letter regarding "Pancreatic lymphangioma and concurrent intestinal lymphangiectasia in a dog:" long-term follow-up and necropsy findings.
papers.authors: Hifumi T, Ishikawa T, Kozuma C, Kozuma M, Kuramoto T, Takahashi M, Miura N, Miyoshi N

papers.title: Case Report: Presumptive subdural hemorrhage as a rare neurological manifestation of primary immune-mediated thrombocytopenia in a dog.
papers.authors: Hong HP, Kei TG, Gagnon NA, Scrivani PV
papers.abstract: A 10-year-old female spayed mixed-breed dog was presented with a history of seizures and acute progressive intracranial signs. The neurological examination was consistent with multifocal brain disease. Clinical examination revealed ecchymoses, petechiae, and bilateral retinal hemorrhage. Clinicopathological evaluation identified severe thrombocytopenia [a platelet count of 9 × 10 3 /μL without clumps on manual smear evaluation] with an increased mean platelet volume. Coagulation testing (activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time) and fibrinolysis markers (D-dimers, quantitative fibrinogen), infectious disease screening, and thoracic and abdominal imaging were within normal limits, establishing a diagnosis of primary immune-mediated thrombocytopenia (ITP). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain showed minimally expanded, bilateral crescent-shaped, extra-axial fluid accumulations overlying both cerebral hemispheres. Based on T1-weighted and T2-weighted hyperintensities and peripheral susceptibility artifact on T2*-weighted gradient-recalled echo (GRE) imaging, a late subacute subdural intracranial hemorrhage was diagnosed. Despite initial uneventful anesthesia and recovery, the dog experienced acute neurological deterioration and suffered cardiopulmonary arrest, suspected due to ongoing hemorrhage or brain herniation. This report describes a rare neurological manifestation of primary ITP in a dog. While canine ITP generally carries a favorable prognosis, life-threatening secondary intracranial hemorrhage can occur. Primary ITP should be considered as a differential diagnosis for an acute, progressive neurological presentation until a normal platelet count is confirmed.

papers.title: Effects of transient intravascular volume overload on endothelial glycocalyx thickness in healthy anesthetized cats.
papers.authors: Yozova ID, Thomson N, Irie M, Owen R, Munday JS
papers.abstract: Previous studies suggest that the endothelial glycocalyx is damaged by volume overload. This study assessed the effects of transient intravascular volume overload on estimated endothelial glycocalyx thickness in healthy cats, using sidestream dark field videomicroscopy and the Glycocheck™ software. This was a prospective blinded cross-over single-center experimental study on twenty healthy cats. Cats were randomized to either receive 30 mL/kg/10 min of Hartman's solution (volume overload group) or no fluids (control) with a washout of 7 days. Sublingual mucosa videomicroscopy images were acquired at T0 (baseline), T1 (immediately after intervention), T2 (3 h after end of intervention) and T3 (24 h after end of intervention) with three measurements performed per timepoint under propofol anesthesia. The perfused boundary region (PBR), an inverse estimate for endothelial glycocalyx thickness, for vessels with diameter of 5-25, 5-9, 10-19 and 20-25 μm, respectively, was then automatically calculated with the Glycocheck™ software. Packed cell volume (PCV) was measured at each timepoint. Data normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test and visual inspection. Linear mixed-effects regression modelling, with cat as a random effect, analyzed interactions between GlycoCheck™ and other parameters. PBR 5-25 μm, 5-9 μm and 10-19 μm increased over time, reaching significance at T2 ( p = 0.001 , p = 0.017 and p = 0.008 , respectively). A significant group x timepoint interaction was identified for PBR 5-9 with decreased values at T2 ( p = 0.028 ) and T3 ( p = 0.010 ) in the volume overload group. Decreases in PCV were significantly associated with increases in PBR 5-25 μm ( p = 0.003 ) and PBR 10-19 μm ( p = 0.001 ). This study did not demonstrate decreases in estimated endothelial glycocalyx thickness after transient volume overload in healthy cats. The PBR did increase over time, suggesting potential anesthetic effects. Changes in PCV affected GlycoCheck™ parameters and this finding should be further explored. Further studies designed with understanding of feline volume kinetics are required to investigate the effects of IV fluids on the feline endothelial glycocalyx.

papers.title: Rapid test performance for the diagnosis of canine visceral leishmaniasis using blood, serum, and saliva.
papers.authors: Lamattina D, Sánchez-Fernández C, Depasquino AF, Laiño MA, Siccardi FM, Salomón OD
papers.abstract: A key aspect of controlling canine visceral leishmaniasis (CVL) is the availability of accurate diagnostic tools capable of reaching most of the population. In endemic areas with socially vulnerable populations, facilitating rapid CVL diagnosis by reducing sampling difficulties and diagnostic costs could provide substantial benefits. This study evaluated the performance of the Kalazar Detect™ Canine Rapid Test for CVL diagnosis using blood, serum, and saliva samples, and compared the results among sample types and with PCR detection in lymph nodes. Samples were collected from 100 dogs. Prevalence detected by the rapid diagnostic tests (RDT) was 21% using blood and serum and 17% using saliva, whereas PCR detected a prevalence of 46%. Agreement between serum and blood-based RDTs was 100%, while comparison between serum/blood and saliva showed a kappa index of 0.87, indicating almost perfect agreement. Using PCR as the reference standard, RDTs on serum and blood showed a sensitivity of 0.39 and specificity of 0.94, whereas saliva-based RDT showed a sensitivity of 0.33 and specificity of 0.96. The low sensitivity of the RDTs currently used by the National Leishmaniasis Program indicate that an additional diagnostic method should be incorporated into CVL surveillance in endemic areas. Nevertheless, our results suggest that saliva may be a suitable sample for the Kalazar Detect Canine Rapid Test, as it is easy to collect, less expensive, and less invasive. To our knowledge, this is the first study to evaluate the performance of this RDT for CVL diagnosis using saliva samples.

papers.title: Effects of a gluten-free hydrolyzed diet in dogs with paroxysmal dyskinesia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Okonji S, Del Baldo F, Garuti E, Vecchiato CG, Di Carlo A, Costantini G, Cauduro A, Di Paola A, Falzone C, Gallucci A, Tartari I, Baroni M, Poli F, Bianchi E, Buffagni V, Valentini A, Gagliardo T, Gandini G
papers.abstract: Paroxysmal dyskinesia (PD) is an episodic movement disorder in dogs. Gluten-sensitive etiology has been suggested, but prospective studies in different breeds are lacking. Investigate whether a gluten-free hydrolyzed diet (GFHD) decreases PD episode frequency and gastrointestinal (GI) signs, and evaluate associations with serum anti-gliadin peptide immunoglobulin G (AGA IgG) and anti-transglutaminase-2 immunoglobulin A (TG-2 IgA) titers. Twenty-three client-owned dogs with PD. Prospective cohort study with 3 time points: baseline (T0), 90 days (T1), and 180 days (T2). Dogs were fed a GFHD. Episode frequency, GI signs and AGA IgG and TG-2 IgA titers were assessed at each time point. Response to GFHD was classified as excellent (episode disappearance), good (≥50% decrease), fairly good (<50% decrease), or poor (no change or increase). Median number of episodes decreased from 6 (range, 2-60) at T0 to 2 (range, 0-10) at T2 (P = .0003). At T2, 17/23 dogs were responders (5 excellent, 12 good). Gastrointestinal signs were present in 15/23 dogs at T0 and in 6/23 dogs at T2, with significant decreases in vomiting and diarrhea (P = .01). No significant correlation was found between episode frequency and AGA IgG or TG-2 IgA titers at any time point (P > .1). Antibody results did not significantly change between T0 and T2. The GFHD was associated with a significant decrease in PD frequency and GI signs in most dogs. The AGA IgG and TG-2 IgA titers were not predictive of dietary response, suggesting limited value as biomarkers.

papers.title: Outcomes of a 42-day course of molnupiravir in cats with feline infectious peritonitis: a prospective descriptive study.
papers.authors: Hishinuma K, Inoue A, Fukushima K, Sato M
papers.abstract: Antiviral therapy for cats with feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) has traditionally been administered for 84 days, although the optimal duration of molnupiravir treatment remains unknown. To evaluate the efficacy of a 42-day course of molnupiravir, orally (PO), for naturally occurring FIP in cats. Nineteen client-owned cats with newly diagnosed FIP. Prospective pilot study. Cats received molnupiravir, PO, q12h for 42 days at a median dosage of 11.5 mg/kg (IQR, 10.2-12.5 mg/kg). Cats with ocular or neurological involvement were excluded. Clinical assessments were performed during treatment and for 6 months after treatment cessation. Nineteen cats were enrolled. Two cats failed to complete treatment because of death or persistent clinical signs. Fourteen of 19 cats (74%; 95% CI, 49-91) achieved sustained remission on an intention-to-treat basis. Each non-completer failed on day 5 or 10, respectively, within a window common to 42- and 84-day protocols, and therefore do not inform the question of treatment duration; among the 17 cats reaching day 42, 14 (82%; 95% CI, 57-96) remained in remission for at least 6 months. Three cats relapsed after treatment cessation; all responded to retreatment with molnupiravir at the same dosage extended to 84 days. This prospective study suggests that a shortened course of molnupiravir is feasible in selected cats with non-ocular, non-neurological FIP. : (FIP) にするウイルスは 84 されてきたが、モルヌピラビルのなはらかではない。 : FIP のにするモルヌピラビル 42 のをすること。 : たに FIP とされた19。 : きパイロット。モルヌピラビルを 12 ごとに 42 した。のは 11.5  mg/kg (、 10.2-12.5  mg/kg) であった。またはをするはした。および 6 か、をった。 : 19 をした。 2 はまたはのによりをできなかった。 Intention-to-treat では 19 14 (74 %； 95% 、 49-91) がをした。の 2 はそれぞれ5および10にとなり、いずれも 42 および 84 のプロトコルにするであったため、のにはしなかった。 42 までをした 17 のうち 14 (82% ； 95% 、 57-96) はなくとも 6 かをした。 3 はにしたが、がのモルヌピラビルによる 84 のにした。 および: きパイロットのから、およびをわない FIP のでは、モルヌピラビルのがであるがされた。. Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) is a serious disease in cats caused by feline coronavirus. Antiviral treatment is commonly given for 84 days, but the best treatment duration for molnupiravir is unknown. In this prospective pilot study, 19 cats without eye or neurological involvement received molnupiravir by mouth for 42 days. Seventeen cats completed the 42-day course. Fourteen of the 19 enrolled cats remained in remission for at least 6 months after treatment. Three cats relapsed after completing treatment. All 3 responded when molnupiravir was restarted at the same dose and continued for approximately 84 days. Two cats did not complete the initial treatment course because of death or persistent clinical signs early in treatment. These findings suggest that a 42-day course of molnupiravir can be feasible for selected cats with FIP, although this study was small and did not directly compare 42-day and 84-day treatment courses.

papers.title: Antimicrobial resistance and molecular characterization of extended-spectrum β-lactamase/AmpC β-lactamase-producing Proteus mirabilis isolates from companion dogs in South Korea (2018-2024).
papers.authors: Hwang YJ, Lee YH, Ali MS, Choi JH, Park SC, Moon BY, Lim SK
papers.abstract: To investigate antimicrobial resistance profiles and molecular characteristics of third-generation cephalosporin- and cephamycin-resistant Proteus mirabilis isolated from clinically ill dogs across South Korea from 2018 through 2024. Antimicrobial susceptibility of isolates was assessed by broth microdilution. Molecular characteristics were determined by polymerase chain reaction and multilocus sequence typing. In total, 667 P mirabilis were isolated from skin/ear, feces, and urine/reproductive systems of companion dogs. Among them, 27.3% of isolates exhibited a multidrug-resistant (MDR) phenotype. Molecular characterization of 38 extended-spectrum β-lactamase (5.7%)/AmpC β-lactamase-carrying strains revealed a high prevalence of β-lactamase cephamycinase-2 gene blaCMY-2 (65.8%) and β-lactamase cefotaximase gene blaCTX-M variants, including blaCTX-M-65, blaCTX-M-15, and blaCTX-M-90. Multilocus sequence typing identified 16 distinct sequence types (STs), with ST135 (39.5%) and ST212 (21.1%) emerging as the most prevalent lineages. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that the first major cluster contains 31 isolates (81.6%) across 10 STs centered around ST135, whereas the second cluster comprises 7 isolates (18.4%) across 6 STs centered on ST292. Notably, the ST135-centered cluster was associated with robust MDR phenotypes. These findings indicate that companion dogs harboring MDR P mirabilis are among several potential reservoirs within the One Health context. Especially, clone ST135 may serve as a primary evolutionary axis and a high-risk endemic clone within the Korean canine population. Our study highlights the critical role of dominant lineages in dissemination of extended-spectrum β-lactamase/AmpC β-lactamase genes and emphasizes the urgent need for continuous One Health surveillance to monitor potential transmission of these clones between companion animals and humans.

papers.title: Monocortical locking screws in the tibial diaphysis maintain tibial plateau angle and support osteotomy union after tibial plateau leveling osteotomy in dogs.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
papers.authors: Wong N, Eckart LH, Yu J, Bleakley S, Jermyn K, Michelsen J, Sul R, Iversen J, Chong WL
papers.abstract: To evaluate the effect of distal monocortical locking screw fixation on construct stability and bone healing following tibial plateau leveling osteotomy (TPLO) in dogs. We hypothesized that monocortical fixation would result in acceptable maintenance of tibial plateau angle (TPA) of < 5° and satisfactory osteotomy union. Medical records from a companion animal referral hospital between December 8, 2021, and February 23, 2024, were retrospectively reviewed. Dogs were included if TPLO was performed for cranial cruciate ligament insufficiency using monocortical screws in the distal tibial segment and complete radiographic follow-up was available. Change in TPA between postoperative and follow-up radiographs were recorded. Bone healing was assessed using the modified Radiographic Union Scale for Tibial Fractures. Associations between outcomes and clinical variables were evaluated with linear regression models. A total of 117 dogs met the inclusion criteria. Median change in TPA during healing was 2.15° (95% CI, 1.70° to 2.65°), and no evaluated variables were associated with TPA change. Median modified Radiographic Union Scale for Tibial Fractures score was 10 (range, 4 to 12), consistent with satisfactory radiographic union at a mean follow-up time of 43 days. The overall complication rate was 8.5%, including an infection rate of 2.6%. Use of monocortical distal tibial screws within a titanium alloy conical locking TPLO system was associated with acceptable maintenance of TPA and satisfactory radiographic union scores. Monocortical distal tibial fixation may provide sufficient stability to support osteotomy healing per manufacturer recommendations. Additional studies are needed to evaluate outcomes for different locking systems, patient size categories, screw combination, and longer-term follow-up periods.

papers.title: Changes in flea and tick infestation following topical fipronil, permethrin, piperonyl butoxide, and pyriproxyfen in naturally infested dogs: an exploratory uncontrolled field study.
papers.authors: Romero-Núñez C, Heredia-Cárdenas R, Flores-Ortega A, Bautista-Gómez LG, Gaxiola-Camacho SM, Torres-Cruz JD
papers.abstract: Flea and tick infestations impair canine welfare and may have public-health relevance in rural settings. To describe temporal changes in ectoparasite infestation and associated clinical signs after a single topical application of fipronil, permethrin, piperonyl butoxide, and pyriproxyfen (PROTECH) in naturally infested dogs. This prospective, uncontrolled exploratory field study enrolled 44 privately owned dogs in Tahdziú, Yucatán, Mexico. Dogs received one topical application at Day 0 and were reassessed on Days 15 and 30. An approximately 5-min whole-body examination documented ectoparasite presence or absence. Field-recorded numerical skin-lesion and pruritus scores and observed adverse events were summarized. Among dogs with flea-only infestation ( n = 18), positivity decreased from 18/18 at Day 0 to 0/18 at Days 15 and 30. Among tick-only dogs ( n = 11), positivity decreased from 11/11 to 0/11 and 1/11, respectively. In mixed infestations ( n = 15), positivity decreased from 15/15 to 3/15 and 2/15. Mean lesion and pruritus scores also declined in all subgroups. No adverse reactions were observed. A single application was followed by marked temporal reductions in ectoparasite positivity and clinical signs through Day 30. Because the study lacked a comparator and used non-validated clinical scores, the findings are descriptive and exploratory; they do not establish a causal treatment effect or comparative efficacy.

papers.title: Prospective multicenter study of murmur localization and stage-associated murmur grading in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac diseases: the LISTEN study.
papers.authors: Wess G, Häggström J, Stadler J, König L, Kraszewska K, Bittenecker D, Domenech O, Santamarina G, Van den Noortgate G, Bjerknaes MB, Eberhard J, Kriström K, Vatne L, Gajewski M, Schinner-Peters C, Tater G, Torti M, Schummer C, Ljungvall I
papers.abstract: Cardiac auscultation remains fundamental in dogs with suspected cardiac disease, but large prospective datasets describing clinician-recorded murmur localization and intensity across echocardiographic diagnoses are limited. This study aimed to characterize point of maximal intensity (PMI) patterns in dogs with echocardiographically diagnosed cardiac abnormalities and to evaluate the association between murmur grade and disease stage in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). This prospective international multicenter observational study included 6,996 client-owned dogs examined by 50 cardiology-trained veterinarians. Dogs underwent standardized cardiac auscultation at four predefined thoracic locations and transthoracic echocardiography during the same clinical visit. PMI localization was described across cardiac diagnoses, and murmur grade was evaluated in relation to disease stage in MMVD and DCM. Dogs with MMVD and DCM predominantly had a left apical PMI, whereas congenital outflow tract diseases and patent ductus arteriosus were predominantly associated with a left basilar PMI. Tricuspid regurgitation and ventricular septal defect were more commonly associated with right apical and right basilar PMIs, respectively. In MMVD, murmur intensity increased with advancing disease stage ( p < 0.001), and dogs with a murmur greater than soft had higher odds of being in stage B2 or C/D than B1 (OR 35.9, 95% CI 27.6-46.6). In DCM, 25.8% of dogs had no audible murmur. Although murmur grade distribution differed across DCM stages ( p = 0.03), intensity did not show a consistent stage-associated increase. Clinician-recorded four-point auscultation identified characteristic regional PMI patterns across several canine cardiac diseases. Murmur grade was strongly associated with disease stage in MMVD but provided limited stage-related information in DCM. Auscultation may support initial clinical assessment and prioritization of differential diagnoses, but echocardiography remains essential for definitive diagnosis and staging.

papers.title: Case report: long-term clinical remission of food-responsive enteropathy in a dog fed a yellow mealworm-based diet.
papers.abstract: Food-responsive enteropathy (FRE) is the most common form of canine chronic inflammatory enteropathy. Novel protein diets constitute first-line therapy, and many dogs have already been exposed to "novel" meat alternatives. Edible insects are a novel, highly digestible, and sustainable protein source. In the present study, a five-year-old male York-shire Terrier with chronic FRE and gallbladder sludge was transitioned to a diet with a 35% inclusion level of Tenebrio molitor larvae meal. Clinical indices improved from "severe" (CIBDAI = 9 and CCECAI = 11) to "clinically insignificant" (CIBDAI = 0 and CCECAI = 2) within 3 weeks and remained stable for 24 months. Body weight normalized (from 5.4 to 4.0 kg), coat quality improved, and the ultrasound examination revealed that gallbladder sludge was eliminated. A brief interruption of the insect-based diet coincided with the recurrence of sludge and gastrointestinal signs, both of which resolved after the reintroduction of T. molitor larvae meal. Hematological and serum biochemical parameters remained within the reference ranges. The mealworm-based diet led to long-term remission of FRE and elimination of gallbladder sludge without adverse effects. Insect protein is a viable hypoallergenic option for canine elimination diets and may convey additional gut and hepatobiliary benefits.

papers.title: Application of a convolutional neural network for automatic cytological diagnosis of 7 common canine tumors on whole slide images: a proof-of-concept.
papers.authors: Attini M, Newing E, Oikonomidis IL, Tsouloufi TK, Ressel L
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence may help improve speed and consistency of diagnostic veterinary cytology, but validated tools remain limited. To develop and evaluate a convolutional neural network (CNN) for automatic classification of 7 common canine tumors on cytology whole-slide images (WSIs). Ninety-one May-Grünwald Giemsa-stained canine cytology cases were selected, representing carcinoma, histiocytoma, lymphoma, mast cell tumor, melanoma, plasma cell tumor, and soft tissue sarcoma, together with a background class. Slides were tiled into 22,577 image patches (512 × 512 pixels) and manually labeled and split using a case-wise 3-fold design to avoid data leakage. An ImageNet-pretrained Inception-v3 CNN was fine-tuned for 8-class classification. Performance was assessed at tile level, Grad-CAM was used for qualitative interpretability analysis, and majority-vote prediction was further evaluated at ROI level using attention-guided inference and at WSI level using attention-free whole-slide inference. Mean test accuracy at tile level was 86.3%, with mean macro balanced accuracy of 92.0% and mean macro F1-score of 85.6%. Grad-CAM showed attention focused predominantly on cytologically relevant cellular regions. At ROI level, attention-guided inference achieved 100% Top1 accuracy (28/28 cases). At WSI level, attention-free whole-slide inference achieved 92.9% Top1 accuracy (26/28 cases), and the correct diagnosis was included within the top 3 predictions in all cases. Inception-v3 achieved high diagnostic performance on canine cytology WSIs. The results support the feasibility of both AI-assisted ROI-based decision support and fully automated whole-slide inference in veterinary cytology. These findings are proof-of-concept evidence from a curated, single-institution cohort of typical, well-differentiated cases and require validation on diagnostically challenging and external cases before clinical use.

papers.title: Phenotypic comparison of idiopathic epilepsy in English Springer Spaniels and Cocker Spaniels using a validated owner-completed questionnaire.
papers.authors: Dose JC, Matz MS, Harmas T, Hytönen M, Hakanen E, Lohi H, Parmentier T, Volk HA, Nessler JN, Bhatti SFM, De Risio L, Mandigers P, Ito D, James FMK, Jokinen TS, Ricketts S, Steffen F, Wielaender F, Eschenberg A, Fischer A, Tipold A
papers.abstract: In response to the recurring identification of medication-resistant idiopathic epilepsy (IE) in English Springer Spaniels (ESS), the objective of this retrospective questionnaire-based observational study was to delineate the phenotypic characteristics of IE in this breed in comparison to a cognate breed, the English Cocker Spaniel (ECS), employing a novel, validated, owner-completed multilingual online questionnaire. Owners of 49 ESS and ECS with seizures completed the questionnaire, of which 16 ESS and 14 ECS fulfilled the inclusion criteria and were subsequently included in the study cohort, while the remaining questionnaires were excluded due to incomplete or inconsistent information or because the criteria for IE were not fulfilled. At the time of the survey 43.3% of the dogs had died, including five that died in association with epilepsy. The median age at seizure onset was 2.5 years in ESS and ECS (range: 0,5-9 years; IQR 2.0-4.0 years). Notably a high proportion of dogs in both breeds had experienced ≥1 cluster seizure and ≥1 status epilepticus. In ECS a significantly higher rate of marked reduction in seizure severity following initiation of anti-seizure therapy compared to the ESS ( p = 0.009) was observed. Both breeds exhibit a moderate to severe disease course, with ESS showing a comparatively poorer response to antiseizure drugs. Furthermore, 43.3% of dogs with suspected IE also had affected relatives. The owner-reported occurrence of IE in related dogs may suggest a potential hereditary component in both breeds.

papers.title: Prognostic significance of EGFR-1 and VEGF-A expression in feline cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Linhares LCM, Rangel MMM, de Oliveira KD, Fonseca-Alves CE, de Moura FBC, Bispo GA, Queiroga FL, de Nardi AB
papers.abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is a prevalent malignancy in cats, and advanced cases remain challenging to manage due to their high potential for local invasion and recurrence. Epidermal growth factor receptor 1 (EGFR-1) and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) have emerged as promis- ing prognostic biomarkers in epithelial tumors, given their roles in proliferation, invasion, and angiogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate EGFR-1 and VEGF-A immunoexpression in cats with cSCC treated with electrochemotherapy (ECT) and their associations with clinicopathological variables and survival outcomes. Immunohistochemical expression of EGFR-1 and VEGF-A was evaluated in tumor samples from 33 cats with cSCC enrolled prospectively (n = 24) and retrospec- tively (n = 9). Associations between immunoexpression scores and clinicopatho- logical variables, overall survival time (OST), disease-free interval (DFI), and time to progression (TTP) were assessed using appropriate statistical tests. EGFR-1 positivity was detected in 78.8% (26/33) of cases and was significantly associated with shorter OST, perineural invasion, and intense inflammatory infiltrate. VEGF-A immunoexpression was detected in 71.9% (23/32) of cases and was significantly associated with previous history of cSCC, perineural invasion (PNI), and tumor invasion beyond the subcutaneous fat. These findings suggest that EGFR-1 and VEGF-A immunoexpression are associated with clinicopathological variables linked to aggressive tumor behavior in feline cSCC, supporting their potential role as prognostic biomarkers in this species and warranting further investigation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Cadaveric study of the ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block over the dorsolateral edge of the transverse process of the ninth thoracic vertebra in dogs: transverse vs. longitudinal approach.
papers.authors: Herrera-Linares ME, Sanchis-Mora S, Zamora-Perarnau C, Fernández-Salesa N, Rico-Pérez B, Herrera-Gutiérrez ME, Serra-Aguado CI, Fernández-Parra R
papers.abstract: Studies of the ultrasound-guided thoracic erector spinae plane (ESP) blocks in dogs are limited. This study aimed to describe a transverse (TV) ultrasound-guided ESP approach at the dorsolateral edge of the transverse process (DLETP) of T9, compare its distribution with a longitudinal (LNG) approach, and analyze the thoracic transverse process anatomy. Twenty-three canine cadavers were used in this double-blinded experimental study. An ESP injection using 0.6 mL/kg of dye/contrast was performed on each lateral of 21 cadavers with a TV or LNG approach at T9, followed by computed tomography and dissection. Five cadavers were excluded from dissection analysis. All TV injections were placed over the DLETP, whereas 18.75% of LNG injections were misplaced laterally. Both approaches produced craniocaudal spread within the ESP, with median (range) spreads of 8 (5-14) and 8.5 (4-13) vertebrae for the TV and LNG groups, respectively. Cranial spread exceeded caudal in the TV group, with 4.5 (2-6) vs. 3.5 (0-7) vertebrae ( p = 0.027), and LNG, with 5 (3-7) vs. 3 (0-6) ( p = 0.004). Staining of the medial branches of the dorsal rami (MBDR) of the spinal nerves showed median (range) values of 5 (4-8) and 5 (0-6) in TV and LNG. Cranial MBDR staining predominated in TV, with 4.5 (1-6) over caudal with 1 (0-3) ( p = 0.003), and LNG, with 4 (0-6) vs. 0 (0-3) ( p < 0.001). Lateral branches (LBDR) staining showed 4 (1-9) and 4 (2-12) in TV and LNG. Cranial LBDR staining exceeded caudal in TV, with 3 (0-6) vs. 1 (0-3) ( p = 0.019), and LNG, with 3 (1-8) vs. 1 (0-5) ( p = 0.034). Ventral branches staining occurred in 10/16 TV injections (62.5%) and 11/16 (68.75%) LNG. Both approaches showed epidural and sympathetic trunk spread while one intravascular injection occurred in LNG. No significant differences were found between approaches. The DLETP was predominantly absent caudal to T10 and smaller than the transverse process ( p < 0.001). The TV and LNG approaches produced comparable nerve staining and ESP spread at T9 in dogs, with preferential cranial distribution. The TV approach reduced injectate misplacement. The DLETP was smaller than the transverse process and consistently identified cranial to T11.

papers.title: Pyelonephritis in cats and dogs - a scoping review.
papers.authors: Pelander L, Ekstrand C, Scahill K
papers.abstract: There is a lack of consensus regarding the diagnosis and treatment of bacterial pyelonephritis (PN) in dogs and cats. The aim of this scoping review was to increase knowledge by describing published scientific literature on the subject, specifically to collate definitions and diagnostic criteria, antimicrobial regimens, reported outcomes, and to identify knowledge gaps. A structured search was performed of the bibliographic databases Biosis, CAB Abstracts, Medline, Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. We included 176 original studies written in English or German that reported on any aspect of spontaneous PN (risk factors, signalment, history, clinical findings, diagnostic criteria, treatment, prognosis, and outcome) in cats or dogs. Three types of PN were identified in the literature: histologically diagnosed PN, clinically diagnosed PN, and pyonephrosis. Multiple information gaps regarding clinical aspects of PN in dogs and cats were detected. There were no universally accepted clinical criteria for clinical diagnosis of PN and no clinical trials evaluating antimicrobial or other treatment options. Information about short-term outcomes for dogs and cats with PN was scarce, and there were no data regarding long-term outcomes. More information regarding all aspects of clinical PN in dogs and cats is needed.The study protocol was registered prospectively in 2023 ( https://syreaf.org/protocols/ ).

papers.title: High prevalence of virulent and multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli as the most frequently isolated bacterium associated with bacterial pneumonia in farmed raccoon dogs.
papers.authors: Li H, Li C, Zhu X, Zhu Z, Chen G, Ren C, Zhu S, Wu T, Chen L, Li Y, Shi Q, Zhang Z
papers.abstract: Bacterial pneumonia is a leading cause of mortality in fur-bearing animals, representing a significant challenge for the industry. Bacterial pneumonia is caused by a variety of pathogens, making its prevention and control difficult. This study aims to identify the primary etiological agents of bacterial pneumonia in farmed raccoon dogs in eastern Hebei and southern Liaoning provinces. To this end, we collected 159 pneumonic raccoon dogs between 2022 and 2025 for bacterial isolation and identification. We isolated 109 strains of Escherichia coli, 37 strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and 13 strains of Klebsiella pneumoniae, identifying E. coli as the most frequently isolated bacterium. Further investigations revealed that E. coli caused multisystemic infection in raccoon dogs: the bacterium was detected in the liver, spleen, kidney, and blood, with the most severe lesions observed in the lungs, suggesting potential systemic dissemination. Histopathological examination results revealed multi-organ damage consistent with bacterial infection, which correlates with the isolation of E. coli from affected tissues. Pathogenicity assays demonstrated that the isolated E. coli strains exhibited notable pathogenic potential in a mouse model, capable of reproducing typical pneumonia symptoms via intranasal inoculation. Virulence gene profiling of the isolates showed that all strains harbored at least 5 virulence genes. Among these, the virulence genes ompR, phoU, tonB, fimH, fimC, and Ecs3737 exhibited high detection rates, at 94.5%, 94.5%, 93.58%, 84.4%, 77.98%, and 60.55%, respectively. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) results revealed severe multidrug resistance (MDR) among the clinical E. coli isolates. The isolates showed universal resistance to nalidixic acid and ampicillin, and no single antimicrobial agent was fully effective against all strains. The resistance profiles of the E. coli isolates varied significantly between the two geographic regions studied. Resistance gene detection showed extremely high detection rates (≥ 80%) for quinolone resistance-associated chromosomal target genes and plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance (PMQR) genes, as well as integron-associated mobile elements. The detection rates of aminoglycoside, sulfonamide, and polypeptide resistance genes ranged from 30% to 70%, while those of amphenicol, β-lactam, macrolide, and tetracycline resistance genes were between 3% and 30%. Taken together, these data indicate that E. coli is the most frequently isolated bacterium associated with bacterial pneumonia in sampled farmed raccoon dogs in eastern Hebei and southern Liaoning, with notable pathogenic potential in mouse models and a high prevalence of complex multidrug resistance. These findings provide critical baseline data for guiding clinical antimicrobial use and developing disease control strategies in raccoon dog farming.

papers.title: Vertebral cardiac size and heart location of the Syrian hamster (Mesocricetus auratus) in radiographs and in situ gross dissections.
papers.authors: Nourinezhad J, Molaei A, Moarabi A, Borujeni MP, Sabiza S, Janeczek M
papers.abstract: Syrian hamsters (SHs) are a widely used translational cardiovascular research model and popular pets in which cardiac disease has been reported. However, despite their relevance, no information on vertebral heart size (VHS) and cardiac location in this species has been published. This study aimed to examine the hearts of SHs using radiographic and anatomical methods, focusing on VHS and cardiac location, along with the effects of sex, body weight, and body length. Twenty-four healthy adult Syrian hamsters were included in this study. Evaluation of the cardiac silhouette, its radiographic measurements, and cardiac topography was performed in 22 animals, while anatomical cardiac measurements were obtained from 18 suitable cadavers. The cardiac silhouette was typically located between the first intercostal space and the fourth rib, with the majority of the cardiac silhouette oriented to the left side of the median plane. Radiographic VHS values were significantly greater in females than in males A statistically significant inter-observer variation in the radiographic VHS was noted. No significant correlation was found between radiographic or anatomic VHS and body weight or body length. The mean radiographic and anatomic VHS were 8.9 and 6.69 vertebrae, respectively, with the former being significantly higher than the latter (P ≤ 0.001), indicating that the magnification of the heart was greater than the magnification of the vertebrae. Although the cardiac silhouette orientation in SHs was similar to that in rats, mice, and chinchillas, its position differed from that in mice, rats, guinea pigs, agoutis, and rabbits. The mean radiographic VHS in this study was larger than values reported for rabbits, rats, guinea pigs, agoutis, and prairie dogs, but smaller than those of chinchillas and mice. This study provides the first baseline reference values for VHS in Syrian hamsters and suggests that radiography, considering sex-related variations, is a reliable tool for cardiac size assessment. These findings provide useful data for both clinical and experimental cardiology in this species.

papers.title: Seventeen Cases of Fungal Otitis Externa in Dogs and Cats.
papers.authors: Tang X, Luo X, Liu X, Zhao B, Wang F, Han HS
papers.abstract: Otitis externa (OE) is common in dogs and cats. Fungal OE (FOE) caused by non-Malassezia species fungi is relatively uncommon. Comprehensive information on clinical manifestations, risk factors and breeds or species predispositions remains sparse. In this case series, we describe 17 companion animals in China with FOE. To describe the clinical signs, potential risk factors and treatment of FOE in dogs and cats. Seventeen cases: four dogs and 13 cats. Retrospective review of medical records of cases presented to dermatology specialty practices for OE between 2022 and 2024 was performed. Records with positive fungal culture results were included. Case demographic, diagnostic and treatment information was extracted. Aspergillus spp. was isolated from 13 animals (three dogs, 10 cats), Microsporum canis from one dog and two cats, and one cat had a mixed infection with M. canis in the left ear and Aspergillus spp. in the right. The most common clinical signs were excessive cerumen and pruritus. Of 16 cases that received antifungal treatment, 13 received combined oral and topical therapy, and three received only oral therapy. Aspergillus spp. or dermatophyte infection should not be overlooked in cases of chronic or recurrent OE. Cytological examination of exudates and fungal culture are useful for establishing the diagnosis of FOE. Larger prospective studies are needed to elucidate risk factors and appropriate treatment for FOE.

papers.title: Efficacy of Heat-Killed Lactobacillus plantarum L-137 Supplementation in Treatment of Canine Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.authors: Kiewsiri C, Patumcharoenpol P, Kovitvadhi A, Chermprapai S
papers.abstract: Canine atopic dermatitis (cAD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease and has been associated with gut dysbiosis. To evaluate the efficacy of heat-killed Lactobacillus plantarum L-137 (HK L-137), a postbiotic supplementation in managing cAD. Twelve client-owned dogs with cAD. A randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blinded crossover trial. Dogs were divided into two groups (n = 6) and received oral HK L-137 or placebo once daily for 12 weeks. After a 2-week washout period, they received the alternative treatment. Oral oclacitinib (0.4-0.6 mg/kg once daily) was permitted throughout the study. Clinical severity was assessed with the 4th iteration of the cAD Extent and Severity Index (CADESI-04) and owner-evaluated pruritus Visual Analog Scale (PVAS) and faecal scoring at 0, 12, 14 and 26 weeks. Serum concentrations of C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin (IL)-4, interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and C-C motif chemokine ligand 17 (CCL17), and haematological and biochemical findings were analysed at the same time points. Faecal microbiota composition (genomic DNA) was assessed at 12 and 26 weeks. PVAS scores mildly improved in both groups, with greater reduction in the HK L-137 group, yet this was not statistically significant. Serum CRP concentrations increased significantly in the control group (p = 0.02). Serum CCL17 concentrations decreased significantly in the HK L-137 group (p = 0.01). No significant changes were observed in CADESI-04, IL-4, IFN-γ or faecal scores or faecal microbiota diversity and composition. HK L-137 represents a potential, well-tolerated adjunctive therapy for dogs with cAD. Therapy was associated with reduced CCL17. Further studies with fewer variables are indicated.

papers.title: Diagnostic and stewardship considerations in fungal lower urinary tract infections of dogs and cats.
papers.authors: Prior C, Sykes JE, Barrs VR, Rautemaa-Richardson R, Klingspor L, Cornely OA, Gull T, Allerton F, Govender NP, Weese JS
papers.abstract: Fungal cystitis in dogs and cats presents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, with implications for antifungal stewardship in veterinary medicine. Unlike bacterial cystitis, diagnostic pathways for fungal infection are less well-defined, and antifungal therapy is often empirical. This article discusses key considerations for the diagnosis and management of fungal urinary tract infections, including the interpretation of urine cytology, the potential role and limitations of fungal culture, and the value of species-level identification and antifungal susceptibility testing. Clinical, laboratory, and pharmacokinetic factors that influence treatment decisions are highlighted, alongside the effect of confounding host and iatrogenic risk factors. The article also explores current gaps in evidence, variability in laboratory capabilities, and opportunities for strengthening antifungal stewardship in veterinary practice. Rather than providing prescriptive recommendations, this work aims to raise awareness, facilitate informed decision-making, and guide future research and consensus-building efforts to improve outcomes for animals while contributing to broader antifungal stewardship initiatives. Fungal infections of the urinary tract are uncommon in dogs and cats but can be difficult to diagnose and treat. Unlike bacterial urinary infections, there is less agreement about the best way to confirm a fungal infection and choose appropriate treatment. This article discusses how veterinarians can interpret findings from urine examination and fungal culture, and how identifying the fungal species and testing its response to antifungal drugs might help guide treatment decisions. It also considers factors related to the animal, laboratory testing, and medications that can affect diagnosis and treatment. The article highlights important gaps in current knowledge and differences in laboratory capabilities and emphasizes the need for careful use of antifungal drugs. Rather than providing specific treatment recommendations, this work aims to improve understanding of fungal urinary tract infections, support informed clinical decision-making, and identify priorities for future research and development of veterinary antifungal stewardship.

papers.title: Intestinal angioleiomyoma in a dog.
papers.authors: Nivy R, Bruchim Y, Eley T
papers.abstract: Angioleiomyoma is a rare, smooth muscle tumor of vascular origin, which primarily affects the skin. A 9-year-old, castrated male dog presented for transient ataxia. Abnormalities were not detected on physical examination, but blood tests revealed a mild, severely microcytic anemia and transferrin saturation of 2.5% (reference interval, 27%-66%). An exhaustive diagnostic work-up ensued but failed to find the cause of the severe iron deficiency in laboratory, imaging, and endoscopic studies. Severely microcytic anemia had persisted for 6 months, despite iron-dextran injections, and in the absence of clinical signs, until intussusception developed. The abnormal jejunal segment was removed and diagnosed as angioleiomyoma, based on characteristic histological features, positive immunolabeling with α-smooth muscle actin and CD31, and negative S100 and c-Kit/CD117 staining. Hitherto unreported in dogs, intestinal angioleiomyoma was associated with protracted, occult, asymptomatic intestinal blood loss, until intussusception developed. Prognosis appears favorable with full excision, based on clinical behavior in other organs, and the present case.

papers.title: Fibrostenotic intestinal stenosis associated with chronic enteropathy in two cats: case report.
papers.authors: Choi J, Yang S, Lee Y, Sung Y, Chae Y, Yun T, Kang BT, Kim S, Lee S, Kim H
papers.abstract: Two cats presented with acute progressive vomiting. One cat (Case 1) received prednisolone for suspected chronic inflammatory enteropathy for 14 months. The cat showed hypoalbuminemia, hypocobalaminemia, small intestinal thickening, and focal jejunal stricture with severe proximal dilation on ultrasonography. Exploratory laparotomy confirmed the stricture, and histopathology revealed submucosal fibroplasia with mild lymphoplasmacytic enteritis. The cat died on postoperative day 12. Another cat (Case 2) showed proximal small intestinal obstruction on ultrasonography. A wide-margin resection of the obstructed lesion was performed. Histopathology revealed mild intestinal wall fibrosis with mesenteric inflammation. Masson's trichrome staining showed submucosal collagen bundles. Immunohistochemistry and clonality analysis by PCR for antigen receptor rearrangement supported the diagnosis of low-grade intestinal T-cell lymphoma. The cat recovered uneventfully and remained restenosis-free during prednisolone treatment for 12 months after surgery. Intestinal stenoses were identified during long-term medical management of chronic enteropathy. This suggests that the extent of the lesion and the surgical resection strategy could be relevant factors for management and prognosis.

papers.title: A comparative study of diet choice and feeding management among UK pet and child caregivers.
papers.authors: Lumbis RH, Yam PS, Reilly JJ, Fontaine SJ
papers.abstract: Caregivers play a central role in shaping the dietary habits and nutritional health of dependents. However, the diversity of available diets and feeding advice can complicate everyday food decisions. This qualitative study explored how caregivers make feeding decisions for their children and pets, focusing on factors influencing diet choice, feeding practices, perceptions of nutrition, and emotional attachment to dependents. UK-based caregivers aged 18 years or older, responsible for at least one child aged up to 10 years and a cat and/or dog, were recruited between July and November 2024. Semi-structured online interviews were conducted with 17 participants. Audio recordings were transcribed and analyzed thematically using an interpretive approach. Ethical approval was granted. Four key themes emerged. First, participants framed nutrition as a moral responsibility across both children and pets, positioning feeding as central to health and wellbeing and shaped by knowledge, identity, emotional attachment, habits, and practical realities. Second, diet choice and feeding practices were shaped by psychosocial determinants, with caregivers' knowledge, beliefs, routines, emotional motivations, and social norms influencing feeding decisions across both children and pets. Third, feeding dynamics differed between contexts. Children's diets involved negotiation and bidirectional relationships shaped by preferences, routines, and agency, whereas pet feeding was more caregiver-directed, routine-based, and influenced by trust in nutritional adequacy and pet-specific needs. Fourth, feeding practices reflected relational attachment and emotional bonds. Although pets were considered valued family members, their feeding needs were generally prioritized below those of children. Across both contexts, caregivers relied on observable cues, emotional responses, and socially shared norms to assess appropriate feeding. Caregiving beliefs and feeding philosophies transfer across contexts in complex ways, highlighting opportunities for family-focused interventions that support evidence-based nutrition for both people and animals.

papers.title: Occurrence and antimicrobial resistance of Acinetobacter baumannii in cats, veterinary hospital environments and medical wastes in Bangladesh.
papers.authors: Hasan M, Lira SA, Islam A, Miti AA, Rahman A, Suchy SA, Jahan I, Ali SB, Parvin MS, Islam MT
papers.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii presence in veterinary hospitals and companion animals is still poorly investigated despite its significance. The present study aimed to investigate the prevalence, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and resistance genes of A. baumannii in cats, veterinary hospital environments, and veterinary medical wastes in Bangladesh. Samples were collected from oral, rectal, and wound swabs of cats (n = 100) attending ten veterinary hospitals, as well as from environmental surfaces (n = 111) and wastes (n = 61) generated within these facilities. Isolates were identified by PCR targeting 16S rRNA (genus) and bla OXA-51-like (species) genes; antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed by disk diffusion and broth microdilution following CLSI standards, and resistance genes (bla OXA-23-like , bla NDM-1 ) were screened by PCR. A high prevalence of A. baumannii was observed in cats (37%), while 26.1% in environmental samples and 21.3% in waste samples. Apparently sick cats had significantly higher prevalence (p = 0.049) than apparently healthy cats. All isolates were imipenem resistant, consistent with carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB). High resistance was also observed against cefotaxime and ceftriaxone. Multidrug resistance (MDR) was detected in 26.7%, 37.9%, and 30.8% of isolates from cats, environmental, and waste sources, respectively. The bla OXA-23-like gene was detected in only two cat isolates, whereas bla NDM was identified in one cat isolate and one environmental isolate. In conclusion, these findings identify cats, which live in close proximity to humans, as a possible CRAB reservoir, and veterinary hospital environments and waste as potential sources of persistence and dissemination, raising concern for zoonotic spread and underscoring occupational and public health risk.

papers.title: EXPRESS:Management of Distal Hindlimb Injuries in Cats Using an Exvet External Skeletal Fixation System: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Uygur S, Dogan A, Yardımcı C, Ulusan S, Beale BS, Immler M, Vidoni B, Schnabl-Feichter E
papers.abstract: To evaluate the clinical use of an Exvet external skeletal fixation (ESF) system applied using minimally invasive techniques for the management of distal hindlimb injuries in cats. Cats with distal hindlimb injuries treated using the Exvet Tarsal Fixator (ETF) at four institutions between September 2022 and January 2026 were included. Data collected included fracture type, surgical approach, postoperative complications and additional treatments, time to first limb use, time to fixator removal, radiographic findings, and clinical outcome. Of 73 cats evaluated, 35 cats with 36 distal hindlimb injuries met the inclusion criteria. Twenty-four cats (68.6%) were managed with a closed reduction, while 11 cats (31.4%) were managed with a limited open surgical fashion. Thirty-two of 35 cats (91.4%) started weight bearing immediately after surgery. Complications were recorded in 7 of 35 cases (20.0%), of which 5 cases (14.3%) were classified as minor and 2 cases (5.7%) as major complications. At a mean ESF removal time of 34 days (median: 28 days; range: 21-56 days), a full functional outcome was achieved in 25 of 35 cases (71.4%), while 10 cases (28.6%) showed an acceptable functional outcome. The ETF is an anatomically designed ESF implant specifically developed for feline distal hindlimb injuries. The findings of this multicenter retrospective study support its safe and effective use for the management of feline distal hindlimb injuries.

papers.title: EXPRESS: BENEFITS OF CONTRAST-ENHANCED COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY OVER PLAIN COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY FOR HEAD TRAUMA IN 41 CATS.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Mariaud V, Arinal P, Masson A, Mortier J
papers.abstract: The aim of this study is to evaluate whether contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) provides clinically useful information beyond Plain computed tomography (PCT) in cats with head trauma, and whether this benefit is influenced by the radiologist's level of experience. Forty-one cats that underwent head CT with both pre- and post-contrast sequences were included. Images were independently reviewed by three radiologists with different experience levels, assessing extracranial soft tissue injuries, bone fractures, and intracranial abnormalities. Intra- and interobserver agreements were analyzed using Cohen's kappa statistics. Substantial to almost perfect agreement was obtained for extracranial soft tissue injuries and bone fractures. The most commonly fractured sites were the temporomandibular joints, hard palate, mandibular bones, and pterygoid bones. For intracranial lesions such as hemorrhage and cerebral edema, intra- and interobserver agreements were low and variable, regardless of contrast use or reviewer experience. There was no significant difference found between PCT and CECT for any of the three categories. These results suggest that contrast medium injection is not useful for assessment of bone fractures and extracranial soft tissue and that computed tomography of the head is poorly reliable for intracranial lesions in cats presented for trauma.

papers.title: Feline viral infections: current perspectives on diagnosis, treatment and prevention.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Hosie MJ

papers.title: Effect of oral gabapentin administered in-hospital on behavioral stress, compliance, and physiologic stress markers: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Canosa C, Summers SC
papers.abstract: The aim of the study was to determine whether post admission oral gabapentin improves stress indices and handling tolerance in hospitalized cats. In this double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-design trial, healthy client-owned cats were enrolled. After the initial examination, cats received a 100 mg gabapentin or placebo capsule. At 90 min, a second examination, venipuncture, and brief dorsal positioning were performed. Five stress behaviors (struggling, vocalization, repelling, hypersalivation, mouth breathing), compliance, and enclosure activity score (1, sedate; 5, very active) were recorded; blood glucose, lactate, serum cortisol, and lymphocyte count were measured. Serum gabapentin concentrations were obtained 90 min after the capsule. A total of 30 cats (15 cats/group) were included in analysis. In the 15 cats who received gabapentin, the median gabapentin dose was 21.7 mg/kg (range 14.3-28.1), yielding a median serum concentration of 16.4 µg/ml (range 1.3-24.5). Most gabapentin-treated cats exhibited fewer stress behaviors (n = 13/15, 87%) and better compliance for handling during examination (n = 11/15, 73%) at 90 min post-capsule compared with 3/15 (20%) and 4/15 (27%), respectively, in placebo cats. Between-group differences were not detected for behavioral or compliance scores during venipuncture or dorsal positioning. Enclosure activity scores in the gabapentin group decreased from median 3 at baseline to 2 from 90-360 min post-dose (120, 240, and 300 min; P <0.05, respectively), consistent with mild sedation. Blood lactate and cortisol concentrations were lower in the gabapentin group than the placebo group ( P  = 0.002 and P  = 0.04, respectively). A 100 mg oral dose of gabapentin provides modest improvement in stress behaviors during examination and favorably alters select physiologic stress markers within 90 min of administration, with sustained reductions in kennel activity. Findings support incorporating gabapentin within a multimodal, low-stress approach for cats presenting without preappointment medication, while maintaining contingency plans for additional sedation as needed. Giving gabapentin in the hospital can modestly calm cats for examinations within 90 minutes Many cats become stressed during veterinary visits, which can make examinations and simple procedures difficult. Because some visits are unplanned, cats may arrive without any anxiety-reducing medications on board. We studied whether giving a single oral dose of gabapentin (a commonly used calming medicine) after admission could help. In total, 30 healthy pet cats were enrolled. Each cat first had a brief examination. Then cats received either a 100 mg gabapentin capsule or an inactive placebo pill by mouth. About 90 min later, we repeated the examination and carried out routine handling (a blood draw and brief positioning on the back). We scored each cat’s behavior and how easy the cat was to handle. We also noted how active the cat was while resting in the kennel for several hours. Blood tests included measures linked to stress (cortisol and lactate). Cats who received gabapentin showed modest improvements during the second examination: they struggled less and were easier to handle. Their blood tests also suggested lower stress (cortisol and lactate were lower) compared with cats who received the placebo pill. In their kennels, cats given gabapentin were less active for several hours, consistent with mild calming. However, we did not see clear differences between groups during the more uncomfortable steps (the blood draw and brief positioning). Giving gabapentin in the hospital can help with routine examination and gentle handling within about 90 min, especially for moderately stressed cats. It is best used as part of a broader, low-stress approach (quiet space, gentle handling, towels/pheromones) and may not be enough on its own for more invasive procedures. Responses varied between cats, likely because absorption of a single capsule can differ.

papers.title: Feline-Derived Lactiplantibacillus plantarum -Aloe Vera Polysaccharide Hydrogel as a Topical Control Strategy for Staphylococcus pseudintermedius -Infected Wounds.
papers.authors: Chen Q, Dong H, Wang W, Wang H, Yao J, Ma M, Zhu S, Zhu L, Du Z, Xia Z, Xiong W
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus pseudintermedius (SP) is an important opportunistic pathogen in companion animals, and the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant strains highlights the need for alternative approaches to local infection control. This study evaluated a topical hydrogel containing feline-derived Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ZYpet-014 and Aloe vera polysaccharides (AVEs) for the treatment of SP-infected wounds. AVEs promoted LP growth and organic-acid production and improved short-term LP viability within the carbomer hydrogel. The LP+AVE-hydrogel inhibited planktonic SP growth and biofilm formation in vitro and caused pronounced morphological disruption of SP cells. Therapeutic efficacy was further evaluated using a full-thickness murine wound model challenged with SP. LP+AVE treatment accelerated wound closure, reaching 95.75% by day 14, while qualitative histological observations suggested improved tissue organization and differences in collagen-associated staining patterns. Treatment was also associated with reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels and increased IL-4, IL-10, TGF-β1, and serum VEGF concentrations. In wound tissues, LP+AVE treatment decreased CD80 and increased CD206 immunoreactivity, consistent with a shift in macrophage-associated responses toward a reparative profile. Moreover, 16S rRNA gene sequencing showed reduced relative abundance of Staphylococcus and increased relative abundance of Lactobacillus in treated wounds. Together, these findings demonstrate antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against SP in vitro, accompanied by improved wound healing, modulation of inflammatory responses, and changes in wound microbial composition in vivo, although direct reduction in SP burden in wound tissue remains to be established.

papers.title: Exploratory Evaluation of Refractometric, Biochemical, and Body Weight Change Parameters for Diagnosing Failure of Passive Transfer in Puppies.
papers.authors: Kara H, Şenel Y, Kaya U, Güven M, Şenol A
papers.abstract: Failure of passive transfer (FPT) is an important determinant of survival in neonatal puppies. Practical indirect indicators that could serve as alternatives to measuring serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) have not yet been adequately characterized. In this exploratory study, 76 Turkish Kangal puppies aged 48 ± 4 h, born to 12 dams (mean age 40.2 months) were evaluated. Serum IgG measured by ELISA was the reference method, with values below 2.3 g/L classified as FPT. Whole-blood, fresh-serum, and frozen-thawed serum Brix values were evaluated together with serum total protein, albumin, globulin, gamma-glutamyl transferase, canine parvovirus antibody levels, and percentage change in body weight from birth to sampling, using receiver operating characteristic analysis. FPT was identified in six puppies (7.9%). The area under the curve (AUC) values for total protein, globulin, and percentage change in body weight were 0.986, 0.981, and 0.948, respectively, with the associated cutoffs considered exploratory; each detected all six cases with 82.9-94.3% specificity. Fresh-serum Brix showed moderate discrimination (AUC: 0.771), whereas whole-blood Brix was inconclusive (AUC: 0.432). Total protein, globulin, and early body weight change are promising screening indicators for detecting FPT. However, because of the limited number of cases, their cutoffs should be validated in larger populations, including other breeds, before clinical use.

papers.title: Cardiac Vagal Decoupling in Canine Anesthesia: A Physiological Concept for Graded Vasopressor Titration.
papers.authors: Nagahama S
papers.abstract: During general anesthesia in dogs, vasopressor-induced increases in mean arterial pressure (MAP) may be partly opposed by reflex sinus slowing. Subsequent administration of atropine or another antimuscarinic may cause an abrupt increase in sinus rate; when vascular tone is already elevated, this increase may in turn contribute to an abrupt or excessive MAP rise. This article examines cardiac vagal decoupling, defined as reduced vagally mediated muscarinic restraint at the sinoatrial node, as a physiological concept for graded vasopressor titration. The hypothesis is that reducing this restraint before substantial vasopressor escalation, followed by MAP-guided dose adjustments, may permit more graded pressure control: reaching and maintaining a specified MAP range with fewer abrupt or excessive pressure increases. Canine studies support muscarinic control of sinus rate, baroreflex responses during anesthesia, and modification of vasopressor responses by prior antimuscarinic administration. These findings support components of the proposed concept, but whether it improves graded MAP titration has not been directly tested. The article contrasts the two hemodynamic patterns, evaluates the supporting evidence, and considers the limits of the hypothesis. Effects of such titration on cardiac output, tissue perfusion, and clinical outcomes require separate evaluation.

papers.title: CT-Clinical Dissociation and Focal Obstruction in Feline Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Pilot Study.
papers.authors: Lee G, Chang J, Lee J, Song KH
papers.abstract: Feline chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is common and difficult to manage, and the relationship between computed tomography (CT) findings and clinical severity remains unclear. This exploratory retrospective pilot study included 10 cats with chronic upper respiratory signs for at least 4 weeks that underwent CT of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses at a single referral hospital. Newly developed, unvalidated semiquantitative scores graded CT severity (0-12) and clinical severity (0-12), and cats were grouped into four provisional clinicoradiologic patterns using integrated CT, clinical, and cytologic findings and, where available, microbiologic findings. CT scores ranged from 2 to 10 (median 8.0) and clinical scores from 4 to 11 (median 6.5), without a consistent monotonic association (Spearman r s = 0.250, 95% bootstrap confidence interval (CI) -0.558 to 0.885, p = 0.486). The provisional patterns were active/exudative ( n = 2), structural/remodeling ( n = 4), obstructive ( n = 3), and immune/mucosal ( n = 1). Focal obstruction defined both the obstructive pattern and the conceptual surgical candidacy categories, so their overlap is by design; of interest is that cats with the highest CT scores did not necessarily have focal obstruction. No cat underwent surgery. These hypothesis-generating findings require validation in larger prospective studies with validated scores.

papers.title: Regulatory Science for Veterinary Therapeutic Innovation: A Comparative Analysis of Drug Development Incentives Within the One Health Framework.
papers.authors: Hong S, Lee SM
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in antiviral therapeutics, targeted biologics, RNA medicines, and precision veterinary medicine are generating unprecedented scientific opportunities for veterinary healthcare, yet translation of these innovations into approved veterinary products remains disproportionately slow. This review employs a comparative regulatory science framework to identify the regulatory and economic determinants of this innovation gap across four jurisdictions-FDA-CVM (US), EMA-CVMP (EU), PMDA/MAFF (Japan), and APVMA (Australia)-and to compare existing incentive instruments and identify the regulatory gaps between them. Two illustrative case studies, GS-441524 for feline infectious peritonitis and canine osteosarcoma therapeutics, illustrate how the absence of breakthrough pathways, limitations in the practical translation of Minor Use/Minor Species (MUMS) eligibility, and unresolved intellectual property barriers can suppress development investment. The multi-jurisdictional analysis indicates that this innovation gap is evident across the jurisdictions examined and is consistent with differences in the availability and strength of regulatory incentives, though scientific and market factors likely also contribute. Policy reforms are proposed, including a Veterinary Breakthrough Drug Designation, a One Health Innovation Designation with enhanced exclusivity, adaptive regulatory pathways, and strengthened VICH harmonization. Additionally, the regulatory preparedness for advanced veterinary therapeutics-including gene therapies, mRNA-based vaccines, and cell-based products-is examined as a critical frontier. The analysis highlights the role of regulatory science in translating emerging veterinary therapeutics into clinical practice within the One Health framework.

papers.title: Dietary Pieris japonica Leaf Powder Enhances Hepatic Antioxidant Capacity, Modulates Cecal Microbiota, and Improves Eggshell Thickness in Laying Hens.
papers.authors: Wu Y, Chen J, Chen F, Liu Y, Lian J, Tang Y, He B, Lin Q
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress and intestinal health are critical factors that are closely linked to the production performance and physiological status of laying hens. This work assessed how dietary incorporation of Pieris japonica leaf powder (PJP) shapes egg quality attributes, hepatic antioxidant defence, gut tissue morphology, and cecal microbial community profiles in layers. A total of 360 healthy 56-week-old Hy-Line Brown layers were randomly assigned to four treatments, each containing six replicate pens housing 15 birds apiece. Animals received basal feeds containing 0.00% (control), 0.05%, 0.10%, or 0.20% PJP throughout the 10-week experimental run that including a 2-week adaptation period. Relative to the control group, diets with 0.05% PJP significantly increased eggshell thickness ( p < 0.05). Hepatic total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) were significantly elevated in PJP-supplemented groups ( p < 0.05). The 0.10% PJP addition improved duodenal villus-height-to-crypt-depth ratio (V/C). Regarding cecal microbiota, 0.10% PJP reduced the Simpson index while elevating Collinsella relative abundance ( p < 0.05). Noticeably, the 0.20% supplementation exerted adverse effects on egg-related indices. Correlation analysis indicated that cecal microbiota was closely associated with hepatic antioxidant indices and eggshell-related indicators. In summary, dietary PJP inclusion may improve the eggshell thickness of eggs from laying hens by enhancing host antioxidant defense, reshaping the composition of cecal microbial communities. It was reported that 0.10% PJP supplementation yielded the most favorable comprehensive responses under the conditions adopted within this trial.

papers.title: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia with Secondary Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection in a Dog: Endoscopic and Diagnostic Findings.
papers.authors: Maggi G, Pirgher F, De Lorenzi D, Aresu L, Marchesi MC
papers.abstract: A 7-month-old, 3.6-kg, intact male Dachshund was presented with a lifelong history of chronic respiratory signs. Multiple courses of antimicrobial therapy resulted in partial or complete clinical improvement, followed by recurrence after treatment discontinuation. To investigate the underlying cause of the persistent respiratory disease, rhino-tracheobronchoscopy was performed. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid and respiratory mucosal biopsy specimens were collected for cytological, histopathological, and ultrastructural evaluation. Cytological examination of BAL fluid revealed septic neutrophilic inflammation, and bacterial culture yielded P. aeruginosa.
