Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) identified ultrastructural abnormalities of the ciliary axoneme in 50% of the examined respiratory cilia. Based on these findings, primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) was diagnosed. PCD is a rare congenital disorder characterized by structural and functional abnormalities of motile cilia, resulting in impaired mucociliary clearance and recurrent respiratory infections. This case highlights the diagnostic value of a detailed clinical history, endoscopic examination, and TEM in dogs with suspected PCD.

papers.title: Pulmonary Neoplasms with Pleuropulmonary Blastoma-like Features in Two Young Labrador Retrievers: Clinicopathological, Molecular and Comparative Characterisation.
papers.authors: van der Weyden L, Francis BA, Olson DR, Schultz KAP, Di Palma S, Ryan T, Kamieniarz K, Miguel-Garces M, Thompson L, Jones R, Nix C, Haugland S, Ortiz AL
papers.abstract: Pleuropulmonary blastoma (PPB) is a rare, paediatric, mesenchymal, pulmonary neoplasm that can be highly aggressive. To date, there are only two reports of PPB in animals. We describe the finding of pulmonary neoplasms with PPB-like features in two unrelated Labrador Retrievers. Both dogs presented with acute dyspnoea, pneumothorax and pulmonary lesions. Treatment consisted of emergency thoracostomy tube placement followed by lung lobectomy. At follow-up, one dog experienced no recurrence 20 months post-surgery, whereas recurrence developed in the second dog 2 years postoperatively. Histopathological examination revealed spindle-shaped neoplastic cells with blastematous-to-sarcomatous appearance, associated with cystic spaces lined by non-neoplastic respiratory epithelium. Immunohistochemistry showed that the neoplastic cells were positive for mesenchymal markers but negative for epithelial and neuroendocrine markers, with some tumour cells showing desmin positivity, supportive of myogenic differentiation, possibly compatible with rhabdomyoblastic differentiation. Genome profiling revealed a heterogeneous somatic landscape. No pathogenic somatic or germline DICER1 variants were found. We compared these findings with those reported in human PPB. This is the first comprehensive analysis of pulmonary neoplasms with PPB-like features in animals, and reveals parallels with PPB in humans, further supporting the 'One Medicine' approach.

papers.title: Prostaglandin-Endoperoxide Synthase 2 (PTGS2) Expression Is Increased in Chronic Asymptomatic Orchitis in the Dog.
papers.authors: Packeiser EM, Körber H, Morawietz J, Goericke-Pesch S
papers.abstract: Chronic asymptomatic orchitis (CAO) in dogs lacks effective treatment options. To elucidate the involvement of prostaglandin endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2), associated with inflammation and physiological steroidogenesis, testicular PTGS2 and StAR gene (via RT-qPCR) and protein expression (via immunohistochemistry) were analyzed in 11 canine CAO samples and compared to five normospermic control group (CG) samples. The percentage of immunopositive area (PIA) and mean gray scale (MGS) intensity were evaluated in the interstitial and tubular compartments. In CAO, PTGS2 and StAR gene expression levels were significantly increased compared to CG ( p < 0.001 and p = 0.0034). Leydig cells and some peritubular cells stained immunopositive for PTGS2 and StAR and Sertoli cells positive for PTGS2. PIA and MGS for PTGS2 differed significantly between groups in the interstitial (PIA: p < 0.0001; MGS: p = 0.0051) and tubular (PIA: p = 0.0006; MGS: p = 0.0413) compartments. For StAR, PIA, but not MGS, was significantly higher in CAO ( p = 0.0010). Except for PTGS2 gene expression, higher degrees of spermatogenetic impairment correlated with more prominent expression changes. This study demonstrates an association between increased PTGS2 expression and CAO. Further research is needed to investigate potential clinical benefits of selective PTGS2 inhibitors.

papers.title: Perioperative Glycemic Changes Following Partial Pancreatectomy for a Pancreatic Islet Cell Neoplasm in a Dog: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Choi CH, Kim JW, Park MS, Cho JS, You DH, Kim JH, Eom KD, Kim HY, Kim JM
papers.abstract: Canine insulinomas are functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors that typically cause hypoglycemia, but blood glucose may fluctuate before surgery and increase after resection. This report describes the diagnostic evaluation, surgical treatment, and perioperative glycemic course of a 12-year-old female Miniature Schnauzer with a pancreatic islet cell neoplasm considered clinically consistent with insulinoma. Intermittent low or low-normal blood glucose concentrations ranging from 54 to 72 mg/dL were documented before surgery, and the blood glucose concentration on the day of surgery was 73 mg/dL. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography identified a mass in the left pancreatic limb, and partial pancreatectomy was subsequently performed. Blood glucose reached 416 mg/dL 2 h after pancreatic mass removal while surgery was ongoing, then initially declined without insulin administration. Recurrent postoperative hyperglycemia was treated with regular insulin on postoperative days (PODs) 2 and 3, whereas subsequent decreases in blood glucose were treated with dextrose supplementation. Blood glucose continued to fluctuate on POD 4; no additional insulin was administered after POD 3. Histopathologic examination identified a pancreatic islet cell neoplasm. Although a paired serum insulin concentration during documented hypoglycemia was not available and immunohistochemical staining for insulin or other neuroendocrine markers was not performed, the clinical, imaging, glycemic, and histopathological findings were considered consistent with a clinicopathologic diagnosis of insulinoma. Blood glucose was 150 mg/dL on POD 7; subsequent recorded concentrations through POD 150 ranged from 107 to 133 mg/dL. Serial glucose monitoring helped characterize the perioperative course and guide postoperative insulin and dextrose treatment.

papers.title: Cytologically Suggested Vulvar Involvement in a Dog with Multicentric Lymphoma After a Nodal Response to CHOP-Based Chemotherapy, with Discordant Clonality Results: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Roh T, Song K
papers.abstract: Involvement of the female reproductive tract is rare in canine lymphoma. A 9-year-old spayed female Maltese dog was presented with generalized lymphadenopathy. Cytology of a mandibular lymph node aspirate indicated large cell lymphoma, whereas PCR for antigen receptor rearrangement (PARR) of the same sample was polyclonal. Splenectomy confirmed splenic large cell lymphoma, classified as World Health Organization clinical stage IVa. After 12 cycles of a CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisolone)-based protocol, restaging computed tomography showed a marked reduction in all measurable lymph nodes, whereas gastric and subcutaneous nodules persisted. On Day 181 (168 days after the start of chemotherapy), vulvar swelling was noticed and progressed despite antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory treatment, together with inguinal lymphadenopathy. Disease progression was diagnosed by inguinal lymph node cytology, and rescue chemotherapy was started; however, the dog developed acute dyspnea and died two days later. Results reported after death showed a mixed monoclonal and polyclonal immunoglobulin heavy chain (IgH) pattern in the inguinal lymph node and a clonal IgH rearrangement in the vulvar aspirate, which was cytologically consistent with lymphoma. In dogs treated for lymphoma, vulvar swelling may reflect neoplastic infiltration, and PARR results may differ between samples obtained at different sites and time points.

papers.title: A Salivary Conglomerate with a Substantial Organic Component Mimicking a Mineral Sialolith in the Mandibular-Sublingual Gland Complex of a Dog.
papers.authors: Schidu D, Zelinschi V, Hrițcu OM, Acomi ȘM, Ștefănescu RA, Șindilar EV, Burtan LC, Solcan G
papers.abstract: Solid lesions of the mandibular-sublingual salivary gland complex are rare in dogs. We report the case of an 11-year-old, 5 kg, intact female Maltese dog that presented with a non-painful, 2-3 cm left cervical swelling, soft at the surface and firm in depth. Fine-needle aspiration yielded clear, sero-mucous fluid. Radiographs revealed a well-defined, ovoid radiopaque structure measuring 3.1 × 2.9 cm in the cranial cervical region. Mandibular and monostomatic sublingual sialoadenectomy via a ventral approach revealed a large, heart-shaped, solid conglomerate within the glandular complex. Histopathological examination confirmed glandular atrophy, fibrosis and sialoadenitis. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectrometry of the submitted fragments indicated a substantial organic, protein- and lipid-rich component, with additional bands suggesting a possible minor mineral component. The dog healed completely, with no recurrence detected at the 2-week examination. Limitations include the absence of cross-sectional imaging and elemental analysis and the limited clinical follow-up. This case shows that protein-rich solid conglomerates should be included in the differential diagnosis of cervical swellings in dogs, that radiopacity alone does not establish mineral composition, and that complete surgical excision was associated with a favourable short-term outcome.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of the Fatty Acid Profiles of Hypoallergenic Veterinary Diets, Commercial Dog Foods, and Oral Fatty Acid Supplements Available on the Hungarian Market.
papers.authors: Tóth Z, Fébel H, Wágner L, Buránszki B, Lajos A, Vida K, Tarpataki N
papers.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), particularly the long-chain n-3 PUFAs (eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)), are integral to the dietary management of canine atopic dermatitis (CAD). However, the fatty acid profiles of commercially available canine products on Hungarian markets have not been systematically characterised, and the present study aimed to address this gap. A total of 35 products selected from those available on the Hungarian market at the time of sampling were analysed by gas chromatography with flame ionisation detection (GC-FID): 8 hypoallergenic veterinary diets (HVD), 22 commercial dog foods (CD), and 5 oral fatty acid supplements (FS). FS1-FS4 are complementary feeds under Regulation (EC) No 767/2009. FS5 is a food supplement under Directive 2002/46/EC. FS5 was included for comparative reference only. Fatty acid composition is expressed as % of total peak area. The n-6/n-3 ratio differed substantially across categories (HVD mean 6.16, range 2.65-10.71; CD mean 9.94, range 2.68-18.16; FS1-FS4 mean 18.08, range 0.29-63.49 (FS5 excluded as human product)). Combined % of EPA + DHA was lower in dietary products (HVD mean 0.94%, range 0.16-2.10%; CD mean 0.19%, range 0.09-0.34%) than in marine-based supplements (FS3 7.52%, FS4 24.19%). Alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) was the predominant n-3 fatty acid in 29 of 30 dietary products. Pronounced inter-product heterogeneity was observed among supplements, including one plant-based product with an n-6/n-3 ratio of 63.49. These findings indicate that commercial and hypoallergenic diets contain low proportion of EPA, and that marine-based oral supplementation provided substantially higher proportions of EPA and DHA than any dietary product evaluated.

papers.title: Transosseous Suture Fixation of an Inverted Palatal Mucoperiosteal Flap to Residual Buccal Alveolar Bone for Oronasal Fistula Repair in a Dog.
papers.authors: Lee JH, Lee S, Cho JS, Park C, Park BJ, Yoon S, Jeongwon L, Kim J, Kim HY, Kim JM
papers.abstract: Advanced periodontal disease can compromise the recipient tissues available for flap fixation during oronasal fistula repair. This report describes double-layer repair of an acquired periodontal oronasal fistula in an eight-year-old castrated male Beagle. Radiographs and computed tomography (CT) identified regional bone loss and residual alveolar bone adjacent to the defect. Following extraction of the left maxillary canine and second premolar and debridement of the fistula margins, an inverted hard palatal mucoperiosteal flap was anchored to residual buccal alveolar bone through four transosseous bone holes created with an 18-gauge needle. Transosseous suture fixation used 4-0 polydioxanone simple interrupted sutures. A buccal mucosal advancement flap covered the inverted flap and palatal donor site; no interpositional graft was used. Healing without clinically evident dehiscence was documented on postoperative day 18, and nasal discharge had resolved by day 45. At 555 days, visual oral examination revealed an intact repair, with concordant CT findings obtained for an unrelated otologic indication. This case illustrates the use of residual buccal alveolar bone for palatal flap attachment when periodontal tissue loss limits gingival recipient margins, with maintained closure documented at late clinical and imaging reassessment.

papers.title: Dietary Curcumin Protects Common Carp ( Cyprinus carpio ) Against Potassium Permanganate-Induced Toxicity: Hematological, Immunological, Oxidative, and Molecular Docking Evidence.
papers.authors: Eroğlu M, Mişe Yonar S, Tanrıkulu D, Uslu H, Yonar ME
papers.abstract: Potassium permanganate treatment can adversely affect fish physiology despite its usefulness in aquaculture. This study evaluated the protective effects of dietary curcumin against potassium permanganate-induced disturbances in common carp (Cyprinus carpio). Fish were fed a basal diet or diets supplemented with 1%, 2%, or 4% curcumin for eight weeks, with or without subsequent exposure to potassium permanganate at 2 mg/L for 30 min daily for seven days. Hematological and immune parameters and oxidative status in the liver, kidney, spleen, and gill were assessed. Potassium permanganate exposure altered blood and immune parameters, increased lipid peroxidation, and weakened antioxidant defenses. Curcumin supplementation alleviated these effects, with protection evident at 1%, the lowest dietary inclusion level tested, and further improvements in selected parameters at 4%. Inclusion levels below 1% were not evaluated, so the minimum effective level remains unknown. Molecular docking predicted interactions between curcumin and the antioxidant enzymes SOD, CAT, GPx, and GST at structurally plausible binding sites. These computational findings were interpreted alongside the biological results as supportive, hypothesis-generating evidence rather than confirmation of functional effects on these enzymes in vivo. Overall, dietary curcumin showed potential to reduce the physiological disturbances associated with repeated potassium permanganate exposure. Further dose-response studies should evaluate inclusion levels below 1% to identify effective and economically viable supplementation rates and determine whether curcumin affects the antiparasitic or antibacterial efficacy of potassium permanganate.

papers.title: Clinical Diagnostic Assessment of Serum Testosterone in Intact and Castrated Tomcats.
papers.authors: Tekin K, Pereira M, Pimazzoni L, Bonsembiante F, Zucchini P, Romagnoli S
papers.abstract: Basal serum testosterone may help determine reproductive status in tomcats with an uncertain surgical history, but interpretation of a single result is limited by episodic secretion and reduced analytical precision at very low concentrations. We evaluated the analytical performance and diagnostic accuracy of an automated fluorescence enzyme immunoassay (FEIA) in 80 male cats (40 intact and 40 castrated). Within-run and between-day precision and dilutional recovery were assessed using pooled feline serum, and diagnostic performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Testosterone concentrations were significantly higher in intact than castrated cats ( p < 0.001), although overlap occurred at low concentrations. ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.773 (95% CI, 0.665-0.859). The Youden-derived threshold > 0.124 ng/mL had 60.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 43.3-75.1%) and 90.0% specificity (95% CI, 76.3-97.2%). No castrated cat had a concentration > 0.271 ng/mL; this cohort-specific rule-in threshold had 47.5% sensitivity (95% CI, 31.5-63.9%) and 100% observed specificity (95% CI, 91.2-100.0%). Therefore, clearly elevated basal testosterone can support the presence of functional testicular tissue, but concentrations ≤ 0.271 ng/mL cannot exclude intact status. Low or equivocal results require integration with clinical examination and, when indicated, GnRH stimulation and/or anti-Müllerian hormone measurement. Independent validation is required before broad clinical application.

papers.title: Hematologic Responses to Molidustat in Cats with Anemia of Heterogeneous Etiology: A Retrospective Descriptive Study.
papers.authors: Lee G, Lee J, Song KH
papers.abstract: Molidustat, an oral hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, is approved for nonregenerative anemia associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in cats but is also used for anemia of other causes. This retrospective, single-center study described the hematologic response to molidustat in 39 cats with anemia of heterogeneous etiology and identified factors that complicate attribution of improvement to the drug. Response was defined as a hematocrit (HCT) increase of ≥4 percentage points from baseline at the complete blood count closest to day 28 (days 14-45), without transfusion to treat anemia. Molidustat was used outside the approved indication in 33 cats (84.6%). Seventeen cats (43.6%) had a response-window measurement; they had a longer treatment span and differed in etiology and concurrent treatment from non-evaluable cats. Among these 17 cats, 12 (70.6%; 95% CI 46.9-86.7%) met the response criterion; sensitivity analyses specified before formal analysis gave 70.6-75.0% and post hoc attribution analyses 29.4-50.0%. In 7 of the 12 responders, darbepoetin or transfusion preceded the qualifying measurement, or it was obtained more than 7 days after the last dose. These data describe clinical use but do not establish effectiveness outside CKD-associated anemia.

papers.title: Detection of Zoonotic Protozoan Enteropathogens in Stray and Owned Dogs with Diarrhea in Trabzon Province Using Microscopic and Molecular Methods.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic protozoan parasites in dogs represent a significant public health concern because of their ability to infect humans. This study aimed to detect and determine the prevalence of zoonotic protozoan infections, including Balantidium coli , Entamoeba histolytica , Giardia duodenalis , Cryptosporidium spp., Sarcocystis spp. and Cystoisospora spp. in stray and owned dogs with diarrhea in Trabzon Province, Türkiye. Fecal samples were obtained from 450 dogs of various ages, sexes, and breeds. Samples were preserved in 70% alcohol for molecular analysis and incubated in 2.5% potassium dichromate for microscopic examination. Parasite DNA was analyzed using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and identified by restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP). Microscopic examination identified the Cystoisospora ohioensis group, Cystoisospora canis , and Sarcocystis spp. in 56 samples (12.44%). Specifically, Cystoisospora spp. and Sarcocystis spp. were detected in 36 (8.00%) and 20 (4.44%) of the samples, respectively. A mixed infection involving C. canis and the C. ohioensis group was observed in one sample. Molecular analyses detected Cystoisospora spp. DNA in 36 samples (8.00%) and Sarcocystis spp. DNA in 20 samples (4.44%). RFLP analysis confirmed that all detected Cystoisospora spp. DNA belonged to C. ohioensis , while Sarcocystis spp. could not be differentiated at the species level. This study reports the first microscopic detection of Sarcocystis spp. and C. ohioensis in dogs in Trabzon Province and constitutes the first molecular identification of C. ohioensis in Türkiye.

papers.title: MicroRNA Regulation of the Estrogen Receptor Alpha 3'UTR in Canine Mammary Tumor (CMT28) Cells.
papers.authors: Goyal D, Bird RC
papers.abstract: Reduced estrogen receptor alpha (ERα/ ESR1 ) expression is seen in canine mammary tumors, but the mechanisms involved are not fully understood. This study examined ESR1 , miR-18a, and miR-19a expression in canine mammary cell lines. Further CMT28, a canine mammary tumor cell line, was used to test whether these miRNAs can regulate the reporter activity through selected regions of the canine ESR1 3'UTR containing predicted miR-18a and miR-19a binding sites. ESR1 mRNA expression was measured by RT-qPCR, and miR-18a and miR-19a expression was measured using LNA-based assays. ESR1 mRNA expression was much lower in CMT27, CMT28, and CMT47 compared with normal canine mammary epithelial cells, while CMT12 showed higher expression. miR-18a and miR-19a were increased to different levels across the tumor cell lines. Bioinformatic analysis identified predicted miR-18a and miR-19a seed-match sites in the canine ESR1 3'UTR. Luciferase reporter assays showed that both miR-18a and miR-19a significantly reduced activity of the reporter containing selected regions of the 3'UTR of ESR1 encoding predicted miR-18a and miR-19a binding sites. In contrast, neither miRNA significantly reduced activity of the mutant reporter containing deletions in the predicted miR-18a and miR-19a seed-match regions. Anti-miR-18a and anti-miR-19a also significantly increased reporter activity compared with the corresponding miRNA alone. These findings provide functional evidence that miR-18a and miR-19a can regulate reporter activity through selected regions of the canine ESR1 3'UTR. Further studies are needed to determine the role of this regulation in endogenous ESR1 expression and canine mammary tumor biology.

papers.title: Intra-Articular Autologous Conditioned Serum Alone or Combined with Oral Cannabidiol in Dogs Undergoing Tibial Plateau Leveling Osteotomy: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Ardaum P, Kashemsant N, Wibulchan W, Pooliam J, Vijarnsorn M
papers.abstract: Autologous conditioned serum (ACS) contains anti-inflammatory mediators, whereas cannabidiol (CBD) may have analgesic and immunomodulatory effects. This exploratory randomized trial evaluated intra-articular ACS, alone or combined with oral CBD, after tibial plateau leveling osteotomy in dogs. Twenty-seven dogs were randomized to placebo, ACS, or ACS + CBD ( n = 9/group). Outcomes included C-reactive protein (CRP), peak vertical force, orthopedic assessment scores (lameness, joint mobility, pain on palpation, weight-bearing, and overall clinical condition), Canine Brief Pain Inventory, radiographic outcomes, and safety. CRP peaked on Day 1. In the linear mixed model using a heterogeneous first-order autoregressive covariance structure, treatment-group ( p = 0.001) and visit ( p < 0.001) effects were significant, whereas the treatment-group × visit interaction did not reach significance ( p = 0.053). Exploratory comparisons showed lower CRP in ACS + CBD than placebo on Days 3 (adjusted p = 0.007) and 5 (adjusted p = 0.001), with model-dependent sensitivity findings. No consistent treatment-group differences were identified in clinical or structural outcomes. One ACS-treated dog developed a surgical site infection, and alkaline phosphatase activity was higher in ACS + CBD on Day 28. The CRP findings remain hypothesis-generating, with uncertain clinical relevance.

papers.title: Sinonasal aspergillosis-associated pneumocephalus in a dog: recovery after endoscopic interventional debridement and antifungal treatment.
papers.authors: Costes MTA, Saunders JH, Rickerts V, Daminet S, Rösch S
papers.abstract: A 16-year-old Border Collie was referred for acute severe apathy and chronic nasal discharge. Computed tomography (CT) performed 2 weeks earlier was suggestive of sinonasal aspergillosis (SNA) with severe turbinate destruction and mucosal thickening in the left nasal cavity and frontal sinus. No treatment was initiated. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at presentation identified intrameningeal pneumocephalus, meningitis, frontal sinusitis with ventral focal frontal bone lysis of the cranial cavity. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was unremarkable, suggesting pneumocephalus as the cause of apathy. Rhinoscopy confirmed fungal plaque (qPCR: Aspergillus spp.). Systemic antifungal treatment and endoscopic debridement were initiated. Despite frontal bone lysis, topical antifungal treatment also was administered. A 3-week follow-up MRI showed complete resolution of pneumocephalus. Final imaging identified scarring around the defect and no active infection. These findings indicate that intrameningeal pneumocephalus secondary to SNA can be reversible and should not preclude antifungal treatment. Endoscopic therapeutic intervention may enable full recovery.

papers.title: Prophylactic strategies to reduce cyclophosphamide-induced sterile hemorrhagic cystitis in dogs: a first-opinion practice retrospective study and a referral survey.
papers.authors: Ivanovs A, MacKenzie C, Wardle Z, Pinchbeck G, Grieve H, Noble PJ, Killick DR
papers.abstract: Cyclophosphamide occasionally causes sterile hemorrhagic cystitis (SHC) in dogs. Prophylactic coadministration of furosemide reduces SHC risk, yet the extent of the implementation in practice is unknown. To explore the frequency of cyclophosphamide and furosemide coadministration in first opinion practice (FOP) and referral settings. Small Animal Surveillance Network (SAVSNET) searches identified 106 dogs receiving cyclophosphamide, of which 72 met the inclusion criteria. This study was composed of: (1) electronic health record (EHR) review using the SAVSNET database, in which data regarding dosage, co-prescribed medications, preventative measures, and suspected SHC occurrence were collated (2014-2024); and (2) a survey of referral oncology practitioners and educators (2023-2024) exploring contemporary approaches to SHC prevention. Treatment approaches were evenly divided between maximum-tolerated dose cyclophosphamide (MTDC, 53%) and metronomic cyclophosphamide (MC, 47%). Furosemide was prescribed in 32% of cases, most commonly with MTDC protocols (53%). The overall frequency of suspected SHC was 15% (11/72); notably, no suspected SHC cases occurred in dogs receiving furosemide (P = .013). Survey results showed frequent use of prophylactic diuretics: 88% recommended furosemide for MTDC and 55% for MC protocols. Diuretic co-prescription with cyclophosphamide was inconsistent in FOP, which was unexpected given the prior evidence regarding reduction of risk of SHC. Greater standardization of guidance and improved dissemination of best-practice recommendations are necessary to optimize dog safety. Cyclophosphamide is a chemotherapy drug used to treat dogs with cancer. It can occasionally cause inflammation and bleeding in the bladder. Furosemide, a drug that increases urine production, can be given alongside cyclophosphamide to reduce this risk. This study investigated how often furosemide and other preventative measures were used in dogs receiving cyclophosphamide in general veterinary practice. Veterinary specialists and educators were also surveyed about their prevention practices, recommendations to general veterinary practitioners, and veterinary student teaching. Furosemide was used inconsistently in general veterinary practice, whereas specialists more commonly recommended its use. No suspected cases of bladder inflammation and bleeding occurred in dogs receiving furosemide, although the study had limitations that should be considered when interpreting this finding. More consistent guidance on preventative measures might improve the safety of dogs receiving cyclophosphamide.

papers.title: An observational retrospective study of online owner perceptions of diet-related health signs in dogs using social media listening.
papers.authors: Kaur JP, Hollands T, Clarke C, Tarrant G, Rai T, Street T, Wells K, Armstrong SK
papers.abstract: Dog owners increasingly link health to diet type, and the pet food market has diversified beyond kibble/canned diets (KC) to raw and fresh diets (FD; human-grade, gently/mildly cooked, and home-cooked). However, it remains unclear which owner-reported health-related signs (ORHS) are associated with dietary changes, including KC-FD transitions. Social media listening (SML) enables large-scale capture of naturally-occurring online owner discussions. Investigate owner perceptions of diet-related ORHS in dogs within online discourse using SML. None. Observational, retrospective study of 21 896 KC and 2336 FD online posts (>96% from Reddit) collected using Pulsar Platform™ (January 1, 2025 to July 3, 2025). After preprocessing and large language model (LLM)-based zero-shot filtering, 8040 KC and 924 FD posts were analyzed using LLM-assisted topic modeling and dictionary-based ORHS quantification. Topic modeling identified recurrent themes across KC (number of topics [k] = 7, coherence score [Cv] = 0.58) and FD (k = 6, Cv = 0.44) posts. Owners discussed diet as both the perceived cause and management strategy for gastrointestinal (GI), dermatologic, allergy/intolerance, appetite, and body condition ORHS, alongside decision uncertainties. Gastrointestinal (2286/8040, 28.4%; 282/924, 30.5%) and allergy/intolerance (1932/8040, 24.0%; 194/924, 21.0%) ORHS predominated within KC and FD posts, respectively; allergy/intolerance co-occurred with skin/coat (478/918, 52.1%; 57/114, 50.0%), and GI with allergy/intolerance (476/1,932, 24.6%; 68/194, 35.1%). Our study demonstrates the feasibility of SML-LLM-assisted analysis for capturing diet-related ORHS in online dog owner discourse. The study captured owner perceptions rather than clinically verified outcomes, highlighting the need for future studies to align ORHS with clinically validated endpoints to support veterinary nutrition discussions and informed owner decision-making.

papers.title: Effects of transcription units and a specific hexanucleotide motif of porcine circovirus-like virus P1 on viral DNA synthesis, viral protein expression, and progeny virus production.
papers.authors: Song J, Li Z, Li N, Xie J, Zhu H, Lai H, Xiang Z, Zhong Y, Sun H, He K, Suolang S, Wen L, Xiao Q
papers.abstract: Porcine circovirus-like virus P1 has a broad host range and is known to cause post-weaning multisystemic wasting syndrome in pigs, as well as infect and propagate in cattle, goats, dogs, cats, yaks, and rabbits. To investigate the functional importance of its eight open reading frames (ORFs) and the conserved hexanucleotide motif (GGATCC), we generated a panel of site-directed mutants based on the P1 infectious clone rpSK-2P1. These mutants were transfected into PK-15 cells and serially passaged four times. Viral replication capacity and genetic stability were assessed using polymerase chain reaction (PCR), quantitative PCR, and Sanger sequencing. All the mutant viruses retained the ability to replicate their genomes and transcribe viral RNA. However, sequencing of viral genomes recovered at the fourth passage revealed selective reversion at multiple mutated sites, indicating a strong replicative advantage conferred by wild-type sequences during sustained propagation. Notably, mutant Y1, which harbored a mutation in ORF1 that encoded the capsid protein (Cap), initially exhibited reduced replication but rapidly reverted upon passaging, restoring Cap expression and fitness. These findings demonstrate that although these ORFs and nucleotide sites do not abolish P1 replication, their native sequences play pivotal roles in modulating replication efficiency and maintaining genetic stability, thereby providing key insights into the molecular mechanisms governing P1 replication. Thus, P1 tolerates limited genetic change but is under intense pressure to maintain its wild-type sequence, offering critical insight into the replication strategy and evolutionary constraints of this compact, broad-host-range DNA virus.

papers.title: Efficacy and tolerability of a sequential COP and doxorubicin chemotherapy protocol for treatment of high-grade lymphoma in cats.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Neiderfer K, Iwaki Y, Donnelly LL, Bryant JE, Bryan JN, Henry CJ
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate tolerability of a COP/DOX protocol, where cats received COP (vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and prednisolone) induction weekly for 6 weeks followed by doxorubicin (DOX) consolidation every 3 weeks for six doses. A secondary objective was to evaluate the efficacy of the COP/DOX protocol in this cohort of cats. Records were retrospectively reviewed for cats with high-grade lymphoma treated with the COP/DOX protocol between 2005 and 2024. Data collected included signalment, method of diagnosis, tumor location, staging, baseline diagnostics, drug dosages, adverse events, restaging diagnostics, and treatment response. Progression-free survival and survival time were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared across selected variables using log-rank test. In total, 27 cats met the inclusion criteria. Gastrointestinal lymphoma was the most common form, occurring in 33.3% of cats. The number of cats achieving a maximal response of clinical remission and partial remission throughout COP was 10 (37.0%) and 12 (44.4%), respectively. Of the five cats who had stable disease or progressive disease during COP, one achieved partial remission on DOX. Four cats (14.8%) did not respond to either the COP or DOX part of the protocol. The overall response rate at 6 weeks after initiation of COP/DOX was 77.7%. Median progression-free survival was 98 days (interquartile range 41-141) and median survival time was 154 days (interquartile range 102-546). The cats who had clinical remission at the completion of DOX had progression-free survival of 554.5 days and median survival time of 546 days. High-grade adverse events included grade 3 and 4 neutropenia (n = 3 for each) during COP. Lymphocyte:monocyte ratio and response at the completion of DOX were significantly associated with progression-free survival and median survival time. We conclude that the COP/DOX protocol was well tolerated by this population. Progression-free survival and median survival time were similar to previous reports. The COP/DOX protocol is an effective treatment approach for cats with lymphoma. Effectiveness and side effects of a sequential COP and doxorubicin chemotherapy plan for cats with aggressive lymphoma This study looked at how well cats with aggressive lymphoma tolerated and responded to a chemotherapy protocol that combined two types of treatment: COP and doxorubicin. The COP part used three drugs (vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and prednisolone) given weekly for 6 weeks. After that, cats received doxorubicin every 3 weeks for up to six treatments. Records from 27 cats treated between 2005 and 2024 were reviewed. Most commonly, lymphoma started in the intestines. After the first part of the treatment (COP), 37% of cats went into full remission, meaning no signs of cancer could be found, and 44% had their cancer shrink. Among cats who improved but did not reach full remission after COP, three later reached full remission after adding doxorubicin. Only four cats did not respond to either treatment. Overall, about 85% of the cats had some level of improvement. On average, disease progression occurred at approximately 3 months (98 days), and cats survived for about 5 months (154 days) after the initiation of treatment. Cats whose cancer went fully into remission after the full treatment lived much longer, around 1.5 years. The treatment was generally well tolerated. Some cats had temporary drops in white blood cell counts, but serious side effects were uncommon. In summary, this combined COP and doxorubicin treatment was safe and effective for many cats with aggressive lymphoma, offering similar outcomes to other chemotherapy options reported in previous studies.

papers.title: Comparative Effectiveness of COP and CHOP Chemotherapy Protocols in Feline Intermediate- to Large-Cell Lymphoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Lam YWS, Pimentel PAB, Nekouei O, Giuliano A
papers.abstract: Feline intermediate- to large-cell lymphoma is commonly treated with COP or CHOP chemotherapy, but the clinical benefit of adding doxorubicin (CHOP) remains controversial given its associated toxicity profile and cost. This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis summarized response and survival outcomes reported for COP- and CHOP-based protocols in feline intermediate- to large-cell lymphoma. Searching PubMed, Scopus, and CAB Abstracts (2000-2024), we included 21 studies comprising 1054 cats. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis utilizing Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) estimation was conducted to evaluate overall (ORR), complete (CR), and partial response (PR) rates. The overall pooled ORR was 81.0%. Subgroup meta-regression revealed no statistically significant differences between COP and CHOP for ORR (83.0% vs. 77.0%, p = 0.360), CR (57.0% vs. 49.0%, p = 0.350), or PR (28.0% vs. 22.0%, p = 0.468). Profound heterogeneity (overall I 2  = 85.4%-89.6%) persisted across all analyses, driven primarily by the pooling of diverse anatomical subtypes and uncontrolled confounding by Feline Leukaemia Virus (FeLV) status. Furthermore, inadequate variance reporting and a widespread lack of standardized response criteria (e.g., VCOG-RECIST) precluded a formal meta-analysis of survival outcomes. Descriptively, reported median survival times ranged broadly (COP: 108-610 days; CHOP: 62-973 days) without a clear advantage for CHOP. A custom weighted risk-of-bias assessment highlighted significant methodological deficiencies across the literature. In conclusion, current aggregate evidence does not demonstrate a statistically detectable difference in response rates between CHOP- and COP-based protocols. Severe methodological heterogeneity and retrospective selection bias prevent definitive conclusions regarding long-term survival, emphasizing the critical need for homogeneous, prospective randomized trials utilizing standardized reporting guidelines.

papers.title: Differences in DNA Methylation Status Between Epithelial and Mesenchymal Phenotypes in Canine Malignant Mucosal Melanoma.
papers.authors: Ishizaki T, Yamazaki J, Aoshima K, Kimura T
papers.abstract: Canine malignant mucosal melanoma is one of the common cancers with a high mortality rate. Pathologically, malignant melanomas show multiple morphological patterns including epithelioid, spindle and round, indicating that neoplastic cells change their morphology. Regarding morphological change, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) has been considered to be an important mechanism. EMT is a reversible biologic process being suggested the correlation with DNA methylation in human cancer. The aim of this study was to assess the difference in DNA methylation status between epithelial and mesenchymal phenotypes and correlation with EMT in canine oral malignant melanoma. Sixteen samples were classified into epithelial phenotype and eight samples were classified into mesenchymal phenotype based on E-cadherin expression using immunohistochemistry or western blotting. We analysed DNA methylation level of 46 673 cytosine-guanine dinucleotides (CpG sites) in all samples and compared average DNA methylation level between epithelial and mesenchymal phenotypes. In a comparison of average DNA methylation level at each site in CpG island promoters (3089 sites), 17 and 6 hypermethylated sites were identified in epithelial phenotype and mesenchymal phenotype, respectively. Finally, 10 out of 23 sites showed de novo hypermethylation, and two genes, NEUROG1 and ITGAV, which are associated with cell adhesion, were found to be hypermethylated in epithelial phenotype. This study revealed the difference of DNA methylation status between epithelial and mesenchymal phenotypes suggesting the influence of DNA methylation on EMT in canine malignant mucosal melanoma.

papers.title: Factors associated with antimicrobial drug prescription in cats receiving outpatient care at a veterinary teaching hospital.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Thane K, Kwong M, DeStefano I, Sweigart B, Beaulac K, Doron S, Fellman CL
papers.abstract: ObjectivesInvestigations of factors associated with antimicrobial drug prescription(s) (ADP) in cats receiving outpatient care are lacking, which limits antimicrobial stewardship efforts and benchmarking of veterinary antimicrobial use. This study aimed to identify factors associated with ADP in cats receiving outpatient care at a veterinary teaching hospital.MethodsA retrospective analysis of electronic medical record data from cats receiving outpatient care at a veterinary teaching hospital in 2022 was performed. Subjects included 2245 cats with 3973 outpatient visits. The primary study outcome was receipt of at least one systemic ADP during or immediately after an outpatient visit; an exploratory outcome was receipt of a 'Watch' or 'Reserve' (WR) ADP using the World Health Organization (WHO) Access-Watch-Reserve (AWaRe) classification adapted to include veterinary agents. Independent variables, including patient demographics, hospital service and owner sociodemographic factors, were identified for model fitting using univariable logistic regression; multivariable models were built using generalized estimating equations.ResultsOf outpatient visit records, 367/3973 (9.2%) were associated with one or more ADP. Factors significantly associated with receipt of ADP included patient sex, hospital service visited, veterinarian training status, visit duration and urine culture performed. Among patients receiving any antimicrobial drugs, factors associated with receipt of WHO-WR ADP included hospital service, visit date, receipt of more than one ADP and history of a visit to any hospital service within the prior month.Conclusions and relevanceThese findings expand our understanding of antimicrobial usage in cats. This knowledge of identifying factors associated with antimicrobial use can be used to refine local prescribing practices and supports the development of veterinary and One Health antimicrobial stewardship initiatives and veterinary antimicrobial use benchmarking metrics. A study of health record data in cats receiving outpatient veterinary care that evaluates whether measurable characteristics related to the patients, pet owners and hospital are associated with higher or lower odds of receiving an antimicrobial drug during the veterinary care visit Pet cats receive routine veterinary care, which sometimes includes receiving antimicrobial prescriptions (sometimes referred to as antibiotics) to treat bacterial infections. The use of antibiotics can be necessary to treat bacterial infections in pets. However, when antibiotics are not used appropriately, it can cause problems for the pets receiving treatment and can reduce how well those antibiotics work in the future to effectively treat disease in humans and animals. The amount of information about cats receiving antibiotics is very limited. Knowing more about how antibiotics are used in cats will help veterinarians improve treatment options for patients and will provide important information about how antibiotics are used in the hospital setting. We studied the medical records of cats who received outpatient care (day appointments, in which the patient did not need to be admitted to the hospital for additional care) and analyzed information that is routinely collected in the medical record to try to identify patterns associated with which feline outpatients had higher odds of receiving antibiotics. In our study population, approximately 9% of cats receiving outpatient care received an antibiotic. We found that patient sex, hospital service visited, training status of the care provider, how long the visit took and whether a urine culture was performed all significantly affected the odds of a patient receiving an antibiotic. We also identified some factors associated with higher odds of receiving an antibiotic with greater importance to human healthcare. These findings help us better understand how antibiotics are used in cats receiving outpatient veterinary care and help researchers and hospital teams develop ways to monitor and optimize ongoing antibiotic use in cats.

papers.title: Prospective evaluation of the prevalence and characteristics of heart murmurs and gallop sounds in anemic cats.
papers.authors: Robertson A, Boswood A, Luis Fuentes V, Lo EJY, Humm K
papers.abstract: Heart murmurs and gallop sounds are common in anemic cats; however, their association with underlying cardiac disease is unclear. Determine the prevalence of murmurs and gallops in anemic cats. Investigate the association of auscultatory abnormalities with anemia severity and heart disease. Investigate whether change in anemia severity affects the audibility of murmurs and gallop sounds. Sixty-four anemic cats (packed cell volume [PCV] below 30%) presenting to a referral hospital. Single-center prospective observational study. On presentation, cats were examined and had PCV measurement. Each cat underwent echocardiography. Cats had PCV checks and daily auscultation to document heart sounds. Fifty-eight percent (37/64) had a murmur and 23% (15/64) had a gallop. Mean PCV at enrollment was 18% (±6). Lower PCV was associated with the presence of a murmur (P = .03) and gallop (P = .016). Cardiac disease was present in 34% (22/64) of cats. After adjusting for anemia severity, murmur presence showed no statistically significant association with cardiac disease (P = .636 (OR: 1.31, 95% CI, 0.43-3.95)). A gallop sound was associated with greater odds of cardiac disease (P = .037 (OR: 3.97, 95% CI, 1.09-14.5)). Murmur intensity (P = .001) and likelihood of a gallop sound (P = .022) were lower in individuals when their PCVs increased. Murmurs and gallop sounds are common in anemic cats with and without cardiac disease. Anemic cats with gallops are more likely to have underlying cardiac disease than anemic cats without gallops. Abnormal heart sounds, known as heart murmurs and gallop sounds, can occur frequently in cats with a low red blood cell count (anemia). Murmurs and gallops are also common in cats with heart disease. Whether the abnormal heart sounds are due to anemia or if anemic cats have underlying heart disease causing the murmur or gallop is unknown. This study aimed to determine how many anemic cats had abnormal heart sounds, if murmurs or gallops were associated with heart disease or red blood cell count, and if change in red blood cell count over time affected the presence of abnormal heart sounds. In this study abnormal heart sounds were common in anemic cats. Lower red blood cell count was associated with having a murmur or gallop. Heart disease was frequently present in our cats. Having a heart murmur was not associated with having heart disease, but a gallop sound was associated with having heart disease. When individual cats’ red blood cell count increased, the severity of their heart murmur and likelihood of a gallop sound were lower.

papers.title: Clinical reasoning in canine meningoencephalitis of unknown origin and glioma: the role of signalment, history and neurological examination.
papers.authors: Spohn F, Abani S, Dickinson PJ, Vernau KM, Toedebusch CM, Woolard KD, Beineke A, Volk HA, Nessler JN
papers.abstract: Meningoencephalitis of unknown origin (MUO) is a group of presumed immune-mediated inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system (CNS) in dogs. Differentiating MUO from intracranial diseases such as glioma can be challenging based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis. Because glioma represents an important differential diagnosis in dogs clinically suspected to have MUO, distinguishing these diseases is relevant for diagnostic reasoning, therapeutic planning, and owner communication. This study assessed whether readily available clinical variables contribute to clinical reasoning in dogs with histopathologically confirmed MUO or glioma. This retrospective multicenter study included 138 dogs with histopathologically confirmed MUO or glioma. Medical history, signalment, and neurological examination findings were compared between groups. Binary logistic regression was used to identify clinical variables associated with diagnosis. Seventy dogs were diagnosed with MUO and 68 dogs with glioma. Dogs with MUO had a lower median body weight (10.50 kg vs. 23.90 kg; p = 0.0007) and age (5.00 years vs. 7.04 years; p = 0.0007) than dogs with glioma. In the final multivariable model, disease onset was associated with the distinction between MUO and glioma ( p = 0.0282), while lower body weight and head tilt were associated with MUO. Increasing body weight was associated with lower odds of MUO (OR: 0.910; 95% CI: 0.861 - 0.961; p = 0.0007). Dogs without head tilt were less likely to be diagnosed with MUO than dogs with head tilt (OR: 0.249; 95% CI: 0.062 - 0.998; p = 0.0497). An exploratory, cohort specific body weight cut-off of ≤ 7.70 kg yielded 40.6% sensitivity and 95.6% specificity for MUO. Readily available clinical variables may provide supportive information when MUO and glioma are differential diagnoses, particularly when MRI and CSF findings are equivocal. However, overlap between groups and limited discriminatory performance of individual variables indicate that these findings should not be used as standalone criteria. Instead, signalment, history, and neurological examination findings should be interpreted as part of an integrated assessment together with MRI, CSF analysis, and infectious testing.

papers.title: Case Report: Surgical treatment of feline pituitary apoplexy in 3 cases.
papers.authors: van Schaik MA, van Stee LL, Grinwis GCM, Meij BP
papers.abstract: Surgical treatment of feline pituitary apoplexy has not been previously described. To describe the clinical course and follow-up of 3 cases of feline pituitary apoplexy. Cases were selected based on histopathological confirmation of pituitary masses with haemorrhagic lesions, following transsphenoidal hypophysectomy. Details of physical examination, diagnostic test results, treatment and follow-up course were retrospectively acquired by review of medical and imaging records. Two cats were presented with acute onset of neurologic signs (case 1 and 2), and one cat showed subacute endocrinological dysfunction (case 3). All cases underwent successful transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, followed by intensive care hospitalization and successful discharge. Pituitary apoplexy was identified by histopathological examination of the excised pituitary glands in cases 1, 2, and 3. Imaging findings compatible with pituitary apoplexy were present in all 3 cases, although only case 3 was imaged with a hemorrhage-sensitive sequence, providing unequivocal evidence of intralesional hemorrhage. Case 1 had a survival time at least 716 days, underwent a second transsphenoidal surgery because of tumor recurrence and was subsequently lost to follow-up. Case 2 had a survival time of at least 1,098 days and is still alive at the time of writing this manuscript. In case 3, tumor recurrence was identified radiologically (MRI) at 365 days, and it died during a course of radiation therapy 612 days after transsphenoidal hypophysectomy. Pituitary apoplexy is a rare condition that also affects cats with large pituitary adenomas. Overall, the cats experienced acceptable clinical recovery and postoperative survival, supporting the feasibility of transsphenoidal hypophysectomy as a therapeutic option for cats with pituitary tumors affected by apoplexy. Notably, a favorable outcome was observed even in the presence of remnant pituitary tissue, as illustrated by the cat that later developed pituitary tumor recurrence.

papers.title: Short-course letrozole restores fertility in aged azoospermic dogs.
papers.authors: Liu B, Zhang L, Zhu F, Jin X, Liu T
papers.abstract: Age-related azoospermia is a clinically important cause of male infertility in dogs, yet effective pharmacological treatments for aged males remain limited. Whether transient aromatase inhibition can restore fertility in aged azoospermic dogs without prolonged exposure is unclear. This study evaluated whether a 1-week course of letrozole, an aromatase inhibitor, could restore spermatogenesis and fertility in aged azoospermic male dogs. Untreated aged azoospermic and young fertile dogs served as comparison groups, and a separate cohort of five aged dogs received 3 months of letrozole for safety assessment. Serum testosterone, semen parameters, testicular histology, fertilization-related transcripts, spermatogonia, seminal plasma metabolites, and serum biochemical markers of liver, kidney, and bone metabolism were assessed before and after treatment over a 6-month follow-up. Serum testosterone increased within 1 week and peaked at approximately 2 weeks. Spermatozoa reappeared in ejaculates approximately 3 months after treatment and persisted for more than 6 months; treated males subsequently achieved pregnancies with healthy offspring, although litter size remained smaller than that of young fertile dogs. Compared with 3-month administration, 1-week treatment was not associated with detectable changes in serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP). These findings indicate that a 1-week letrozole course can restore spermatogenesis and fertility in aged azoospermic dogs, supporting its further evaluation as a low-exposure therapeutic strategy; larger, breed-stratified studies with extended safety profiling are recommended before clinical adoption.

papers.title: Fluid balance, electrolyte, and neurohormonal responses to isotonic vs. hypotonic maintenance crystalloids in healthy Beagle dogs.
papers.authors: Her J, Gordon D, Kim K, Wallinger J, Langston C
papers.abstract: To compare the effects of isotonic vs. hypotonic maintenance crystalloid therapy on fluid balance, urine output, and electrolyte homeostasis in healthy Beagles. In this 2-phase clinical study, nine healthy Beagles received intravenous isotonic (lactated Ringer's solution with 5% dextrose plus 26 mEq/L KCl) and hypotonic (Normosol-M and 5% dextrose plus 17 mEq/L KCl) crystalloids at an allometric maintenance rate for 48 h, with a 10-day washout between treatments from July 3 to September 29, 2021. Variables of interests were assessed every 12 h during treatment, and results were analyzed with baseline-adjusted linear mixed-effects models. A p -value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Timepoint-specific comparisons were exploratory and unadjusted for multiplicity. In exploratory timepoint-specific analyses, calculated fluid balance was greater with isotonic crystalloids only at T36 [estimated marginal mean (EMM) difference, 356 ml (95% CI, 105-606)]. The overall treatment-by-time interaction for calculated fluid balance was not significant. Urine output did not differ, whereas cumulative urine output was higher with isotonic crystalloids only at T12 (back-transformed EMMs, 125.3 ml for isotonic vs. 81.2 ml for hypotonic). Isotonic crystalloids were associated with significantly higher urinary sodium and chloride at all time points than hypotonic crystalloids. Serum sodium was lower with hypotonic fluids at T24. Individual concentrations fell modestly below the lower reference limit during both phases, with a lowest recorded value of 137 mEq/L and a maximum interval-averaged rate of decline of 0.58 mEq/L/h, and recovered toward baseline by T48. In this exploratory study, isotonic maintenance crystalloids were associated with a transient, relatively more positive calculated fluid balance and consistently greater urinary sodium and chloride excretion than hypotonic crystalloids. In healthy Beagles, the two maintenance crystalloid formulations produced distinct patterns of renal sodium, chloride, and electrolyte-free water handling, while the hypotonic crystalloid did not cause a rapid or clinically important decline in serum sodium.

papers.title: A proposed framework for practical multimodal management of osteoarthritis in adult dogs.
papers.authors: Marcellin-Little DJ, Huntingford J, Grubb T, Pechette Markley A, Brunke MW, Hulse DA, Frank B
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) affects nearly half of adult dogs and has physiological, physical, and functional consequences. The physiological impact of OA includes joint inflammation, progressive cartilage degeneration, and pain. Physically, OA changes commonly result in reduced limb strength, muscle atrophy, and, in some cases, decreased joint range of motion. Functionally, OA manifests as diminished willingness or ability to climb stairs, jump, play, exercise, or perform routine activities. These functional losses negatively impact quality of life for both dogs and their caregivers. Effective OA management requires a comprehensive and multimodal approach. Therapeutic options include nutrition, nutritional supplementation, medications, lifestyle changes, electrophysical modalities, manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, ergonomic support, and surgery. Because OA is a chronic and progressive condition, management strategies must be practical, individualized, and sustainable over the long term. Protocols should be streamlined to minimize caregiver burden while maximizing clinical benefit. Foundational management includes nutritional strategies to optimize metabolic health and maintain ideal body condition. Nutritional supplements may provide safe and practical adjunctive support to decrease joint inflammation and pain. When joint pain is identified, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs remain a predictably effective first-line pharmacologic therapy. Additional or alternative therapeutic interventions should be added when initial therapy is inadequate or when safety considerations limit use. Sustained and structured client communication is critical to setting expectations, monitoring response to therapy, and adapting management plans over time. Successful OA management depends not only on therapeutic selection but also on long-term adherence, reassessment, and individualized adjustment. A consensus-driven, multimodal framework provides clinicians with a practical and sustainable strategy to optimize outcomes for adult dogs with OA.

papers.title: Canine atopic dermatitis clinical trials: study design and methodological considerations.
papers.authors: Klotsman M, Sagiv SK, Anderson WH, Santoro D
papers.abstract: Canine atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory and pruritic skin disease affecting up to 15% of dogs, with clinical expression shaped by genetic, environmental, and microbial factors. Although the International Committee for Allergic Diseases of Animals (ICADA) established COSCAD as a core outcome set providing standardized outcome measures for evaluating treatment efficacy, comparatively little attention has been given to the upstream methodological considerations that determine the validity and interpretability of trial results. This narrative review uses a structured methodological framework to examine key sources of random error, bias, confounding, and effect modification that can compromise randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in canine AD. We identify critical parameters requiring careful control in trial design, including food and environmental allergen exposures, seasonality, flea infestation, concurrent bacterial and fungal infections, concomitant therapies, and washout period determination. Historical study protocols, conducted primarily in treatment-naïve dogs with mild-to-moderate disease, are analyzed to illustrate how pivotal registration trials mitigated these sources of error through strict case definitions, medication-specific washout intervals, concomitant therapy restrictions, and rigorous blinding and randomization. We further examine the trade-offs between internal validity and external generalizability, and the growing tension between traditional explanatory trial designs and real-world feasibility in an evolving therapeutic landscape. Synthesizing perspectives from a panel of veterinary dermatology experts, we highlight how disease severity, treatment history, and therapeutic modality should inform eligibility criteria, endpoint selection, and assessment timing. Based on these assessments, we highlight the limitations of applying standardized study design methodologies to such a heterogeneous disease. Applying uniform methodologies to such a heterogeneous syndrome risks obscuring clinically meaningful differences in disease presentation and treatment response. Progress requires flexible, fit-for-purpose study designs that align key methodological elements with the phenotype under investigation, enabling accurate interpretation of treatment effects and more effective therapeutic development.

papers.title: Hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension under isoflurane anesthesia.
papers.authors: Seki D, Kusu H, Fujimoto T, Kitagawa H, Goya S, Yamaya Y, Teshima K
papers.abstract: While dopamine and dobutamine are widely used in anesthetized dogs, clinical evidence supporting their use remains limited. We aimed to compare the hemodynamic responses to clinical dosages of dopamine and dobutamine in dogs with hypotension undergoing elective orthopedic surgery under fentanyl-isoflurane anesthesia. The pressor effects at clinical dosages (2-8 µg/kg/min) of dopamine (n = 15) and dobutamine (n = 15) for hypotension were compared and confirmed using the ramped-rate infusion protocol in 30 dogs. The following hemodynamic parameters measured by invasive arterial blood pressure and transesophageal echocardiographic monitoring were analyzed: heart rate (HR), systolic (SAP), mean (MAP), diastolic arterial pressure (DAP), stroke volume index (SVI), cardiac index (CI), and systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI). The proportion of dogs that achieved the treatment goal (MAP: 70-89 mmHg) was 93% (dopamine responders, 14/15 dogs) in the dopamine group and 53% (dobutamine responders, 8/15 dogs) in the dobutamine group, with a significantly higher probability in the dopamine group (P = 0.035, a risk difference of 40% [95% confidence interval: 8.2-63.9%]). In dopamine responders, significant increases were observed in SAP, MAP, DAP, SVI and CI, whereas no significant changes were observed in HR and SVRI. In conclusion, the pressor effect was more likely to be observed at the clinical dosage of dopamine than that of dobutamine for treating hypotension in isoflurane anesthetized dogs. This study was approved by the Nihon University Animal Medical Center Research and Trial Ethics Committee (approval number: 1-007; approval date: September 29, 2022).

papers.title: Demographic and environmental factors associated with canine cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma development in Australia: a retrospective matched case-control analysis.
papers.authors: Zhang JJ, Dejene H, Granados-Soler JL, Henning J, Allavena R
papers.abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is a common canine skin tumour that occurs more frequently in high ultraviolet (UV) environments. Despite Australia's consistently high UV exposure, large-scale epidemiological studies on canine cSCC are limited. This study investigates the frequency of canine cSCC in Australia, its geographic patterns relative to UV index, and its association with animal-level risk factors. A matched case-control study was conducted using records from the VetCompass database from 1st January 2014 to 31st December 2023. In total, 295 histopathologically confirmed cSCC cases and 1,180 matched controls were included. Frequency statistics of cSCC and animal-level risk factors associated with cSCC were analysed and spatial patterns were mapped. The highest proportions of cases were recorded in Queensland (39.7%) and New South Wales (39.3%), with increased frequency along coastal areas of both states. cSCC cases occurred most frequently on body regions caudal to the thorax (54.9%), in senior dogs (58.6%), in desexed males (45.1%), and in dogs with white mixed coat colour (43.7%). In the final multivariable model, senior (seven to 11 years old) and geriatric (12 + years old) dogs had significantly higher odds of cSCC than mature (two to six years old) dogs (odds ratio = 7.4 and 4.8, respectively; p ≤ 0.001). Risk was also markedly elevated in Dalmatians, bulldogs, Staffordshire terriers, and schnauzers compared with mixed breeds. Dogs with white or white mixed coats had higher odds of cSCC than dark-coated dogs (p ≤ 0.001). cSCC demonstrated anatomical and geographic patterns consistent with chronic UV exposure, with age, breed, and coat pigmentation emerging as risk factors.

papers.title: Histomorphometric characterization of cardiac nodes in cattle, ponies, and cats.
papers.authors: Gómez-Torres F, Ballesteros-Acuña L, Ruíz-Saurí A
papers.abstract: The sinoatrial node (SAN) and atrioventricular node (AVN) are essential components of the cardiac conduction system and play a critical role in initiating and propagating the electrical impulse. To characterize these cardiac nodes across different species, we examined the hearts of ten cattle, ten cats, and five male ponies without evidence of cardiac disease using conventional histological and immunohistochemical techniques. Morphometric parameters of the nodes and their constituent cells were quantified at different magnifications. The SAN displayed an oval morphology in all species. Its diameter was 888.58 ± 6.36 μm in cats, 2143.17 ± 199.13 μm in ponies, and 2033.28 ± 939.44 μm in cattle. Mean nodal density was significantly higher in ponies than in cattle (p = 0.011). Pacemaker (P) cells of the AVN were significantly larger in ungulate species than in cats (p < 0.001). Heart bone (os cordis) was identified in all ten cattle hearts and in one cat heart, showing typical features of compact bone and bone marrow. Cartilaginous metaplasia was observed in all pony hearts and in 60% of cat hearts and was associated with reduced AVN size and cellularity in cats. These findings highlight important interspecies differences and contribute to the understanding of conduction system pathology in veterinary cardiology. The structural changes in the cardiac nodes in these species warrant more in-depth functional research, given the lack of functional cardiac assessment and the small sample size.

papers.title: Echocardiographic description of pulmonary vein stenosis in a cat with atrioventricular septal defect.
papers.authors: Seyednejad F, Locquet L, Ardehali P, Astaraki N
papers.abstract: A 2.5-year-old, intact female British Shorthair cat was referred for cardiology evaluation owing to intermittent panting and a heart murmur identified on cardiac auscultation before elective surgery. Physical examination revealed a left parasternal grade II/VI systolic murmur without arrhythmia. Thoracic radiographs showed cardiomegaly without pulmonary infiltration. The echocardiography was prompted by auscultation, history and radiological findings. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated marked right atrial enlargement and eccentric hypertrophy of the right ventricle. Echocardiography revealed a partial atrioventricular septal defect characterised by a large ostium primum defect (0.79 cm) and an anterior mitral valve cleft, resulting in a left-to-right shunt (estimated Qp:Qs ≈ 2.2). Doppler interrogation of the left pulmonary vein entering the lateral wall of the left atrium demonstrated focal turbulence and increased peak velocity (1.08 m/s), corresponding to a pressure gradient of approximately 4.7 mmHg, findings consistent with suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. Tricuspid regurgitation velocity (2.2 m/s) did not reflect increased afterload. Elective surgery was postponed owing to uncertainty regarding peri-anaesthetic haemodynamic risk. Medical treatment with enalapril and clopidogrel was initiated. At the 9-month follow-up, the cat remained clinically stable and echocardiographic findings were unchanged. Pulmonary vein stenosis is rarely reported in cats. This report describes the concurrent presence of partial atrioventricular septal defect and suspected unilateral pulmonary vein stenosis. These findings highlight the detection of a congenital heart defect in a young cat, despite the low-grade murmur. A rare congenital heart condition in a British Shorthair cat A 2.5-year-old, female British Shorthair cat was referred for a heart check after intermittent panting and a heart murmur were noticed before planned elective surgery. Examination confirmed a mild heart murmur and chest radiography showed an enlarged heart. Heart ultrasound revealed a congenital heart defect called a partial atrioventricular septal defect. This means there was an abnormal opening between the upper chambers of the heart, together with an abnormality of the mitral valve. These changes caused increased blood flow from the left side of the heart to the right side, leading to enlargement of the right side of the heart. The ultrasound also showed abnormal blood flow in one of the pulmonary veins, raising suspicion of narrowing of that vein. Because of the heart findings and possible anaesthetic risk, the planned surgery was postponed. The cat was started on medical treatment and remained stable after 9 months, with no worsening of the heart ultrasound findings. This case is important because pulmonary vein stenosis is rarely reported in cats, especially alongside this type of congenital heart disease. It also shows that even a mild heart murmur in a young cat can be associated with significant underlying heart abnormalities.

papers.title: Development and Validation of a New Online Tool for Monitoring Clinical Signs of Canine Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.authors: Harvey N, Watson A, Laxalde J, England G, Gow D
papers.abstract: The aim of the study was to develop a simple, reliable and validated patient-reported outcome tool for use in monitoring the severity of clinical signs in dogs with confirmed or suspected atopic allergies and recurrent otitis externa. The tool is called the Dog-Orientated Severity of Atopy Scale (DOSAS). The human Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure (POEM) was adapted for relevance to the owner-observable clinical signs of canine atopic dermatitis (cAD). Refinements were made via consultation with dog owners and veterinary surgeons to ensure applicability and ease of use. Relevant features of reliability (including internal consistency, intrarater reliability and test-retest reliability) were evaluated. The tool was then tested by owners and clinicians for performance against established clinical sign assessment methods. The DOSAS was shown to be both reliable and valid with psychometric properties above acceptable guidelines for the development of such tools. Guidelines are presented for score creation and stratification of the score to enable interpretation. When compared to how severity assessment scores from Canine Atopic Dermatitis Extent and Severity Index, 4th iteration (CADESI-04) and pruritus Visual Assessment Scale (PVAS) responded to change, the DOSAS performed particularly strongly, although it performed less well when compared to the 0-3 Otitis Index Score (OTIS-3). The DOSAS is presented as a supplementary tool for use in veterinary practice and clinical research programmes alongside existing clinical measurements such as CADESI-04, providing a focus on the disease as it is experienced by the dog and their owner. Unlike clinical measurement, the DOSAS is accessible and interpretable for dog owners, which is important for the management of chronic pruritic conditions, and will enable dog owners to be more actively involved with their dog's disease management.

papers.title: The use of cold-stored platelets to provide hemostasis in dogs with thrombocytopenia.
papers.authors: Monaco SA, Haines JM, Guess SC, Fiedler SM, Wardrop KJ
papers.abstract: Platelet transfusion can be lifesaving in dogs with severe thrombocytopenia and hemorrhage, but platelet products are limited by short shelf life and contamination risk. Cold-stored platelets (CSP) may provide a practical alternative, but in vivo hemostatic efficacy in dogs is unknown. Evaluate the clinical hemostatic efficacy and safety of CSP transfusions in thrombocytopenic dogs. Twenty-four thrombocytopenic dogs from a veterinary teaching hospital population that received CSP transfusions between March 2022 and October 2024. Retrospective cohort study. Medical records of dogs receiving platelet concentrate stored at 4 °C for up to 21 days were reviewed. Hemorrhage severity was assessed using a modified Daily Canine Bleeding Assessment Tool (DOGiBAT) score before transfusion and at 1 and 4 h post-transfusion. Primary outcomes included change in bleeding score, clinical response, transfusion reactions, and survival to discharge. Twenty-four dogs received 27 CSP transfusions. Mean pre-transfusion platelet count was 23 × 103/μL (range, 2-107 × 103/μL) and mean post-transfusion count was 28 × 103/μL (range, 2-100 × 103/μL; P = .84). Mean DOGiBAT score decreased from 3.15 ± 2.4 at baseline to 2.21 ± 2.1 at 4 (mean change, -0.94; P = .002). Clinical improvement occurred in 19 of 27 transfusions (70%). No transfusion reactions were documented. Nineteen of 24 dogs (79%) survived to discharge. Cold-stored platelets were well-tolerated and associated with decreased bleeding severity in thrombocytopenic dogs, supporting CSP as a practical platelet transfusion option for clinical hemostatic support.

papers.title: Tablet crushing, but not splitting, alters the pharmacokinetics of extended-release levetiracetam in dogs.
papers.authors: Mondino A, Nettifee JA, Simon KE, Papich MG, Muñana KR
papers.abstract: To compare the pharmacokinetics of intact, split, and crushed levetiracetam (LEV) extended-release (LEV-XR) tablets in dogs. We hypothesized that splitting produces a pharmacokinetic profile similar to intact tablets, whereas crushing results in earlier and higher maximum concentrations. Healthy research dogs were administered 500 mg LEV-XR orally as intact, split, or crushed tablets in a randomized crossover design. Plasma LEV concentrations were measured over 12 hours by high-pressure liquid chromatography. Pharmacokinetic parameters were estimated using noncompartmental analysis and supplementary compartmental analysis and compared using linear mixed-effects models. The study utilized 7 Beagles. Compared with intact tablets, crushed tablets resulted in higher maximum concentration (Cmax) values (61.5 vs 46.0 µg/mL; geometric mean ratio, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.08 to 1.65) and lower 8- to 12-hour exposure (30.0 vs 49.8 µg·h/mL; geometric mean ratio, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.77). Duration above the targeted concentration of 10 µg/mL was longer with intact than crushed tablets (10.9 vs 8.5 hours; mean difference, 2.37 hours; 95% CI, 1.02 to 3.72). Exploratory compartmental analysis estimated an earlier time to maximum concentration (Tmax) for crushed compared with intact tablets. No statistically significant differences were observed between intact and split tablets. Splitting LEV-XR tablets did not significantly alter the evaluated pharmacokinetic parameters, whereas crushing resulted in a higher Cmax, an earlier model-estimated Tmax, and reduced late exposure. Splitting LEV-XR tablets may provide a practical option for dose adjustment in smaller dogs. Crushed LEV-XR warrants further evaluation as adjunct therapy during cluster seizures when immediate-release LEV is unavailable.

papers.title: Case series: Superficial lipomatous hamartoma in dogs and cats is a previously unreported NLCS-like dermal lesion.
papers.authors: Kästner L, Marchewski J, Henrich M
papers.abstract: In humans nevus lipomatosus cutaneous superficialis (NLCS) is a rare, benign dermal hamartoma characterized by aggregates of adipose tissue within the dermis without any connection to the subcutaneous tissue. Although NLCS is a well-recognized entity, it is considered a rare lesion with limited reports in the human literature. To date, no comparable cases have been reported in dogs and cats. Over the course of one and a half years, six cases (five in dogs, one in a cat), resembling NLCS-like lesions, were examined. In this report, we compare these cases to the human condition regarding macroscopic features, histopathology, sex, and age of the affected patients. In all cases, the dermal lesions were composed of aggregates of well-differentiated adipocytes within the dermis. Given the morphological similarity to the lesion in humans, the term "nevus lipomatosus superficialis-like lesion" might be appropriate. However, given the controversial use of the term 'nevus' in veterinary medicine and a potential for confusion with pigmented lesion, we propose the term "superficial lipomatous hamartoma" for this entity.

papers.title: Case Report: Allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells for severe chronic kidney disease in a dog.
papers.authors: Yu Y, Lv X, Zhou X, Ma Y, Li H, Wang W, Song Y
papers.abstract: This case report explored the clinical improvement and short-term tolerability of allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (AD-MSCs) in the treatment of severe chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs. A 9-year-old female Pomeranian was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) caused by acute kidney injury and, after conventional treatment failed, received intravenous infusion of AD-MSCs from healthy donor dogs. The AD-MSCs were aseptically collected, isolated, cultured, characterized, and subjected to microbiological safety testing, and were then administered intravenously at a dose of 3 × 10 6 cells/kg every 2 weeks for a total of four infusions, with dexamethasone premedication to reduce the risk of adverse reactions. Following AD-MSC administration and continued conventional care, reductions in serum creatinine and phosphorus and a downward trend in blood urea nitrogen were observed, along with improvements in body weight, body condition score, appetite, and mental status; no adverse events were observed. The results of this case suggest the feasibility and short-term tolerability of allogeneic AD-MSCs for severe CKD in dogs and provide a reference for clinical research on cell-based therapy for canine CKD.

papers.title: Case Report: Concurrent ventricular septal defect, pulmonic stenosis, and intrapulmonary arteriovenous anastomoses in a Korean raccoon dog ( Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis ).
papers.authors: Kim S, Kim M, Han JI, Lee K, Yoon H
papers.abstract: A 3-month-old intact male Korean raccoon dog ( Nyctereutes procyonoides koreensis ) was rescued and admitted to the Jeonbuk Wildlife Rescue Center with lethargy, dehydration, and dermatologic lesions consistent with Sarcoptes scabiei infestation. Physical examination detected a grade IV/VI systolic murmur, and thoracic radiography revealed generalized cardiomegaly. Transthoracic echocardiography identified a perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) with left-to-right shunting. Although no distinct structural abnormalities of the pulmonic valve were observed, increased pulmonic flow velocity (3.87 m/s), mild pulmonic regurgitation (1.68 m/s), and post-stenotic dilation of the main pulmonary artery supported a diagnosis of pulmonic stenosis (PS).
