Specifically, in 5.1% (8/155) were detected anti-T. cruzi antibodies, and in four of these samples (2.5%, 4/155) were co-detected antibodies anti-L. infantum. Antibodies against Ehrlichia spp. were observed in 50.9% (79/155), Anaplasma spp. in 8.3% (13/155), and B. burgdorferi in 0.6% (1/155). Antigens for D. immitis were detected in 1.2% (2/155). No statistical associations were observed on variables (sex, mobility, overnight stay and presence of ectoparasites) and pathogen seropositivity. In conclusion, dogs from rural areas are exposed to VBPs, which requires the use of ectoparasiticide preventive compounds to avoid ectoparasite infestation and reduce the risk of pathogen exposure.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Metagenomic Oxford Nanopore sequencing of feline aural inflammatory polyps for pathogen discovery.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Noland E, Conner K, Brame B, Petersen A, Thaiwong-Nebelung T
papers.abstract: ObjectivesFeline aural inflammatory polyps (FIAP) have been proposed to be induced by chronic viral or bacterial infections; however, the cause is still unknown. The aim of this study was to investigate potential etiologies of these polyps using metagenomic sequencing.MethodsPolyp tissue was collected from 13 cats following routine traction and avulsion procedures. Total nucleic acid was extracted and subjected to a host (feline) nucleic acid depletion protocol. Additionally, the Sequence-Independent Single-Primer Amplification (SISPA) method was used to enrich for low-abundance RNA viral genomes. Sequencing was conducted on the Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing platform. Non-feline sequencing reads were taxonomically classified against custom bacterial/viral databases to calculate relative genus-level abundances.ResultsTaxonomic classification of sequencing reads identified various bacteria across samples and, in some samples, rare viruses. However, no common microbial sequences were associated with polyps to suggest a specific infectious etiology. Bacterial communities were dominated by Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota, and Bacillota phyla, with Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota being more frequently dominant. Lasallevirus was detected in few samples with unknown clinical relevance. Culture and sequencing showed partial concordance in identifying bacteria in some cases.Conclusions and relevanceNo common microbial-associated sequences found to be associated with polyp samples; therefore, no suspect causative agent was identified. 16S and ITS metagenomic sequencing on FIAP may help further elucidate if microbial population shifts have a role in polyp development and recurrence and/or persistence of inflammation leading to polyp development.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Assessment of caregiver burden in feline chronic kidney disease.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Lim L, Quimby JM, Caney S
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to investigate caregiver burden associated with management of cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD).MethodsCaregivers who had experience managing a cat with CKD were recruited through social media to anonymously participate in an online Qualtrics survey. The modified Zarit Burden Interview (mZBI) was incorporated into the survey to objectively assess caregiver burden. An mZBI score of ≥ 18 represents clinically significant burden.ResultsA total of 339 surveys were completed. 46% of caregivers reported an mZBI score of ≥ 18. Caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 3/4 had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0, range 3 - 50) than caregivers of cats with IRIS stages 1/2 (median 14.5, range 0 - 58; P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported never to rarely sharing care responsibilities had significantly higher mZBI scores (median 20.0; range 0 - 50) than those who reported sometimes to always sharing care responsibilities (median 15.0; range 2 - 58) (P = 0.0007). Caregivers who reported the need to coax their cat to eat on a daily basis had higher mZBI scores (median 22.8, range 2 - 50) than those who never coaxed their cat to eat (median 14.5, range 0-49) or coaxed their cat 1-2 days/week (median 19.2, range 3 - 42) (both P < 0.001). Caregivers who always felt supported by the veterinary care team had lower mZBI scores (median 13; range 0-58) than those that only felt supported sometimes to never (median 23; range 5-45) (P < 0.001).Conclusions and clinical importanceSignificant caregiver burden is present in feline CKD, emphasizing the need to for clinicians to provide empathetic advice and practical support.

papers.title: The hormonal effects of owner-cat interactions on pet cats of different potential attachment styles.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: He X, Huang H, Chang H, Xu W, Gui C, Pan J, Yan H, Guo Y, Avilas-Rosa E, Yang B, Deng B, Zhang L
papers.abstract: The aim of the present study was to investigate how different owner-cat interaction types influence stress and owner-bonding in pet cats with different potential attachment styles, using salivary cortisol and oxytocin as physiological indicators. Twenty pet cats were classified into potential secure, insecure-anxious or insecure-avoidant attachment styles using the Secure Base Test. Owners engaged in four types of interactions with their cats at home on separate days. Saliva samples were collected before and after each interaction and analysed for cortisol and oxytocin concentrations. The effects of attachment style, interaction type and time on hormonal changes were examined. Significant interactive effects of potential attachment style and time, as well as interaction type and time, were observed for both cortisol and oxytocin. Passive interactions were associated with increased oxytocin and decreased cortisol, whereas forced interactions showed an opposite pattern. Secure cats exhibited more positive hormonal responses to human interactions compared with insecure cats, who showed increased cortisol or limited hormonal changes. Insecure cats also showed higher basal oxytocin levels than secure cats. Human-cat interactions trigger changes in cortisol and oxytocin levels, depending on the interaction type and cat's attachment style. These findings highlight the importance of considering individual cat attachment differences when promoting appropriate interaction strategies to improve cat welfare and human-cat relationships.

papers.title: Effects of a Dietary Supplementation of Bovine Colostrum in Dogs With Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.authors: Schäfer L, Büttner K, Paßlack N
papers.abstract: Bovine colostrum (BC) shows immunomodulatory properties, which could be beneficial in the management of chronic immune-mediated diseases such as canine atopic dermatitis (cAD). To assess if a BC supplementation affects selected immune variables and clinical signs in cAD. Twenty client-owned dogs with non-seasonal, environmentally induced cAD were enrolled in this prospective, double-blinded, placebo-controlled study. After a 2-week adaptation to standardised feeding, the dogs were divided into two groups, receiving either a placebo or BC at 0.2% in dietary dry matter for 4 weeks. Afterwards, the dogs remained on their diets for another 4 weeks, without placebo and BC supplementation. Blood and faecal samples were collected on Day (D)14, D42 and D70 for immunological measurements (proliferative and phagocytic activity of blood leukocytes, faecal immunoglobulin [Ig]A, plasma concentrations of Igs, C-reactive protein [CRP] and serum amyloid A [SAA]). Additionally, the Canine Atopic Dermatitis Extent and Severity Index, 4th iteration (CADESI-04) was assessed. The owners evaluated pruritus (Visual Analog Scale) of their dogs retrospectively and daily (r-/d-pVAS), as well as quality-of-life (QoL), global assessment and quality-of-coat. No significant diet effects were detected for the clinical and immunological parameters evaluated. A slight improvement in QoL could be observed in both feeding groups over time. An oral administration of BC did not alter relevant clinical and immune parameters in patients with cAD.

papers.title: Trichomonads in the oral cavity of dogs and cats: species composition and relationship with animal age and oral hygiene status.
papers.authors: Piekara-Stępińska A, Czerski A, Szczepankiewicz B, Lachowicz-Wolak A, Gorczykowski M, Piekarska J
papers.abstract: The oral cavity provides a suitable environment for various microorganisms, including protozoa such as trichomonads, which may be associated with periodontal disease development. Humans are considered the typical hosts of Trichomonas tenax but it has also been found in dogs, cats, and other animals, which makes it a factor with a significant zoonotic potential. Apart from T. tenax, domestic carnivores may be infected with such species as T. canistomae, T. felistomae and T. brixi. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence, species composition, and risk factors of trichomonad colonization of the oral cavity in dogs and cats from Poland. Oral swabs from 238 household animals (151 dogs and 87 cats) were examined using cultivation methods. Amplification of ITS1- 5.8 S rRNA-ITS2 fragment was performed for microscopic-positive samples and PCR products were further sequenced. Trichomonads were identified in 26 out of 151 (17.22%) canine and 5 out of 87 (5.75%) feline samples. Higher frequency was observed in older dogs and dogs with intense dental calculus. T. brixi and T. tenax were the only species detected in both dogs and cats. The detection of zoonotic T. tenax in a substantial number of examined animals highlights the relevance of this finding also in the context of human health.

papers.title: The Role of Comorbidities in Pyoderma Among Canine and Feline Diabetic Patients.
papers.authors: Wixon V, Pieper JB, Bachtel J
papers.abstract: Pyoderma is considered a secondary complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), yet the relationship remains unclear. One study found 22% of diabetic dogs with dermatopathy had no other comorbidities while cats have not been evaluated. This study evaluated the association of DM and pyoderma in dogs and cats by identifying comorbidities. This retrospective study analysed canine and feline DM cases from August 2019 to November 2022 at Iowa State University and Colorado State University. We analysed cytologically confirmed pyoderma and assessed the prevalence of comorbidities, including allergies, thyroid and adrenal disease, neoplasia and other dermatological disorders. Pyoderma was prevalent in 7.6% (61 of 805) dogs and 4.0% (15 of 372) cats with concurrent DM. Of 61 dogs, two (3.3%) lacked comorbidities which was considered protective (odds ratio [OR] = 0.06; 95% CI 0.01-0.29; p < 0.001). Allergic dermatitis was the most common comorbidity (70.5%) in dogs with increased odds (OR = 9.15; 95% CI 4.25-19.72; p < 0.001). Among 15 cats, one (6.7%) lacked comorbidities (OR = 0.04; 95% CI 0.01-0.34; p = 0.003), while allergic dermatitis appeared most frequent and increased odds (73.3%; OR = 18.67; 95% CI 4.81-72.44; p < 0.001). West Highland white terriers (OR = 4.59; 95% CI 1.43-14.77; p = 0.011) and domestic medium hair cats (OR = 7.31; 95% Cl 1.05-50.68; p = 0.044) had increased odds of pyoderma. This study suggests that pyoderma in DM cats and dogs is uncommon as pyoderma owing to DM alone being seen in only 0.25% of dogs and 0.27% of cats.

papers.title: Mammary secretory carcinoma in a female domestic rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus): histopathological and immunohistochemical features.
papers.authors: Nunes MM, Oliveira ES, Wronski JG, de Souza Ruas Lopes R, da Rocha MLMS, Nakagaki KYR, Cassali GD
papers.abstract: Secretory carcinoma of the breast is a rare histological subtype in women and is uncommon in female dogs and cats, with only two cases described in female dogs and one case described in a cat. This report describes the histopathological and immunohistochemical features of secretory carcinoma of the mammary gland in a domestic rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus). Microscopic evaluation revealed a non-encapsulated, well-demarcated neoplastic proliferation composed of epithelial cells arranged in solid and tubular patterns, supported by a delicate fibrous connective tissue stroma. The neoplastic cells had slightly eosinophilic cytoplasm, frequently containing large, well-demarcated vacuoles that displaced the nucleus to the periphery, giving the cells a signet-ring-like appearance. Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) histochemical staining, performed with and without diastase digestion, showed positivity in the intracellular and extracellular secretory material in both approaches. Immunohistochemical evaluation was performed for the markers α-lactalbumin, Ki-67, estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and COX-2. Positive cytoplasmic immunolabeling for α-lactalbumin was observed in neoplastic cells and in intracellular and extracellular secretory material, confirming their secretory nature. The diagnosis of secretory carcinoma was established based on the association of histopathological, histochemical, and immunohistochemical features. Considering the secretory features of the mammary gland in rabbits, secretory carcinoma should be included in the differential diagnosis of mammary carcinomas with prominent secretory activity in this species.

papers.title: Reassessing neonatal hypoglycemia in kittens: Clinical relevance beyond the laboratory value.
papers.authors: de Oliveira NMS, Carneiro MD, Talieri IC, Milken VMF, Gouvêa FN, Borin-Crivellenti S, Crivellenti LZ
papers.abstract: The underdeveloped metabolism in newborn kittens, along with the quick use of liver sugar reserves and the limited ability to produce glucose, makes them prone to low blood sugar levels during this time. This condition may be potentially fatal, although reduced blood glucose values do not necessarily manifest with clinical signs. Fifteen neonatal kittens born to three clinically healthy pregnant queens were evaluated during the first three days of life. Apgar scoring was done daily, and blood glucose measurements began within the first hour after birth (T1), followed by evaluations every 2 hours, with a total of six measurements each day from T2 to T6. Samples were obtained via capillary puncture with alternating digital pads and analyzed using a glucometer validated for cats. A total of 270 glycemic measurements were performed, demonstrating instability during the first hours of life. On the first day, there was a mean glucose concentration of 61.7 ± 22.2 mg/dL. On the second day, it dropped to 53.9 ± 16.5 mg/dL. On the third day, metabolic recovery occurred (68.5 ± 14.7 mg/dL). All neonates maintained adequate Apgar scores and showed no clinical signs of hypoglycemia (< 50 mg/dL; weakness, apathy, or reduced suckling reflex). Marked fluctuations in blood glucose levels were observed during the first 48 hours, characterized by wide glycemic variability (22-165 mg/dL on day 1 and 21-86 mg/dL on day 2). A high frequency of hypoglycemic values was recorded, reaching 51.1% on the first day and 60% on the second, indicating initial metabolic instability despite intermediate mean glucose levels. Progressive stabilization was observed by the third day (range 26-95 mg/dL), with the rate of hypoglycemic events dropping to 22.2%, reflecting the maturation of neonatal metabolic homeostasis. Despite the laboratory diagnosis of hypoglycemia, none of the kittens exhibited clinical manifestations or required intervention.

papers.title: Comment on 'Fibroepithelial Polyps of the Ear Canal in Dogs: A Retrospective Analysis of 17 Cases'.
papers.authors: Lucas R, Tortoriello R

papers.title: Assessment of bowel preparation quality in dogs undergoing colonoscopy using the Boston Bowel Preparation Scale.
papers.authors: Ruedi GL, Kook PH
papers.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy of a bowel preparation protocol consisting of at-home administration of clear broth and polyethylene glycol 3350 followed by colonic flushing immediately before colonoscopy in dogs. In this single-referral-center retrospective study, dogs with complete video documentation of the colon were included. Colonic cleanliness was assessed using the Boston Bowel Preparation Scale (BBPS), which scores the 3 colonic segments individually (total score range, 0 to 9 with higher scores indicating better preparation quality). Adequate preparation was defined as a total BBPS score ≥ 6 with no individual segment score < 2. Video footage from 49 colonoscopies performed in 47 dogs was assessed by a single examiner. Adequate colonic preparation was achieved in 41 of 49 (84%) colonoscopies. Median total BBPS score was 7 (range, 4 to 9), with median segment scores of 3, 2, and 2 for descending, transverse, and ascending colon, respectively. The ascending colon had significantly lower scores than the descending colon. In 57% of procedures, the indication for colonoscopy was evaluation of chronic enteropathy (combined upper and lower intestinal endoscopy) without specific suspicion of colonic disease. High-quality bowel preparation for colonoscopy can be achieved without complex or logistically demanding protocols. A straightforward, owner-friendly, at-home preparation regimen provided diagnostic-quality colonic visualization in dogs. These findings may facilitate broader clinical use of colonoscopy in dogs by supporting practical bowel preparation protocols that are feasible for owners and sufficient for diagnostic evaluation, particularly when complete colonic cleanliness is not essential for the intended diagnostic objective.

papers.title: Surgical management of cricopharyngeal achalasia in dogs results in low mortality but moderate incidence of recurrence or persistent clinical signs.
papers.authors: Zhang RM, Brisson BA, Holt DE, Park B, Ham KM, Hawker W
papers.abstract: To describe diagnostic and surgical management of cricopharyngeal achalasia (CA) in dogs and to identify patient or management factors that may contribute to postoperative outcomes. Signalment, diagnostic imaging findings, surgical information, complications, and outcomes were retrospectively obtained. Fisher exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests were performed to identify predictors of unsatisfactory outcomes using sex, breed, age, videofluoroscopic swallow study findings, laterality of surgery, and muscles resected as variables. 26 dogs surgically managed for CA from 2009 through 2025 were included. The most common breeds were Poodle mixes (n = 12) and Golden Retrievers (8). Ventral bilateral surgery resulted in shorter operative times than through 2 lateral incisions. Postoperative complication and mortality rates were 23% and 11.5%, respectively. Aspiration pneumonia was the most common postoperative complication. Unsatisfactory outcomes were reported in 42.3%. Recurrence of clinical signs after initial resolution was noted in 34.6%, and revision surgery was performed in 26.9%. Median time to recurrence was 84 days (range, 7 to 1,320 days). No significant association was identified for age, sex, breed, laterality, videofluoroscopic swallow study findings, or muscles resected. Surgical management of CA resulted in low mortality, moderate incidence of recurrence and revision surgery, and residual symptoms requiring long-term conservative management. Surgery is a safe option for management of CA, but owners should be informed of the risks of recurrence and residual clinical signs that may require long-term dietary modifications. Animals with CA are at risk of aspiration pneumonia both pre- and postoperatively and should be monitored accordingly.

papers.title: Cytokine priming shifts mitochondrial architecture and extracellular vesicle cargo of feline placental mesenchymal stromal cells toward an immunosuppressive phenotype.
papers.authors: Soltero-Rivera M, Arzi B, Marycz K
papers.abstract: To characterize effects of inflammatory cytokine priming on viability, mitochondrial morphology, and extracellular vesicle (EV) cargo in feline placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs). Feline placenta-derived MSCs from 7 healthy cats were cultured under control, serum-deprived, or cytokine-stimulated (tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, IL-1, IL-6) conditions in vitro. Viability/apoptosis were assessed by flow cytometry and mitochondrial morphology by confocal microscopy with MicroP/MATLAB; EVs were characterized by surface markers, RNA sequencing, and microRNA (miR) profiling. Viability exceeded 96% across all conditions, with no significant intergroup differences. Kiel 67 proliferation marker and metabolic activity were significantly reduced under serum-free and cytokine-stimulated conditions versus controls (both P < .001). Cytokine priming increased branching and simple tubular mitochondria, whereas serum deprivation increased fragmented forms. Extracellular vesicle transcriptomics identified 329 differentially expressed genes, including upregulated immunosuppressive receptors C-C motif chemokine receptor 8 and poliovirus receptor-related immunoglobulin domain-containing protein and downregulated proinflammatory histone transcripts. microRNA (miR) profiling revealed 23 differentially expressed miRs, with enrichment of anti-inflammatory miR-204, let-7g, and miR-181b-2 and depletion of proinflammatory miR-34a and miR-320a. Cytokine priming induces mitochondrial elongation and shifts EV cargo toward an immunosuppressive phenotype without compromising viability, supporting inflammatory priming as a strategy to optimize MSC-based therapies for T-cell-mediated inflammatory diseases. Inflammatory priming prior to MSC administration may enhance therapeutic efficacy in cats, supporting investigation of cytokine licensing as a translatable approach to improving MSC therapy outcomes in veterinary medicine.

papers.title: Clotting and Coagulation Disorders in Cats: A clinical review of causes, diagnosis and management.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Evans J, Li RHL
papers.abstract: Hemostatic disorders in cats, while uncommon, can be life-threatening. In general, they can be diagnosed by utilizing a combination of history, physical examination findings, point-of-care assays and a basic understanding of hemostasis. This review aims to provide a general overview of hemostasis physiology, discuss common hemostatic disorders, diagnosis and interpretation of hemostatic testing, and summarize treatments of hemostatic disorders. The underlying cause of hemostatic disorders can often be diagnosed by a combination of history, physical examination and directed testing. Based on the information obtained during the work-up, a management plan can be constructed tailored to the individual patient. This article aims to review the literature surrounding the pathophysiology, diagnosis and management of hemostatic disorders in cats. By the end of this article, readers should be able to: understand the basic physiology of hemostasis; understand common primary and secondary hemostatic disorders in cats and their pathophysiologies in relation to clinical signs and diagnostic findings; compare and contrast common diagnostic tests to assess hemostasis and apply those that are appropriate; and list the appropriate therapeutic and management strategies for common primary and secondary hemostatic disorders in cats.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Evaluation of Left Atrial Reservoir Strain by Two-Dimensional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiography in Cats with Stage B1 Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Algan D, Varlik T, Bach MBT, Gleerup CH, Yilmaz Z, Koch J
papers.abstract: Left atrial reservoir strain (LA S_R), assessed by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE), reflects left atrial (LA) function and may reveal subtle alterations in LA mechanics in cats with American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (ACVIM) stage B1 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) compared with healthy cats. This study aimed to determine whether LA S_R differs between cats with HCM (stage B1) and healthy cats using 2D-STE. Sixty-one client-owned cats were retrospectively identified and included from medical databases. These cats were classified as healthy controls (Stage A; n=30) or preclinical HCM (Stage B1; n=31) according to ACVIM consensus guidelines. All cats underwent a comprehensive conventional echocardiographic examination, including two-dimensional, M-mode, color Doppler, pulsed-wave Doppler, and tissue Doppler imaging, as part of clinical care or screening protocols. Conventional two-dimensional assessment of LA size and function included the LA/Ao ratio, LA diameter, LA area, LA fractional shortening (LA FS), and LA ejection fraction (LA EF). LA S_R was subsequently measured offline using automated function imaging software. Reproducibility was assessed via intra- and inter-observer intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to compare the discriminatory performance of LA S_R and the evaluated LA variables between the predefined study groups. Cats with ACVIM stage B1 HCM had significantly lower LA S_R than healthy controls (19.0% [IQR, 14.5-22.0%] vs 38.0% [IQR, 30.25-42.50%], respectively; P < 0.001). LA S_R reproducibility was high with an intra-observer ICC of 0.974 and an inter-observer ICC of 0.894. Assessment of LA S_R was feasible in cats with stage B1 HCM. LA S_R values differed between affected cats and healthy controls, with lower values observed in the affected group and good reproducibility. These findings suggest that LA S_R may provide complementary information on LA function in cats with this stage of disease.

papers.title: Comparison of an Anti-α v β 3 Integrin NIR Fluorescent Probe and Indocyanin Green for Precision Resection of Naturally Occurring Sarcomas in Dogs-A Randomized Blinded Case-Controlled Pilot Study.
papers.authors: Nolff MC, Grest P, Seehusen F, Beer P
papers.abstract: The infiltrative growth of sarcomas represents a challenge for complete resection, as tumour borders are not easily detectable. Fluorescence guided surgery (FGS) allows improved visualization of tumour margins and could improve resection accuracy. Unfortunately, studies validating the impact of FGS are rare, and direct comparisons of different dyes are not available. Dogs (n = 20) that were presented for sarcoma resection were prospectively enrolled and randomized to either receive indocyanine green (ICG, Group 1) or a targeted anti-α v β 3 integrin probe (Group 2) prior to surgery. FGS was performed in both groups with the surgeon blinded to treatment. The false positive and false negative rates as well as tumour-to-background ratio (TBR) were calculated for each dye. Correlation of fluorescent area and histologically confirmed tumour extension was determined using the Dice Coefficient (DC). The clinical impact of FGS was determined by assessing the rate of rightfully adapted resections. False positive signal was detected in 9/10 dogs in group 1 and 3/10 dogs in group 2. Mean TBR at skin level was higher in group 2 (4.5 and 5.3) compared to group 1, and this difference reached significance in formalin-fixed tissue (5.3 vs. 2.6, p = 0.016). Correlation of fluorescent signal and histologic tumour extent was strong for both dyes (DC group 1 = 0.64; group 2 = 0.78). Resection of additional neoplastic tissue based on FGS was more frequent in group 2 (3/10 dogs) compared to group 1 (1/10 dogs). The initial results of this study indicate that the targeted anti-α v β 3 integrin probe is more tumour selective than ICG in dogs. This pilot as well as the subsequent follow up study are registered at animalstudyregistry.org https://doi.org/10.17590/asr.0000321.

papers.title: Systemic oxidative stress, selected nonenzymatic exogenous and endogenous antioxidants, and hematologic and biochemical alterations in bitches with pyometra.
papers.authors: Peker C, Uçar EH, Ekren Aşıcı GS, Musal B
papers.abstract: To evaluate oxidative stress biomarkers (malondialdehyde [MDA] and total oxidant status [TOS]), selected nonenzymatic endogenous (glutathione [GSH], albumin, and bilirubin), and, for the first time, exogenous (ascorbic acid, α-tocopherol, β-carotene, and retinol) antioxidants together with hematobiochemical alterations in canine pyometra. 33 bitches were classified into pyometra (n = 17) or control (16) groups based on clinical and hematological evaluations. Ascorbic acid was measured by the phosphotungstate method; GSH, MDA, β-carotene, and retinol spectrophotometrically; α-tocopherol by ELISA; and TOS by a colorimetric assay. Hematobiochemical variables were analyzed using automated analyzers. Bitches with pyometra had higher MDA and TOS than controls (36.30 ± 13.95 µmol/L vs 24.61 ± 4.80 µmol/L and 27.78 ± 15.51 µmol H2O2 Eq/L vs 13.13 ± 1.84 µmol H2O2 Eq/L; Hedges' g = 1.08 and 1.27, respectively). Glutathione tended to increase in pyometra (12.04 ± 10.80 nmol/g Hb vs 6.40 ± 2.97 nmol/g Hb; Hedges' g = 0.68), whereas the other antioxidants were similar between groups. Pyometra was also associated with leukocytosis, neutrophilia, monocytosis, decreased erythrocyte counts and Hct, and increased ALP, ALT, and cholesterol. Canine pyometra is accompanied by systemic oxidative stress and hematobiochemical alterations. However, circulating nonenzymatic antioxidants remained largely unchanged, suggesting complex antioxidant regulation rather than simple depletion. Increased GSH may reflect a thiol-based compensatory response to increased oxidative burden. Nonenzymatic antioxidant regulation in canine pyometra may be more complex than simple depletion. Further studies incorporating disease-severity stratification and tissue-level assessments of both enzymatic and nonenzymatic antioxidants are warranted.

papers.title: Subcutaneous medetomidine at the governing vessel 20 acupuncture point provides faster early sedation than intramuscular administration without altering intraocular pressure in cats.
papers.authors: Gölgeli Bedir A, Yanmaz LE, Akçora Y, Özkalipçi Ç, Kartal T, Okur S
papers.abstract: To compare sedation, intraocular pressure (IOP), mean pupil diameter, and recovery profiles after IM or SC administration at the governing vessel 20 (GV20) acupuncture point of medetomidine in cats. This prospective, randomized, controlled clinical study was conducted at the Animal Hospital of Ataturk University in April and May of 2026. Cats undergoing elective castration received medetomidine (70 µg/kg) either IM or SC at GV20. Sedation score, IOP, and mean pupil diameter were recorded before and 5, 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes after injection. 16 cats completed the study, with 8 cats in each group. Governing vessel 20 produced higher sedation scores at 5 minutes (GV20, 10 [range, 8 to 11]; IM, 5 [range, 4 to 8]; r = 0.69; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.97) and 10 minutes (GV20, 11 [range, 11 to 12]; IM, 8 [range, 8 to 11]; r = 0.66; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.98), with comparable scores thereafter. Intraocular pressure did not differ significantly between groups or over time. The mean pupil diameter was larger in the GV20 group than in the IM group from 10 to 30 minutes, with the greatest difference 30 minutes after medetomidine administration (GV20, 9.35 ± 0.98 mm; IM, 6.94 ± 1.78 mm; mean difference, 2.41 mm). GV20 administration produced faster early sedation than IM medetomidine without clinically detectable IOP alteration or clinically relevant changes in mean pupil diameter, although early recovery should be monitored. GV20 administration may be useful when rapid early sedation is desired in healthy cats, but early recovery should be monitored.

papers.title: Service dogs in a matched survey were more physically active and had higher odds of being fed grain-free diets than companion dogs.
papers.authors: Otero DK, Wilson K, James TG
papers.abstract: There is a strong, bidirectional relation between the health outcomes of service dogs and their human handlers. Despite this relation, limited information is available on service dog health. This study assesses differences in health status, diet, and physical activity among service dogs and companion dogs. We conducted a cross-sectional study of the Dog Aging Project's Health and Life Experiences Survey, using data collected on or before December 31, 2021. Service dogs and companion dogs were matched on signalment. Descriptive statistics, conditional logistic regression, and Poisson regression were estimated to assess health differences. 240 canines were in each group. A higher prevalence of service dog owners reported annual household income of less than $39,999. Owners in both groups reported their dogs' health to be very good to excellent, and almost 50% of each group used daily joint supplements. Service dogs had a higher adjusted OR of ever being on a grain-free diet (1.98; 95% CI, 1.18 to 3.33), 15% more total minutes of daily physical activity, and longer leashed physical activity compared to companion dogs. Service dogs in this matched cohort had higher activity levels, greater odds of grain-free diet exposure, yet similar prevalence of joint supplementation to companion dogs. Further studies are needed to elucidate functional impacts on both handlers and service dogs and to limit inherent selection bias. This study adds to the relatively limited evidence base regarding service dog health outcomes. The distinct lifestyle patterns of service dogs may warrant tailored veterinary monitoring and client communication, particularly for nutritional and musculoskeletal health.

papers.title: Epidural analgesia reduces or eliminates neuropathic pain refractory to oral medications in dogs and cats for weeks to months.
papers.authors: Bergstein O, Boesch JM, Thomson ACS, Todd-Donato A
papers.abstract: To describe epidural injection for neuropathic pain in dogs and cats and report outcome. Medical records of patients presented to an academic pain medicine service from 2015 through 2026 with clinical signs of neuropathic pain and a somatosensory nervous system lesion or disease that underwent epidural injection after failing treatment with at least 2 oral analgesics were reviewed; incomplete records were excluded. Six animals met these criteria. 4 domestic shorthair cats and 2 dogs (Dalmatian and mixed-breed) presented with neuropathic pain beginning after amputation (2 cats), blunt force trauma (1 cat, 1 dog), hemilaminectomy (1 dog), or parturition (1 cat). Abnormalities included paroxysmal, spontaneous self-mutilation, body-focused repetitive behavior, panic, and/or vocalization; signs of allodynia; teeth chattering; tail and skin twitching; abnormal posture or gait; and/or inability to perform normal activities. MRI was not performed in feline amputees but showed intervertebral disk disease in 2 cats and the Dalmatian and sciatic nerve neoplasia in the mixed breed. At least 1 epidural injection containing triamcinolone (0.1 to 0.5 mg/kg) and 0.125% to 0.250% bupivacaine or ropivacaine (with or without other analgesics) was performed. In 1 feline amputee, 1 injection was curative. In the other cats, injection mitigated or eliminated pain for a median of 6 months (range, 0.25 to 8); in 2 cats, repeat injections lasted 5 and 2.5 months. In the Dalmatian and mixed breed, initial and repeat injections lasted 6 and 3 weeks and 4 and 2 weeks, respectively. Epidural analgesia may relieve neuropathic pain when oral analgesics fail.

papers.title: Canine gastric polyps are predominantly hyperplastic, and endoscopic polypectomy is a safe and effective treatment associated with no recurrence during follow-up.
papers.authors: Zanardi S, Cola V, Del Magno S, Sabattini S, Dondi G, Romagnoli N, Foglia A, Pisoni L, Pietra M
papers.abstract: To characterize the clinical presentation, endoscopic features, and histopathological findings of gastric polyps in dogs and to evaluate the safety and outcomes of endoscopic polypectomy. Dogs diagnosed with gastric polypoid lesions during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy from January 2020 through December 2024 at the University Veterinary Hospital, University of Bologna (Italy), were retrospectively evaluated. Inclusion criteria were endoscopic identification of gastric polyps; dogs with primary gastric neoplasia were excluded. Signalment, clinical signs, history of proton pump inhibitor administration, endoscopic findings, histopathology, treatment, complications, and follow-up data were collected. Endoscopic polypectomy was performed using cold biopsy forceps or electrosurgical snare. Over a 5-year period, 57 dogs were included from 574 canine gastroscopies performed, yielding a detection rate of 9.9% (57 of 574). Polyps were solitary in 54.4% and multiple in 45.6% of cases, mainly located in the gastric antrum (77.2%). All polyps were hyperplastic on histopathology. Endoscopic polypectomy was performed in 17 of 57 dogs, with no intraoperative complications. Mild postoperative complications occurred in 5 of 17 dogs. Clinical signs resolved in all but 1 case and remained absent during follow-up (median, 16 months). Polyps removed with electrosurgical snare were significantly larger than those removed with cold biopsy forceps, with an exploratory cutoff of 10 mm distinguishing between the 2 techniques. No recurrences were documented based on clinical follow-up. Gastric polyps in dogs are uncommon lesions, typically hyperplastic and associated with chronic inflammation. Endoscopic polypectomy appears to be a safe and effective treatment and recurrence-free at follow-up. Endoscopic polypectomy represents a minimally invasive option for the management of gastric polyps in dogs, allowing clinical resolution with low morbidity in selected cases.

papers.title: Brachyspira hyodysenteriae detected in a dog with acute haemorrhagic diarrhoea: a case report.
papers.authors: Jeong H, Ahn H, Cheon DS, Oh Y, Yoon WK
papers.abstract: Brachyspira hyodysenteriae is a well-known pathogen of swine dysentery, a severe mucohaemorrhagic colitis in pigs. While several Brachyspira species are reported in dogs, natural Brachyspira hyodysenteriae detection in dogs is extremely rare. This case report aims to provide insight into the pathogenic potential and clinical significance of Brachyspira hyodysenteriae in dogs. A 5-year-old male mongrel dog was presented with acute haemorrhagic diarrhoea shortly after being adopted from a shelter, where he had a history of soft stools. The faeces were watery, containing fresh blood and fibrinous mucus. Initial wet mount and faecal flotation tests were negative for parasites or ova, but faecal smear cytology revealed diverse bacterial morphologies, including chevron- and spiral-shaped forms. Real-time PCR identified Brachyspira hyodysenteriae with a low Ct value (27.19), alongside Campylobacter coli, Campylobacter jejuni, canine astrovirus and Cystoisospora. The dog was treated with enrofloxacin, metronidazole, and fenbendazole, leading to complete resolution of haematochezia and gradual normalization of stool consistency. Follow-up real-time PCR confirmed the absence of all previously detected pathogens, and the patient remained asymptomatic. This case suggests that Brachyspira hyodysenteriae, traditionally regarded as a swine-specific pathogen, may contribute to gastrointestinal disease in dogs. However, because confirmatory bacterial culture was not performed and multiple enteropathogens were detected concurrently, a definitive association between Brachyspira hyodysenteriae and the observed haemorrhagic diarrhoea cannot be established. Nevertheless, it highlights the importance of considering Brachyspira hyodysenteriae in unexplained cases of infectious diarrhoea in dogs, particularly regarding mixed infections. These findings also raise concerns regarding potential interspecies transmission and associated biosecurity risks. Further research is warranted to enhance understanding of diagnostic strategies, treatment approaches and antibiotic resistance patterns.

papers.title: Comparative Phenotypic and Molecular Characterisation of Feline Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Cell Lines Reveals Marked Biological Heterogeneity.
papers.authors: Tanveer Q, Pang LY, Farquharson C, Bergkvist GT
papers.abstract: Feline oral squamous cell carcinoma (FOSCC) is the most common oral malignancy, characterised by aggressive local invasion, frequent bone involvement, and poor prognosis. The limited availability of well-characterised in vitro models has hindered the understanding of tumour heterogeneity and invasive behaviour. This study aimed to establish and comparatively characterise a panel of FOSCC cell lines derived from tumours with and without documented bone invasion to identify intrinsic biological differences. Four FOSCC cell lines were evaluated for epithelial identity, growth kinetics, clonogenicity, migratory capacity and chemosensitivity. All cell lines retained epithelial characteristics, with consistent expression of epithelial markers; however, variation in cytokeratin-19 and vimentin suggested phenotypic heterogeneity and partial epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity. The cell lines demonstrated distinct proliferation rates, doubling times, and clonogenic capacities. Morphologically, these cells displayed varying degrees of peripheral filopodial activity. Functional assays further revealed substantial migratory capacity under both serum-supplemented and serum-free conditions, with differences across cell lines. Chemosensitivity profiling showed heterogeneous responses to targeted and cytotoxic agents, highlighting cell line-specific differences in drug susceptibility and potential intrinsic drug responsiveness. These findings demonstrate that FOSCC cell lines possess distinct biological properties consistent with phenotypic differences. The observed heterogeneity underscores the potential relevance of tumour origin in shaping functional behaviour and highlights the value of using multiple, well-characterised cell line models to better represent disease diversity. This study provides a comprehensive comparative characterisation of four FOSCC cell lines, including a newly established model, and establishes a baseline resource for future mechanistic and translational investigations in feline and comparative oncology.

papers.title: Effects of Supplementing Semen Extenders With Spirulina platensis Extract on Post-Thaw Ram Sperm Quality.
papers.authors: Jaberi K, Mousavi SM, Forouharmehr A
papers.abstract: Supplementation of semen extender with natural antioxidants represents a promising strategy to mitigate cryopreservation-induced damage in ram spermatozoa. This study evaluated the dose-dependent effects of Spirulina platensis extract (0-70 µg/mL) supplemented to Tris-based extenders on post-thaw sperm quality in Lori rams. Semen was collected twice weekly over a four-week period (eight replicates) from four mature rams using an artificial vagina. On each collection day, ejaculates meeting the acceptable criteria were pooled and extended in a Tris-based diluent containing 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, or 70 µg/mL of Spirulina extract, designated as Spir-0 through Spir-70, respectively. All samples were equilibrated at 5°C for 3 h, then cryopreserved in liquid nitrogen and subsequently thawed in a 37°C water bath for 30 s. Post-thaw sperm quality was comprehensively assessed for motility (using CASA), viability, plasma membrane integrity, acrosome morphology, mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), DNA denaturation (via AO), and oxidative biomarkers, including malondialdehyde (MDA), hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), and antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase [SOD], catalase [CAT], and glutathione peroxidase [GPx]). Data were analysed using a completely randomised design with one-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey's HSD post-hoc test, with statistical significance set at P < 0.05. Supplementation at the concentration of 50 µg/mL Spirulina extract (Spir-50) yielded the highest post-thaw total (TM; 50.23%) and progressive motility (PM; 33.0%), as compared to the control (TM; 32.30%; PM; 18.8%). Moreover, this concentration significantly enhanced viability (59.16%), plasma membrane functionality (56.95%), and the proportion of spermatozoa exhibiting high mitochondrial membrane potential (hMMP; 54.5%). In addition, Spir-50 markedly increased glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity (35.49 vs. 23.73 mU/mL in control) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity (213.07 vs. 190.74 U/mL in control), along with total antioxidant capacity (TAC; 4.53 µmol/L vs. 3.34 µmol/L in control). Conversely, this treatment substantially reduced malondialdehyde (MDA; 2.60 nmol/mL vs. 7.69 nmol/mL in control), DNA denaturation (2.87% vs. 6.67% in control), and hydrogen peroxide levels (H 2 O 2 ; 16.4% vs. 27.7% in control). Supplementation with the concentration of 50 µg/mL Spirulina extract exhibited the most effective cryoprotective effects among the tested concentrations by improving sperm motility, viability, membrane and DNA integrity, mitochondrial function, and endogenous antioxidant defences, while attenuating lipid peroxidation and oxidative stress. These findings support the incorporation of Spirulina extract in Tris-based extenders to improve post-thaw ram sperm quality in ram semen cryopreservation protocols.

papers.title: Successful management of nesidioblastosis in a dog with persistent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia following staged bilateral partial pancreatectomies.
papers.authors: Teyssandier S, Rendon ME, Lameroli H, Centurion B, Galac S
papers.abstract: Nesidioblastosis is a rare but important differential diagnosis for hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia in dogs, a condition most commonly associated with insulinoma. A nine-year-old spayed female dog was presented with recurrent episodes of collapse and documented hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. Diagnostic imaging failed to identify a pancreatic mass, prompting exploratory laparotomy with left partial pancreatectomy and regional lymphadenectomy. Histopathological examination excluded insulinoma and established a diagnosis of nesidioblastosis. Although clinical signs initially resolved following surgery, hypoglycemia recurred 45 days later, prompting a right partial pancreatectomy. Following the second procedure, the patient remained euglycemic and free of clinical signs, without evidence of clinical diabetes mellitus or exocrine pancreatic insufficiency throughout an eight-month follow-up period. This case underscores the importance of considering nesidioblastosis in dogs with hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia when a pancreatic mass is not identified. Furthermore, this case suggests that recurrence after unilateral partial pancreatectomy may occur because of the diffuse nature of nesidioblastosis. In this patient, staged bilateral partial pancreatectomy was associated with sustained glycemic control and clinical remission, without clinically apparent endocrine or exocrine pancreatic dysfunction during an eight-month follow-up period.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Modified transcanal perendoscopic myringotomy and septotomy technique for cats with otitis media - a retrospective study of 38 cats.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Wetzels BN, Pickee E, Passon M, Den Hertog E, Ter Haar G
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThis study solely aims to describe a convenient minimally invasive technique for access to the ventromedial compartment of the middle ear in cats with polypoid or non-polypoid otitis media.MethodsPatients' records were retrospectively retrieved from cats with otic symptoms. Cats were included based on the presence of fluid/soft tissue within the tympanic cavity on CT imaging, abnormal tympanic membranes on oto-endoscopy and/or abnormal auditory tube openings upon nasopharyngoscopy.ResultsA total of 38 cats with uni- or bilateral bulla effusion and endoscopic abnormalities were included and 43 ears were treated. On CT, all treated ears had effusion of both dorsolateral and ventromedial compartments. Otoscopy revealed an abnormal tympanic membrane in 93% (discoloration in 28%, bulging in 28%, rupture in 16% and a protruding polyp in 21%). On normograde nasopharyngoscopy, the ipsilateral auditory tube was visibly open in 81% and partly or completely obstructed with discharge or polypous material in 19%. A transcanal perendoscopic myringotomy and septotomy using a 1-mm rigid Frazier suction tube was performed in all cases. During treatment, inflammation of the mucosal lining in the bulla was seen in all ears, with intracavital polyp formation in 33%, which was subsequently perendoscopically debrided. All cats were treated with a 7-day course of doxycycline and a tapering course of prednisolone. No procedure-related complications were seen intra- or postoperatively to discharge.Conclusion and relevanceTranscanal perendoscopic myringotomy and septotomy in cats is a rapid, minimally invasive and apparently safe technique which allows access to both compartments of the feline middle ear. Short- and long-term outcome have to be evaluated in future research.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Echocardiographic prevalence and attachment-site patterns of left ventricular bands in cats.
papers.journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery
papers.authors: Van den Noortgate G, Zablotski Y, Wess G
papers.abstract: ObjectivesTo determine the echocardiographic prevalence and attachment-site patterns of left ventricular bands (LVBs) in cats and assess whether LVB counts differed by sex, sedation status, or echocardiographic group.MethodsIn this prospective observational study, 200 cats undergoing complete transthoracic echocardiographic examination were evaluated for the presence, number, and attachment-site patterns of LVBs. LVBs were defined as discrete intracavitary linear structures connecting two myocardial structures within the left ventricle without insertion into the mitral valve leaflets. Each visible connection was classified according to predefined attachment-site categories. For the phenotype comparison, cats with normal LV wall thickness or focal insertion-site thickening (n = 89) were compared with cats with a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) phenotype (n = 86).ResultsA total of 884 LVBs were identified. At least one LVB was detected in 199/200 cats, yielding an echocardiographic prevalence of 99.5%. The median number was 4 LVBs per cat (range 0-10). The most frequently observed attachment patterns involved the interventricular septum and papillary muscle or accessory papillary muscle-like structures. Overall, 51.9% of LVBs had at least one septal attachment, and 94.3% involved a papillary muscle or accessory papillary muscle-like structure. LVB counts did not differ by sex (P = 0.47), sedation status (P = 0.26), or between the normal/focal insertion-site thickening and HCM phenotype groups (P = 0.98).Conclusions and relevanceLeft ventricular bands were identified in nearly all cats examined and represent a common echocardiographic finding. Most involved septal and papillary muscle-related attachment sites. Sex and sedation status were not significantly associated with LVB number, and no significant difference was identified between the combined normal/focal insertion-site thickening group and the HCM phenotype group. These findings provide a reference framework for the echocardiographic recognition and classification of LVBs in cats under clinical imaging conditions.

papers.title: De Ritis ratio and L-FABP as supportive biomarkers of hepatic involvement in cats with effusive FIP.
papers.authors: Gulersoy E, Erturk A, Kısmet E
papers.abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP), caused by feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), is a systemic disease affecting multiple organs. Although routine biochemical parameters are not diagnostic, they may aid in clinical suspicion. The aim of this study was to investigate the clinical utility of the De Ritis ratio (AST/ALT) and liver-type fatty acid-binding protein (L-FABP) as candidate biomarkers of liver-associated biochemical alterations in cats with effusive FIP. A total of 47 client-owned cats naturally infected with feline coronavirus (FCoV) were included: 37 cats with suspected effusive FIP (thoracic effusion, n = 14; abdominal effusion, n = 23) and 10 FCoV-positive asymptomatic cats as controls. FIPV infection was confirmed by RT-PCR of thoracic or abdominal effusion samples in all cats with suspected effusive FIP. Control cats were clinically healthy, FCoV-positive by fecal RT-PCR, and had no evidence of FIPV infection. The De Ritis ratio was significantly higher in cats with abdominal effusive FIP than in asymptomatic FCoV-positive controls and demonstrated excellent discriminatory performance for identifying abdominal effusive FIP (AUC = 0.843) and effusive FIP overall (AUC = 0.808). Although serum L-FABP concentrations did not differ significantly between groups, ROC analysis demonstrated acceptable-to-excellent discriminatory performance for cats with effusive FIP (AUC = 0.730-0.854), suggesting complementary rather than standalone clinical utility. These findings suggest that the De Ritis ratio may represent a supportive indicator of liver-associated biochemical alterations in cats with effusive FIP, whereas the clinical utility of L-FABP remains preliminary and warrants further clinical validation.

papers.title: Taeniid infection in dogs: a coprological and knowledge, attitude and practices study in Gondar and Bahir Dar cities, Ethiopia.
papers.authors: Yayeh M, Birhan M, Ayalew A, Menigstu A
papers.abstract: The zoonotic cestodes such as Taenia and Echinococcus species belonging to family taeniidae are of paramount importance in the developing world since they pose serious public health impacts. Dogs serve as definitive hosts, shedding eggs into the environment that can infect livestock and humans. To determine the occurrence of Taeniid infections in dogs, assess the risk factors and evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of dog owners. A cross-sectional study was conducted from September 2025 to February 2026 in Bahir Dar and Gondar cities, Ethiopia. A total of 424 dog fecal samples were collected, and standard fecal flotation techniques were used to examine the eggs. Structured questionnaires were used to gather information on host, management, and owner-related factors. Data were analyzed using chi-square tests and logistic regression in Stata 17, with P < 0.05 considered significant. The overall prevalence of taeniid infections was 29.5%, with dogs showing clinical signs such as diarrhea and proglottids in the feces having the highest infection rates (81.1%). Chi-square analysis revealed significant associations with age, sex, clinical signs, roaming behavior, feeding patterns, and owner knowledge. Multivariate analysis confirmed that old age (AOR = 2.8, P = 0.024), female sex (AOR = 0.43, P = 0.007), clinical signs (AOR = 25.9, P = 0.001), free-roaming behavior (AOR = 0.05, P = 0.001), and inadequate owner knowledge (AOR = 0.38, P = 0.029) as independent risk factors. The study found that taeniid infections were common in dogs in Bahir Dar and Gondar. The main predictors were age, sex, clinical symptoms, free-roaming behavior, and a lack of owner knowledge. To lower the risk of taeniid infection in the study areas, integrated control measures like routine deworming; responsible dog management, public education, and appropriate offal disposal were suggested.

papers.title: An Updated Checklist and Narrative Review of Helminth Parasites of Terrestrial and Semiaquatic Carnivorous Mammals in Uzbekistan.
papers.authors: Safarov A, Okkiyev S, Ionică AM, Said MB
papers.abstract: Helminth parasites are critical components of biodiversity and influence the health of both wild and domestic carnivorous mammals. Despite their ecological and public health importance, comprehensive data on helminth diversity in Uzbekistan remain fragmented. This study delivers a thorough and updated synthesis of helminth parasites infecting 15 species of terrestrial and semi-aquatic carnivorous mammals in Uzbekistan. This study was designed as an updated checklist and narrative review rather than a formal systematic review or meta-analysis. A total of 120 documents published between 1926 and 2024 were reviewed, including 61 journal articles, 54 national conference abstracts and 5 PhD theses written in Russian, Uzbek and English. Data were obtained from PubMed, ResearchGate, Google Scholar and local archival sources. Parasite and host nomenclatures were updated using internationally recognized taxonomic databases and recent parasitological references. The review identified 74 helminth species, including 9 trematodes, 24 cestodes, 5 acanthocephalans and 36 nematodes, recorded from 15 carnivorous mammal species belonging to the families Canidae, Felidae and Mustelidae. Among these parasites, 37 species (50.0%) were retained as having zoonotic relevance after reassessment, although their public health importance varies from well-established zoonoses to occasional or accidental human infections. Research efforts were strongly biased toward domestic dogs, jackals and foxes, while several host taxa and geographic regions remain poorly investigated. This review highlights the rich but unevenly documented helminth diversity of carnivorous mammals in Uzbekistan and provides a taxonomically updated baseline for future regional studies. Persistent gaps in host coverage, geographic sampling, molecular identification and zoonotic risk assessment limit current understanding. Future research should prioritize representative sampling, inclusion of poorly studied carnivore taxa, molecular and non-invasive diagnostic approaches and integrated One Health surveillance to better assess parasite biodiversity, wildlife health and public health risks in Uzbekistan and Central Asia.

papers.title: Pathologic Characterization and Clinical Significance of Lymphovascular Invasion in Canine Thyroid Carcinomas.
papers.authors: Griffin MA, Stoyle B, Oakes A, Flesner B, Lenz JA, Stefanovski D, Durham AC
papers.abstract: The association between lymphovascular invasion (LVI) and outcomes in dogs with thyroid carcinoma is inadequately described, and a standardized definition of LVI is lacking. This study's objectives were to histopathologically and immunohistochemically characterize LVI and to evaluate associated clinical outcomes in dogs with thyroid carcinoma. Inclusion criteria were: dogs that underwent thyroidectomy for thyroid carcinoma with available histopathology samples, and a minimum of 1-year postoperative follow-up data or follow-up to death. Thirty dogs with 35 distinct tumours, including 26 follicular and nine medullary, were evaluated. LVI was characterized as intracapsular endothelialized tumour emboli (without adhered fibrin) in 26 samples, intracapsular tumour emboli with adhered fibrin in seven samples, extracapsular tumour emboli without adhered fibrin in 10 samples, and extracapsular tumour emboli with endothelial disruptions and adhered fibrin in three samples. CD31 and Prox1 positive vessels contained endothelialized tumour thrombi in 17 and one sample, respectively. Extracapsular invasion with (non-endothelialized) and without (endothelialized) associated fibrin were associated with a 10-fold (p = 0.001) and 3-fold (p = 0.013) increase in the likelihood of death, respectively. No significant difference in the likelihood of death was noted between cases of extracapsular invasion with or without fibrin (p = 0.31). Intracapsular tumour thrombi with or without associated fibrin and non-endothelialized tumour thrombi were not associated with outcomes in this cohort. These results support that in dogs with thyroid carcinoma, extracapsular LVI with or without associated fibrin thrombi, but not intracapsular LVI, is associated with worse outcomes. Further study is warranted on a larger population of dogs with standardized treatment and follow-up.

papers.title: Tolerability and Outcome of Medical Treatment in Feline Nasal Carcinomas: A Multi-Institutional Retrospective Study.
papers.authors: Amato F, Gobbetti M, Giuliano A, Treggiari E, Pieri M, Bonazzi I, Bianchi ML, Valenti P
papers.abstract: Carcinomas are the second most common feline intranasal neoplasm. Various treatment options, including radiotherapy, surgery or a combination of both, have been described, but data on medical therapy efficacy are lacking. This retrospective study evaluated the outcome of cats with nasal carcinoma (NC) treated with antineoplastic treatment. Cats with a histopathological or cytopathological diagnosis of NC were included. Patients receiving antineoplastic treatment were compared to patients receiving palliative treatment alone. Response to therapy, median time to progression (MTTP) and median survival time (MST) were described and compared for both groups. Analysed clinical variables included the presence of epistaxis, facial deformity, stage, use of NSAIDs and previous surgical debulking. Thirty-three cats were included in the study: 18 in the antineoplastic treatment group and 15 in the palliative treatment group. Forty-eight percent of the entire population had worsening of the clinical signs, 36% remained stable and 16% showed clinical benefit. MTTP of the entire population was 104 days and MST was 178 days. No statistically significant differences were found between groups for either MTTP (96 vs. 111 days; p = 0.95) or MST (197 vs. 262; p = 0.77). None of the evaluated clinical variables was associated with outcome. In this retrospective study, antineoplastic treatment was not associated with a detectable survival advantage over palliative treatment alone. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and heterogeneity of treatments administered.

papers.title: Precision-Guided Therapy for Canine Cancers: An Oasis or a Mirage?
papers.authors: Modiano JF

papers.title: Nasal Colonization of Antimicrobial-Resistant and Biofilm-Producing Staphylococcus spp. in Surgical Canine Patients From Italy.
papers.authors: Nocera FP, Schena R, Romano A, Cavalli S, Cortese L, Fatone G, Martino L
papers.abstract: Staphylococcus spp. commonly colonise the skin and mucosal surfaces of dogs and may act as opportunistic pathogens under favourable conditions. Antimicrobial resistance and biofilm formation are key traits that may contribute to bacterial persistence and reduced susceptibility to antimicrobial agents. This study aimed to characterise the antimicrobial resistance profiles and biofilm-forming ability of Staphylococcus spp. isolated from the nasal cavities of dogs admitted to the Surgical Unit of the Veterinary Teaching Hospital in Naples, Italy. Nasal swabs were collected from 100 dogs prior to surgery. Strains were identified by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method according to international guidelines. Biofilm formation was assessed using a quantitative crystal violet assay. A total of 65 Staphylococcus strains were recovered. Staphylococcus pseudintermedius was the most prevalent species (40%; χ 2  = 134.6, df = 14, p < 0.001), followed by Staphylococcus aureus (15.4%) and Staphylococcus epidermidis (7.7%). High levels of resistance were observed to several antimicrobials, with 61.5% and 4.6% of strains being classified as multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR), respectively. Notably, all tested isolates exhibited biofilm formation, with the majority (56.9%) classified as moderate producers. These findings highlight the presence of antimicrobial-resistant and biofilm-forming Staphylococcus spp. in the nasal cavities of dogs undergoing surgery. The coexistence of these traits may contribute to bacterial persistence, representing a concern for clinical management. Therefore, preoperative nasal screening in high-risk patients should be considered to optimize prophylactic antimicrobial protocols and reinforce infection control in veterinary surgical settings.

papers.title: Palliative Debulking of an Aortic Body Tumour With Right Atrial Invasion in a Dog Under Partial Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
papers.authors: Suzuki S, Tanaka S, Kanno N, Yogo T, Harada Y, Michishita M, Hara Y
papers.abstract: Aortic body tumours are uncommon heart-base neoplasms in dogs, and intracardiac extension causing clinically significant right atrial obstruction is rarely described. A 7-year-1-month-old, 15.2-kg, castrated male French Bulldog was evaluated for 2 weeks of lethargy, hyporexia, exercise intolerance, abdominal distension, and polydipsia. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe right-sided cardiac enlargement and a heterogeneous right atrial intracavitary mass (3.2 × 3.1 cm) suspected to arise from the heart base, with tricuspid regurgitation (maximal velocity 4.03 m/s). Abdominal ultrasonography showed hepatic venous congestion and marked ascites; fluid was a modified transudate. Medical therapy failed to resolve ascites, and surgical debulking was performed on Day 7 under partial cardiopulmonary bypass. The mass was firmly adherent to the atrial septal aspect and could not be completely excised. Postoperatively, ascites and clinical signs resolved, right-sided cardiac enlargement decreased, and tricuspid regurgitation was no longer detectable; the dog was discharged on Day 14. A recurrent right atrial mass was documented on Day 360 without recurrence of right-sided heart failure. The dog died on Day 390 from pancreatitis-associated biliary obstruction and multiple organ failure. Necropsy confirmed an aortic body tumour with intracardiac extension into the right atrium and pulmonary metastasis with tumour emboli. Partial cardiopulmonary bypass-assisted palliative debulking may temporarily relieve life-limiting intracardiac obstruction in carefully selected dogs; however, this approach is high-risk and non-curative, and its contribution to long-term survival remains uncertain because postoperative toceranib therapy and the natural behaviour of the tumour may also have influenced the clinical course.

papers.title: Evaluation of urinary biomarkers for detection of renal tubular injury in Vipera berus-envenomated and critically ill dogs with and without clinically apparent acute kidney injury.
papers.authors: Selin AK, Lilliehöök I, Strage EM, Larsson A, Pelander L
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) in dogs has high mortality and early diagnosis is essential, but traditional markers are not sensitive enough to detect renal injury in the absence of decreased glomerular filtration rate. The objective of this study was to compare urinary cystatin C (uCysC), N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase (uNAG), and glucose (uGlu) among dogs hospitalised because of envenomation by Vipera berus (EVB) or admitted for intensive care without (IC) or with (AKI APP ) clinically apparent AKI, and 30 healthy dogs. Urine and serum samples were collected on days 1 and 2, and urine samples on days 7 and 14. Urinary CysC, NAG, and glucose concentrations were measured with an automated chemistry analyser, normalised to urinary creatinine concentration (uCr) and compared among groups. Ninety-seven dogs were included (30 HC, 28 EVB, 14 AKI APP and 25 IC dogs). Age, bodyweight, and sex did not differ among groups. On day 1, median [IQR] uCysC/uCr (10 -3 ) and uGlu/uCr were higher (p < 0.008) in EVB (0.05 [0.03-0.11], 0.04 [0.03-0.06)]), IC (0.06 [0.03-0.4], 0.05 [0.03-0.09]), and AKI APP (4.4 [0.13-30.0], 0.12 [0.05-0.45]) groups, compared to healthy dogs (0.02 [0.01-0.03], 0.03 [0.02-0.04]). Urinary markers decreased over two weeks post hospitalisation in all groups except AKI APP . Initial levels of uCysC/uCr were higher (p < 0.002) and remained elevated in non-survivors compared to survivors of AKI APP , suggesting potential prognostic value. Urinary CysC/uCr and Glu/uCr are potential markers of tubular injury in early stages of AKI in dogs.

papers.title: Safety Assessment of Mefepronic Acid in Sheep.
papers.authors: Canbar R, Parlak TM, Uslu M, Yazar E
papers.abstract: Mefepronic acid is used as a choleretic agent in different animal species. Although mefepronic acid is used extra-label in sheep, information on its safety in this species is limited. The aim of this study was to determine the effects of mefepronic acid on serum oxidative stress, lipid metabolism and organ function parameters in sheep. Mefepronic acid was administered to 10 sheep at a dose of 10 mg/kg (intramuscular, once daily, 3 days). Blood samples were taken at 0 and at 24, 48 and 72 h. 8-OHdG, MDA, SOD, GPX, CAT, CK-MB isoenzyme, troponin I, serum ALP, AST, ALT, total bilirubin, BUN, creatinine, cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL and HDL levels were measured. Mefepronic acid administration resulted in a transient increase in 8-OHdG levels (p < 0.05) and a decrease in CAT levels (p < 0.05), a transient increase in CK-MB isoenzyme levels (p < 0.05), and a decrease in BUN, HDL and LDL levels (p < 0.05), but no effect on other parameters (p > 0.05). Administration of mefepronic acid to sheep may cause transient changes in oxidative stress parameters and CK-MB isoenzyme levels. However, these changes were not associated with an increase in troponin I levels or clinically significant myocardial damage. Mefepronic acid did not cause clinically significant adverse effects on liver or kidney function parameters.

papers.title: Retrospective Comparison of Gastrointestinal Toxicity in Dogs With Lymphoma Receiving Doxorubicin With or Without Prophylactic Trimethoprim-Sulfadiazine.
papers.authors: Madden EJ, Chan C
papers.abstract: Doxorubicin is commonly used in the treatment of canine lymphoma and other malignancies but is associated with adverse effects, including gastrointestinal toxicity and myelotoxicosis. Previous veterinary studies have suggested that prophylactic antimicrobial administration may reduce chemotherapy-associated toxicity and hospitalisation. However, the potential benefits of prophylactic antimicrobials must be balanced against risks, including antimicrobial resistance and dysbiosis. This retrospective study evaluated the effect of prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfadiazine administration on gastrointestinal and haematologic adverse events in dogs with high-grade multicentric lymphoma receiving doxorubicin for the first time. Medical records from three referral hospitals in Queensland, Australia were reviewed for dogs treated between January 2008 and November 2025. Adverse events occurring within 14 days of doxorubicin administration were retrospectively graded using the Veterinary Cooperative Oncology Group Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events. Sixty dogs met the inclusion criteria, including 21 dogs receiving prophylactic TMS and 39 receiving no prophylactic antibiotics. Gastrointestinal toxicity occurred in 14/21 (66.7%) dogs receiving TMS compared with 13/39 (33.3%) dogs receiving no antibiotics (p = 0.013). After controlling for lymphoma stage, prophylactic TMS administration was associated with a 3.69-fold increase in the odds of GI toxicity (95% CI 1.13-12.11, p = 0.031). No significant differences were identified between groups in severity of GI toxicity, haematologic toxicity, neutropenia or hospitalisation rates. Prophylactic TMS administration during doxorubicin chemotherapy was associated with increased GI toxicity in this cohort, contrasting with previous reports and supporting the need for prospective evaluation of prophylactic antimicrobial use in contemporary geographically distinct canine chemotherapy populations.

papers.title: Microbiological investigation of conjunctivitis in cats and dogs from Kars, Türkiye (2024-2025): culture- and MALDI-TOF MS-based identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of bacterial isolates.
papers.authors: Tarhane S, Büyük F
papers.abstract: Conjunctivitis is a common clinical disorder in cats and dogs, frequently associated with bacterial and fungal infections. Accurate identification of pathogens and evaluation of their antimicrobial resistance profiles are essential for effective treatment. Bacterial and fungal agents were analyzed using cultural and MALDI-TOF MS methods in conjunctival swab samples taken from 59 domestic animals (53 cats and 6 dogs) diagnosed with conjunctivitis and presented to veterinary clinics in Çankırı, Türkiye, during the period from 2024 to 2025. Among the 59 conjunctival swab samples collected from cats and dogs with conjunctivitis, 20 (33.9%) were positive for bacterial culture. Of these, 17 positive cultures were detected in 53 cat samples (32.08%), whereas 3 were detected in 6 dog samples (50.0%). No growth was observed in cultures for anaerobic and Mycoplasma agents, and no evidence of fungal agents was found. Multiple bacterial isolates were isolated in six (10.17%) animals [5 cats (9.43%), 1 dog (16.67%)]. Species identification by MALDI-TOF MS revealed a total of 16 different bacterial species with high confidence scores (≥2.0) across both animal species. The most frequently isolated strains were Staphylococcus epidermidis (n= 7), Corynebacterium mucifaciens (n= 5), Psychrobacter spp. (n= 5), and Streptococcus lutetiensis (n= 4). Rare strains such as Brachybacterium muris (n= 1), Micrococcus luteus (n= 1), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (n= 1) were also detected. In cats, S. epidermidis, Corynebacterium spp., Psychrobacter spp., and Streptococcus hyovaginalis were the most frequently isolated strains. In dogs, Streptococcus canis, Enterococcus durans, Corynebacterium mucifaciens, Micrococcus luteus, and Staphylococcus hominis ssp. hominis were detected. Antibiotic susceptibility of the isolates was evaluated according to EUCAST and CLSI criteria and interpreted based on the inhibition zone diameter. Of the 37 bacterial isolates recovered, 32 (86.49%) exhibited multidrug-resistant (MDR) profiles. Particularly noteworthy were the extensive MDR patterns observed in Enterococcus durans, Enterococcus faecium, Psychrobacter sanguinis, Streptococcus hyovaginalis, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, which showed resistance to 10-12 antimicrobial agents from multiple classes, including penicillins, tetracyclines, and cephalosporins. Although no fungal agents were recovered, the study demonstrates that the bacterial species isolated from cats and dogs with conjunctivitis are highly diverse and that multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates are common. The antimicrobial susceptibility results provide valuable information on the resistance profiles of microorganisms associated with conjunctivitis cases in the study population. In addition, the detection of certain microorganisms with zoonotic potential underscores the importance of ongoing surveillance from a veterinary public health perspective.

papers.title: Corn husk meal as a sustainable dietary additive in biofloc-cultured koi carp (Cyprinus carpio var. koi): Integrative effects on growth performance, immune response, histology, gene expression, and ammonia-stress resilience.
papers.authors: Khang LTP, Wisetkaew S, Islam SI, Jitjumnong J, Sangsawad P, Dinh-Hung N, Permpoonpattana P, Van Doan H, Linh NV
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary corn husk meal (CHM) on growth, digestive enzyme activity, intestinal morphology, immune- and antioxidant-related gene expression, and ammonia-stress tolerance in biofloc-cultured koi carp. A total of 300 fish (initial weight, 32.20 ± 0.03 g) were fed diets containing 0, 5, 10, 20, or 30 g/kg CHM for eight weeks. Survival remained high across treatments (> 95%), while fish fed CHM-10 showed significantly improved growth and a lower feed conversion ratio than the control (p < 0.05). Polynomial regression estimated a modeled optimum CHM inclusion level of approximately 14.4-14.9 g/kg, which was not directly tested in the feeding trial. Serum total protein was unaffected, whereas digestive enzyme activities increased at moderate CHM levels, peaked at 10 g/kg and declined at higher inclusion levels. Fish fed 10 g/kg CHM also exhibited improved intestinal morphometry, whereas higher inclusion levels produced less favorable villus characteristics. CHM supplementation at 10 g/kg significantly upregulated tlr4, tnf-α, il-8, tgf-β, il-10, gpx, sod, gst, and lyz, while nf-κB and cat were not significantly affected. During ammonia exposure, the CHM-10 and CHM-20 groups showed significantly higher survival than the control. Overall, CHM-10 was the best-performing experimentally tested inclusion level, improving growth, digestive function, intestinal morphology, selected immune- and antioxidant-related gene expression, and ammonia-stress resilience in koi carp, while the regression analysis suggested a higher modeled optimum of approximately 14.4-14.9 g/kg. These findings support the sustainable use of agricultural by-products as dietary ingredients for aquaculture.

papers.title: Multiple Modelling Methods Suggest That Grain-Free Diets Are Not Predictive of New Owner-Reported Cardiac Diagnoses Over Two Years in the Dog Aging Project, Despite Owner Misclassification of Diet.
papers.authors: O'Brien J, Bishop M, Dog Aging Project Consortium, Tolbert MK, Ruple A
papers.abstract: Grain-free diets have been potentially linked to dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in several studies in dogs, although the underlying mechanisms for this potential link, if present, are unclear. Additionally, some studies have found no association between grain-free diets and DCM in dogs. Unfortunately, many of these studies were limited by the validity of owner-reported diet information. Furthermore, the effect of grain-free diets on other cardiac conditions in dogs is even less studied. To assess the validity of owner-reported grain-free diet status information, and to model the potential effect of grain-free diet exposures over the first several years of Dog Aging Project data collection. The validity of owner-reported grain-free status of the diet was evaluated by comparing owner-reported grain-free diet status to the ingredients. Several regression analyses were performed, accounting for likely confounding factors identified with a directed acyclic graph (DAG), to measure the effect of owner-reported grain-free diet status on all cardiac diagnoses. General linear mixed-effects models and general linear regression models were used with similar results. There was a large misclassification error in the diets reported to be grain-free. In spite of this, modelling methods anticipate that any bias introduced into an effect estimate would be very small. Several modelling methods failed to find a statistically significant association between grain-free status of the diet and any cardiac diagnosis. When including incident-only cases in a linear model with confounders, the odds ratio for the effect of grain-free diet status on any new cardiac diagnosis was 1.05 (0.91-1.21, p value 0.52), suggesting no effect. The findings suggested that the potential effect of grain-free feeding on all owner-reported new diagnoses of any cardiac disease within this dataset is likely minimal or absent.

papers.title: Correction: Clinico-pathological and renal morphological findings in dogs naturally infected with Dirofilaria repens.
papers.authors: Szabó KÉ, Aresu L, Müller L, Szilágyi E, Falus FA, Balogh N, Boros M, Papp T, Manczur F

papers.title: Differential diagnosis of microcytic hypochromic anemia in dogs: the role of hepcidin and reticulocyte hemoglobin indices.
papers.authors: Palluy C, Velasco-Martínez MG, Colomer-Selva R, Descalzo-Navarro M, Mena-Moros B, Martins E, Damiá E, Satué K
